push-api/push-event.https.any.js.description: the `window-module` global of the `.any.js` tests (`.any.window-module.html`, the test is run as a module script of a window) is not supported by the runner

push-api/window-pushManager.https.any.js.description: the `window-module` global of the `.any.js` tests (`.any.window-module.html`, the test is run as a module script of a window) is not supported by the runner

web-extensions/*.description: browser extension APIs: the `.extension.js` tests run in a browser extension, which the runner cannot load

cookies/third-party-cookies/third-party-.description: 2 subtests: the third-party cookie heuristics of Chromium (a site that opens a popup of another site, which the user interacts with, gets temporary access to the unpartitioned cookies of the popup's site in its frames; the Storage Access API leaves such grants to the user agent): the cross-site fetches stay blocked

credential-management/credentialscontain.description: `PasswordCredentialData.origin` and `FederatedCredentialInit.origin` are required members (https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dictdef-passwordcredentialdata): the test creates the credential without `origin`, whose conversion throws a TypeError (Chromium does not require it)

"rejects when aborted after the promise creation" calls `create({ signal })` without a type of credential, which is rejected with a NotSupportedError at once; the test expects the promise to stay pending until the signal is aborted

the `otp` member (WebOTP, `OTPCredential`) of `CredentialRequestOptions`: it is ignored, so `get()` with a password and `otp` requests the passwords instead of rejecting the combination with a NotSupportedError

`get({ password: true, federated })` expects a NotAllowedError for the lack of user activation, which the algorithm does not require (https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#algorithm-request): the request resolves with null (no stored credential); and `get({ signal })` without a type of credential is rejected with a NotSupportedError at once (step 7), while the test expects the promise to stay pending until the signal is aborted

the `data:` document posts its message while it is parsed, before the load event of the iframe, and the test only listens for the message after the load event: the message is missed (the test also times out in Edge)

credential-management/idlharness.https.w.description: the test creates the `PasswordCredential` and `FederatedCredential` objects without `origin`, a required member of their dictionaries (https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dictdef-passwordcredentialdata): the constructors throw, so the objects are not tested

credential-management/origin-bound-opaqu.description: `PasswordCredentialData.origin` and `FederatedCredentialInit.origin` are required members (https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dictdef-passwordcredentialdata): the test creates the credential without `origin`, whose conversion throws a TypeError (Chromium does not require it), before the origin is checked

credential-management/otpcredential-*.description: the WebOTP API (`OTPCredential`, https://wicg.github.io/web-otp/); the tests also need the mock SMS receiver of Chromium (`otpcredential-helper.js` throws "Unsupported browser")

digital-credentials/create-non-fully-act.description: the tests create digital credentials with the `openid4vci` issuance protocol, which is not a value of `DigitalCredentialIssuanceProtocol` (`openid4vci-v1`, https://w3c-fedid.github.io/digital-credentials/#dom-digitalcredentialissuanceprotocol): the request is filtered out, so `create()` rejects with a TypeError (and `set_virtual_wallet_behavior()` rejects the protocol with an invalid argument error)

digital-credentials/create.tentative.htt.description: the tests create digital credentials with the `openid4vci` issuance protocol, which is not a value of `DigitalCredentialIssuanceProtocol` (`openid4vci-v1`, https://w3c-fedid.github.io/digital-credentials/#dom-digitalcredentialissuanceprotocol): the request is filtered out, so `create()` rejects with a TypeError (and `set_virtual_wallet_behavior()` rejects the protocol with an invalid argument error)

digital-credentials/user-activation-crea.description: the tests create digital credentials with the `openid4vci` issuance protocol, which is not a value of `DigitalCredentialIssuanceProtocol` (`openid4vci-v1`, https://w3c-fedid.github.io/digital-credentials/#dom-digitalcredentialissuanceprotocol): the request is filtered out, so `create()` rejects with a TypeError (and `set_virtual_wallet_behavior()` rejects the protocol with an invalid argument error)

digital-credentials/webdriver/create.htt.description: the tests create digital credentials with the `openid4vci` issuance protocol, which is not a value of `DigitalCredentialIssuanceProtocol` (`openid4vci-v1`, https://w3c-fedid.github.io/digital-credentials/#dom-digitalcredentialissuanceprotocol): the request is filtered out, so `create()` rejects with a TypeError (and `set_virtual_wallet_behavior()` rejects the protocol with an invalid argument error)

encrypted-media/drm-*.description: the `drm-*` tests use a commercial key system (Widevine or PlayReady, chosen from the user agent string by `getSupportedKeySystem()` of `encrypted-media/util/utils.js`) and the license servers of drmtoday (`util/drm-messagehandler.js`): the library only implements the Clear Key key system (`org.w3.clearkey`), whose variants of these tests (`clearkey-*`) pass; with no recognized browser in the user agent string, the key system is `undefined` and `requestMediaKeySystemAccess()` rejects with a `NotSupportedError` (the `drm-*` tests that pass skip their steps without a key system)

fedcm/fedcm-accounts-push/fedcm-accounts.description: the tentative accounts push of FedCM (the `accounts` of the options of `navigator.login.setStatus()`, used instead of the accounts endpoint, and the prefetch of their pictures)

fedcm/fedcm-accounts-push/fedcm-identity.description: the tentative lightweight FedCM (`navigator.credentials.create({ identity })`, the `IdentityCredential` constructor, the stored identity credentials and their discovery by `origin` and `loginURL`)

fedcm/fedcm-accounts-push/store-account-.description: the tentative accounts push of FedCM: the second argument of `navigator.login.setStatus()` is ignored, so an invalid account is not rejected with a TypeError

fedcm/fedcm-auto-selected-flag.https.htm.description: the test assumes that the third-party cookies of the identity provider are blocked: an account whose `approved_clients` contains the `clientId` is eligible for auto reauthentication when the third-party cookies of its provider are available (https://w3c-fedid.github.io/FedCM/#eligible-for-auto-reauthentication), which they are in the runner (as in the browsers that do not block them), so two accounts are eligible and the account chooser is shown instead of the auto reauthentication

fedcm/fedcm-button-and-other-account/fed.description: the test assumes that the third-party cookies of the identity provider are blocked: an account whose `approved_clients` contains the `clientId` is eligible for auto reauthentication when the third-party cookies of its provider are available (https://w3c-fedid.github.io/FedCM/#eligible-for-auto-reauthentication), which they are in the runner (as in the browsers that do not block them), so two accounts are eligible and the account chooser is shown instead of the auto reauthentication

fedcm/fedcm-delegation/evt-basic.https.h.description: the Email Verification Protocol (the `email-verification-token` autofill of the form fields, issued by the identity provider)

fedcm/fedcm-iframe.https.html.description: the runner does not serve `localhost`: the iframe of `http://localhost:8000` is not loaded

fedcm/fedcm-login-status/confirm-idp-log.description: the login page sets the `accounts` cookie with `document.cookie` without `SameSite` attribute: the cookie is `Lax` by default (https://httpwg.org/http-extensions/draft-ietf-httpbis-rfc6265bis.html#name-the-samesite-attribute), and the accounts endpoint is fetched with the cookies of a cross-site request (`SameSite=None`, https://w3c-fedid.github.io/FedCM/#fetch-the-accounts, which fedcm-same-site-none.https.html checks), so the accounts are still empty and the confirm IDP login dialog is shown again

fedcm/fedcm-multi-idp/fedcm-multi-idp-me.description: "Mediation optional automatically succeeds when there is one returning account": the test assumes that the third-party cookies of the identity provider are blocked: an account whose `approved_clients` contains the `clientId` is eligible for auto reauthentication when the third-party cookies of its provider are available (https://w3c-fedid.github.io/FedCM/#eligible-for-auto-reauthentication), which they are in the runner (as in the browsers that do not block them), so two accounts are eligible and the account chooser is shown instead of the auto reauthentication

fedcm/fedcm-navigation-interception/cont.description: the navigation interception of FedCM (the `federation-initiate-request` response header) and the redirect options of `IdentityProvider.resolve()`

fedcm/fedcm-register/fedcm-no-registered.description: the registration of identity providers (`IdentityProvider.register()`): the config URL `any` is not a valid URL, so the request is rejected with an InvalidStateError (as the browsers reject an invalid config URL) instead of the NetworkError of an unregistered provider

fedcm/fedcm-returning-account-auto-reaut.description: the test assumes that the third-party cookies of the identity provider are blocked: an account whose `approved_clients` contains the `clientId` is eligible for auto reauthentication when the third-party cookies of its provider are available (https://w3c-fedid.github.io/FedCM/#eligible-for-auto-reauthentication), which they are in the runner (as in the browsers that do not block them), so two accounts are eligible and the account chooser is shown instead of the auto reauthentication

fedcm/fedcm-storage-access-api-autogrant.description: the storage access granted to the frames of an identity provider whose account is connected to the site; and the requests of FedCM do not bypass the blocking of the third-party cookies, so the accounts endpoint gets no cookie once the test blocks them

fedcm/fedcm-well-known-validation/well-k.description: the identity provider is same site with the site, so its well-known file is not fetched (https://w3c-fedid.github.io/FedCM/#fetch-the-config-file, `skipWellKnown`): the requests that the test expects to fail because of the format of the well-known file succeed

measure-memory/idlharness.window.js.description: 1 subtest: `measureUserAgentSpecificMemory()` is declared `[CrossOriginIsolated]`, so it is only exposed when the global object is cross-origin isolated (https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#CrossOriginIsolated); the test page has no `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy` headers, and idlharness.js does not implement `[CrossOriginIsolated]`: it expects the operation on the prototype of `Performance`, which Chromium hides too

merchant-validation/complete-method.tent.description: `MerchantValidationEvent` and `PaymentRequest.onmerchantvalidation` were removed from the Payment Request API (https://github.com/w3c/payment-request/pull/884): they are not in its IDL, and no browser implements them

merchant-validation/constructor.tentativ.description: `MerchantValidationEvent` and `PaymentRequest.onmerchantvalidation` were removed from the Payment Request API (https://github.com/w3c/payment-request/pull/884): they are not in its IDL, and no browser implements them

merchant-validation/onmerchantvalidation.description: `MerchantValidationEvent` and `PaymentRequest.onmerchantvalidation` were removed from the Payment Request API (https://github.com/w3c/payment-request/pull/884): they are not in its IDL, and no browser implements them

payment-method-basic-card/apply_the_modi.description: manual test (a person must click the buttons that start the subtests, and check the payment sheet), it times out

payment-method-basic-card/payment-reques.description: the test constructs a request with 500 `this-is-not-supported` payment methods, whose duplicates the constructor rejects with a `RangeError` (https://w3c.github.io/payment-request/#constructor: "If seenPMIs contains pmi throw a RangeError"); Chromium fails it too

payment-method-basic-card/steps_for_sele.description: manual test (a person must click the buttons that start the subtests, and check the payment sheet), it times out

payment-request/delegate-request.https.s.description: capability delegation (the `delegate` option of `postMessage()`, https://wicg.github.io/capability-delegation/spec.html): the subframe has no transient activation, so `show()` rejects with a `SecurityError`

payment-request/payment-request-hasenrol.description: `PaymentRequest.hasEnrolledInstrument()` is a proposal of Chromium that is not in the Payment Request API (it is not in its IDL)

payment-request/rejects_if_not_active.ht.description: the test calls `test_driver.bless()` in an iframe whose parent was navigated away: a document that is not fully active cannot get transient activation, so `show()` rejects with a `SecurityError` (https://w3c.github.io/payment-request/#show-method, step 2) before it checks that the document is fully active (step 4); Chromium fails it too

secure-payment-confirmation/authenticati.description: the test gives `total: PAYMENT_DETAILS['total']`, a `PaymentItem` (`{ label, amount }`), to the `payment` extension, whose `total` is a `PaymentCurrencyAmount` (https://w3c.github.io/secure-payment-confirmation/#dictdef-authenticationextensionspaymentinputs): the conversion of the options throws a `TypeError` (the required member `currency` is missing) before the extension rejects the authentication with the expected `NotAllowedError`

secure-payment-confirmation/constructor-.description: "Large credentialIds value" and "Large challenge value" expect a `TypeError` for 1 MiB buffers: the steps to validate payment method data (https://w3c.github.io/secure-payment-confirmation/#sctn-steps-to-validate-payment-method-data) have no size limit (Chromium limits the JSON serialization of the data of a payment method to 1 MiB)

secure-payment-confirmation/enrollment-b.description: the subtests do not return (nor await) the promise of `testBrowserBoundKeyOnPasskeyEnrollment()`: they pass at once, the three registrations run concurrently, and the second and third ones are rejected with a `NotAllowedError` (a request for a public key credential is already pending, as in Chromium) that nothing handles, so the harness reports an error

secure-payment-confirmation/enrollment-i.description: "SPC enrollment in cross-origin iframe without payment permission": a cross-origin iframe without `allow="payment"` may use neither `publickey-credentials-create` nor `payment` (the alternative create permissions policy of `public-key`, https://w3c.github.io/secure-payment-confirmation/#sctn-permissions-policy), so `create()` rejects with a `NotAllowedError` (https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#algorithm-create, step 9.3: "If document is not allowed to use permission, return a promise rejected with a NotAllowedError"); the test expects the `NotSupportedError` of Chromium

secure-payment-confirmation/enrollment.h.description: the registration processing of the `payment` extension throws a `TypeError` when `authenticatorAttachment` is not `platform`, `residentKey` is not `required` or `preferred`, or `userVerification` is not `required` (https://w3c.github.io/secure-payment-confirmation/#client-extension-processing-registration: "then throw a TypeError"); the test expects a `NotSupportedError`

storage/buckets/bucket-quota-indexeddb.t.description: the quota of the storage buckets for IndexedDB: the quota of a bucket only limits its origin private file system, so the transaction that stores 2 MB in a bucket with a 1.5 MB quota commits

storage/buckets/storage_bucket_object.te.description: 3 subtests: `StorageBucket.durability()` and the `durability` option of `open()`, which the Storage Buckets specification no longer defines (its IDL has no `durability`)

web-based-payment-handler/can-make-payme.description: "can be constructed with an EventInitDict" passes an init dictionary to `new CanMakePaymentEvent()`, whose only constructor argument is the type (https://w3c.github.io/web-based-payment-handler/#the-canmakepaymentevent, `constructor(DOMString type)`): the dictionary is ignored, so `bubbles`, `cancelable` and `composed` are false

the invocation of the payment handlers of the service workers: the just-in-time installation of the payment app of the web app manifest that the payment method manifest names, the `canmakepayment` and `paymentrequest` events fired by the user agent, and `PaymentRequestEvent.openWindow()` (the library implements `PaymentManager` and the event interfaces only)

html/canvas/element/manual/draw-element-.description: HTML-in-canvas: the snapshot is painted when it is recorded, with the colors CSS gamut mapped to sRGB (the gamut of the document, `DisplayColor.FromCss`): the `color(display-p3 .94 .95 .08)` background of the element, outside of sRGB, is drawn into the display-p3 canvas as its sRGB gamut mapped color, (238, 242, 79) in display-p3, where the `fillRect()` of the same color is (240, 242, 20); the colors of a snapshot would have to be mapped to the gamut of the canvas it is drawn into
Intersection Observer v2 (`trackVisibility`, `isVisible`): the elements of a canvas whose content is drawable are reported as visible
WebGL (`getContext("webgl")` returns null)

the order of the intersection observer task and of the timers: the observations are computed before the paint event and delivered after it, as expected, but the event loop queues a due timer after the running task: the `setTimeout(0)` set by the `requestAnimationFrame()` callback of a rendering update runs after the intersection observer task queued later by the same rendering update, so the second observation (made after the style change of the paint event) is delivered before the test checks that only one was delivered (`[onpaint, intersection, intersection]` instead of `[onpaint, intersection]`)
HTML-in-canvas: a change of the rendering of an iframe in a drawable element does not change the snapshot of the element (the paint events of the canvases of the parent documents do not fire)

HTML-in-canvas: the subtest "onpaint should fire and report drawable ancestor when a nested drawable element is removed" expects the drawable ancestor of the removed element in `changedElements`, but the snapshot of the ancestor does not change: its drawable subtree excludes its drawable descendants ("a drawable subtree includes a drawable element and its descendants, excluding drawable descendants and their subtrees") and its size is fixed; the proposal says that implementations "should avoid" firing the event when a snapshot has not changed (the library fires it with no changed element)

container-timing/tentative/containertimi.description: the test expects `lastPaintedElement` to be the SVG `<image>` (`svg_img_id`), but the attribute is an `HTMLElement?` (https://w3c.github.io/container-timing/#dom-performancecontainertiming-lastpaintedelement), so it is null and the test reads the `id` of null. The `containertimingignore` attribute of the SVG `<g>` is ignored as specified (an ignored subtree is rooted at an `HTMLElement`, https://w3c.github.io/container-timing/#ignored-subtree): the entry of the container root is reported. Same issue as `containertiming-with-child-svg-image.html`

the test expects `lastPaintedElement` to be the SVG `<image>`, but the attribute is an `HTMLElement?` (https://w3c.github.io/container-timing/#dom-performancecontainertiming-lastpaintedelement) and the processing model only handles the paints of HTML elements, so it is null and the test reads the `id` of null

content-security-policy/script-src/scrip.description: 1 of 3 subtests: a parser-inserted module script that `strict-dynamic` blocks runs the module that a `modulepreload` of the same URL put in the module map: "fetch a single module script" returns the module of the module map without fetching it (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#fetch-a-single-module-script), so the content security policy of the request is not checked; the test expects it to be blocked with a `script-src-elem` violation, as `script-src-strict_dynamic_modulepreload_integrity_mismatch.html`

css/css-animations/KeyframeEffect-getKey.description: `getKeyframes()` of a CSS animation returns the specified values of the `@keyframes` rule (`var()` is not substituted, the custom properties are listed) instead of computed values: `currentcolor` is returned where the test expects the color of the target in another document (iframe, adopted element, display-locked subtree)

the keyframe effect of a CSS animation keeps the keyframes generated from `@keyframes` (the generated initial keyframe with the computed values of the target) after it is detached from the `CSSAnimation` (moved to an `Animation`, `effect = null` then reattached) and when the target has no computed style (`display: none`), where only the keyframes of the rule are expected; `getKeyframes()` on such an effect also flushes the style, which starts a transition

css/css-backgrounds/animations/backgroun.description: 72 of 492 subtests: `background-image` (and `list-style-image`) is transitioned without `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` (`CssInterpolationKind.Image` in `CssAnimationTypes.cs` is not discrete for `CssInterpolation.Prepare`), so the transitions show the start value before the middle; its animation type is discrete (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds-3/#background-image), and a discrete property does not transition without `allow-discrete` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-transitions-2/#transition-behavior-property), as the test expects since web-platform-tests/wpt commit 24c4209 (WebKit 322918, "as is needed for discrete only properties"). Making the image kind discrete passes the test, but other tests still expect the image transitions and fail then: the transition subtests of `css/css-lists/animations/list-style-image-interpolation.html` (`list-style-image` is discrete too, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists-3/#image-markers) and the 3 `background-image ... / events` subtests of `css/css-transitions/properties-value-003.html` (their `transitionend` event): the fix has to reclassify them as TEST BUG at the same time

css/css-break/grid/grid-lanes/row-breaks.description: a row of a row grid lanes container whose monolithic item (`writing-mode: vertical-lr` or `overflow: hidden`, 150px) overflows the first column (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#pagination): the parallel item of the row is not fragmented (one box fragment), where it is expected to fill the first column (100px) and to resume with an empty fragment at the top of the second column, the overflow of the monolithic item taking no space in the next row fragment

css/css-fonts/font-display/font-display-.description: `font-display` (the block, swap and failure periods of the font display timeline): a font face is used whenever it is loaded, so the `font-display: optional` face that arrives after the first paint would replace the fallback font

css/css-grid/grid-model/grid-gutters-and.description: 2 of 8 subtests: the "Distribute space to non-affected tracks" step of the distribution of the extra space of the grid track sizing algorithm (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-2/#distribute-extra-space, w3c/csswg-drafts#3648): it is skipped on purpose (`GridLayoutAlgorithm.TrackSizing.cs`) because the browsers do not apply it; the expectations were rebaselined on the specification by WebKit (whose new grid layout implements it), so the space goes to the affected tracks instead of the non-affected tracks whose growth limit can take it

css/css-grid/parsing/grid-content-sized-.description: 5 of 42 subtests: the "Distribute space to non-affected tracks" step of the distribution of the extra space of the grid track sizing algorithm (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-2/#distribute-extra-space, w3c/csswg-drafts#3648): it is skipped on purpose (`GridLayoutAlgorithm.TrackSizing.cs`) because the browsers do not apply it; the expectations were rebaselined on the specification by WebKit (whose new grid layout implements it), so the space goes to the affected tracks instead of the non-affected tracks whose growth limit can take it

css/css-highlight-api/custom-highlight-a.description: expects the `animation-*`, `transition-*` and `opacity` declarations of the highlight pseudo-elements (`::highlight()`, `::selection`, `::target-text`, `::spelling-error`, `::grammar-error`, `::search-text`) in their computed style: only `color`, `background-color`, `text-decoration`, `text-shadow`, the stroke and fill properties and the custom properties apply to them (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo-4/#highlight-styling), the others are copied from the originating element, so the library ignores these declarations

css/css-images/parsing/image-resolution-.description: 1 of 12 subtests: the test is not consistent: its other subtests expect the canonical order of the grammar `[ from-image || <resolution> ] && snap?` (https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#serializing-css-values: `2dpcm from-image` is `from-image 2dpcm`, `snap from-image 0dppx` is `from-image 0dppx snap`), which the specified value follows, but it expects `snap -8dpcm from-image` to keep its specified order instead of `from-image -8dpcm snap`

css/css-masking/parsing/clip-path-valid..description: 4 of 58 subtests: the one-value `<radial-size>` of `ellipse()` (`ellipse(3%)`, `ellipse(closest-side)`): css-shapes-1 `ellipse()` takes a `<radial-size>`, which https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images-4/#radial-size extends to `<radial-extent>{1,2} | <length-percentage [0,∞]>{1,2}`; the grammar of the library requires two radii (`ellipse( [ <radial-radius>{2} ]? [ at <position> ]? )`)

css/css-masking/parsing/mask-shorthand.h.description: 6 of 84 subtests: the expected longhands of `mask` do not include `mask-border-mode`, which the shorthand resets with the other `mask-border-*` longhands (https://drafts.fxtf.org/css-masking/#the-mask: "also resets mask-border", whose longhands include `mask-border-mode`; WPT css/css-masking/mask-shorthand-subproperties-reset.html expects it reset); the browsers do not support `mask-border-mode`

css/css-mixins/private/css-private-inval.description: 1 of 8 subtests: the `CSSStyleRule` API of `CSSPrivateRule` (w3c/csswg-drafts#14427: `cssRules`, `insertRule()`, `selectorText`, `style`, `styleMap`): it is a plain `CSSRule`, so the test cannot change the private declarations with `styleMap.set()`

css/css-mixins/private/private-shared-st.description: 2 of 3 subtests: the `CSSStyleRule` API of `CSSPrivateRule` (w3c/csswg-drafts#14427: `cssRules`, `insertRule()`, `selectorText`, `style`, `styleMap`): it is a plain `CSSRule`, so the test cannot change the private declarations with `styleMap.set()` or `style.removeProperty()`

css/css-multicol/abspos-in-inline-contai.description: the lines of an absolutely positioned box whose containing block is an inline box (`<span style="position: relative">` on the third line of a multi-column container) are not fragmented at the column boundary: with `top: 0`, its first line is 5px down the first column (the offset of the inline box in its line, without the 60px of the lines before it) instead of 65px, and with auto insets its lines stay in the first column instead of moving to the top of the second one

css/css-ruby/break-within-bases/overflow.description: 5 of 10 subtests: the line breaks inside the ruby bases (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ruby-1/#break-within): a ruby column is a unit of the line breaking (its items are the items of its bases followed by the items of its annotations), so breaking it needs the bases and the annotations to be broken at different positions on each line; Chrome only

css/css-values/random-computed.tentative.description: 5 of 177 subtests: the `ua-early-` prefix of the cache keys of the `random()` functions evaluated during the substitution of an arbitrary substitution function (a typed `attr()`, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#random-caching), with their own index that increases across the substitutions of the declaration: they get the `ua-` keys of the other `random()` functions of the property

css/cssom/cssom-getPropertyValue-common-.description: 2 of 11 subtests: expect `-webkit-line-clamp` to be unable to represent its initial longhands (web-platform-tests/wpt commit 0c8a0f0, which assumes that the legacy shorthand always sets `block-ellipsis: ellipsis`); `-webkit-line-clamp: none` sets `block-ellipsis` to `no-ellipsis` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow-4/#propdef--webkit-line-clamp, checked by css/css-overflow/parsing/webkit-line-clamp-computed.html), so the initial longhands serialize as `none`

css/cssom/shorthand-values.html.description: 1 of 21 subtests: expects `-webkit-line-clamp: none` to be serialized with `-webkit-line-clamp` because "line-clamp: none resets block-ellipsis to no-ellipsis" (web-platform-tests/wpt commit 0c8a0f0, which assumes that the legacy shorthand always sets `block-ellipsis: ellipsis`); `-webkit-line-clamp: none` sets `block-ellipsis` to `no-ellipsis` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow-4/#propdef--webkit-line-clamp, checked by css/css-overflow/parsing/webkit-line-clamp-computed.html), so its longhands are the ones of `line-clamp: none`, the preferred shorthand (https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-shorthands-preferred-order)

event-timing/keydown-without-paint.tenta.description: the tentative test expects the duration of a `keydown` that causes no repaint to end at most 8 ms after the `processingEnd` of the last `keydown` (Chromium flushes these entries from a posted task); the specification sets the duration to the rendering timestamp of the next rendering update (https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#dispatch-pending-event-timing-entries), which runs at the next frame, 15.5 ms after `processingEnd` (`217.7` instead of at most `210.2`)

fetch/api/cors/cors-preflight-safelist-v.description: 1 of 5 subtests (in the window and the dedicated worker): "fetch" appends `Accept: */*` to the header list of a request without `Accept` before the CORS-preflight (https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetching, step 12), and the CORS-unsafe request-header names count every CORS-safelisted header in the size above 1024 bytes (https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#cors-unsafe-request-header-names): with 1200 bytes of `Content-Language`, the preflight asks for `accept,content-language`, but the preflight response of the test only allows `content-language`, so the fetch fails with a `TypeError` (the test expects the `Accept` header added by the user agent not to be counted, as in Chromium)

fetch/corb/script-resource-with-json-par.description: Opaque Response Blocking (ORB) of no-cors responses: the cross-origin responses labeled as HTML, XML, JSON or plain text that start with a JSON parser breaker are executed as scripts and throw a syntax error

geolocation/watchPosition-accuracyMode.h.description: 1 of 2 subtests: the `accuracyMode` member of `PositionOptions` (approximate positions), which is not in the vendored IDL of the Geolocation specification

hr-time/idlharness.any.js.description: 1 of 31 subtests (in every global): `interfaces/hr-time.idl` extends `AudioWorkletGlobalScope` with a partial interface, but the dependencies of the test are only `html` and `dom`, not `webaudio` where `AudioWorkletGlobalScope` is defined, so idlharness fails "Partial interface AudioWorkletGlobalScope: original interface defined" whatever the implementation

html/cross-origin-opener-policy/reportin.description: 1 of 2 subtests: the tentative delivery of the `coop-access-violation` reports to the `ReportingObserver`s of a window whose `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy-Report-Only` has no reporting endpoint: the HTML Standard reports an access only when the opener policy has a reporting endpoint (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsers.html#coop-check-access-report), as the library does

html/dom/documents/resource-metadata-man.description: the `document.parsed`, `document.contentLoaded` and `document.loaded` promises (https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/1936, tentative): they are `undefined`

html/dom/partial-updates/tentative/fragm.description: the inheritance of the sanitizer of the enclosing parse by `<template for src>` (declarative partial updates, https://github.com/WICG/declarative-partial-updates/blob/main/fragment-include-explainer.md): the sanitization of the fetched content only depends on the `sanitize` attribute of the template, so `sanitize="unsafe"` runs the scripts inside `streamHTML()` or inside the content of a safe outer `template src`, and a default `template src` inside `streamHTMLUnsafe({sanitizer})` does not apply the bespoke sanitizer (with `removeUnsafe()`)

the `sanitize` IDL attribute of `HTMLTemplateElement` (declarative partial updates, https://github.com/WICG/declarative-partial-updates/blob/main/fragment-include-explainer.md): `template.sanitize` is `undefined` (only the content attribute is read by the parser)

the MIME type check of the content of `<template for src>` (declarative partial updates, https://github.com/WICG/declarative-partial-updates/blob/main/fragment-include-explainer.md): only a `text/fragment` response must be patched in, the library patches the content of any successful response (`text/html` and `text/plain` too)

html/semantics/document-metadata/the-lin.description: CSS module style sheet links (`<link rel=stylesheet import="specifier">`, https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/ShadowDOM/explainer.md): the `import` attribute is ignored, the link fetches its `href` as a classic style sheet (no `load` event without `href`, `error` for an invalid one), so the tests time out or fail; `module-stylesheet-controlled.py` and `module-stylesheet-encoding.py` are not emulated either

FileAPI/url/sandboxed-iframe.html.description: the iframes created by the sandboxed document inherit its sandboxing flags, so the document loaded from the blob URL gets a new opaque origin (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsers.html#determining-the-origin, step 1) and is cross-origin with its creator; the two iframe subtests fail the same way in Chrome, Firefox and Safari
the page of the sandboxed iframe loads `url-with-fetch.any.js` without its `META: script=/common/gc.js`, so its call to `garbageCollect()` throws a `ReferenceError` (in every browser)

animation-worklet/idlharness.any.js*.description: the object of the test, `new WorkletAnimation("name")`, throws a TypeError: no animator named `name` is registered in the animation worklet ("If documentAnimatorDefinitions[animatorName] does not exists, throw an TypeError"), and the worker variant evaluates it in a worker, where `WorkletAnimation` (`[Exposed=Window]`) is not defined; `CSS.animationWorklet` is only exposed in the secure contexts, as the `Worklet` interface it returns, and the test is not served over HTTPS (see css/css-paint-api/idlharness.html); these subtests fail in every browser

animation-worklet/inactive-timeline.http.description: the test uses the `scrollSource` option and attribute of `ScrollTimeline`, of an old draft of Scroll-driven Animations (now `source`; the times are now progress-based instead of the times of a `timeRange`): `animation.timeline.scrollSource` is undefined and the test throws; fails in every browser

animation-worklet/playback-rate.https.ht.description: the scroll-linked subtests use the `scrollSource` option and attribute of `ScrollTimeline`, of an old draft of Scroll-driven Animations (now `source`): `animation.timeline.scrollSource` is undefined and they throw (the last one waits for a local time in milliseconds that a progress-based timeline never gives: it times out); they fail in every browser

animation-worklet/scroll-timeline-writin.description: the test creates its timeline with `new ScrollTimeline({ scrollSource, orientation })`, the options of an old draft of Scroll-driven Animations (now `source` and `axis`, with progress-based times instead of the times of a `timeRange`): the unknown members are ignored, so the timeline is the scroll timeline of the scrolling element of the document, which does not scroll (its progress stays 0%, so the transform is the one of the first keyframe); fails in every browser

animation-worklet/worklet-animation-anim.description: the test has no encoding declaration and one of its animator names is Persian: decoded as windows-1252 (UTF-8 is not detected for a document of the network, as in the browsers: `encoding-detection/utf-8.html`), the name contains code points that are not identifier code points (U+00AF, U+00B2…), so `registerAnimator()` throws a TypeError ("If name is not a valid <ident>") and the module does not register the animators

animation-worklet/worklet-animation-crea.description: `new WorkletAnimation('test-animator', [])` is expected to throw a NotSupportedError: the draft creates a WorkletGroupEffect without children (https://drafts.css-houdini.org/css-animation-worklet-1/#dom-workletanimation-workletanimation); `new WorkletAnimation('unregistered-animator', effect)` is expected to throw an InvalidStateError DOMException: the draft, which is followed, throws a TypeError ("If documentAnimatorDefinitions[animatorName] does not exists, throw an TypeError"); both are behaviors of the former Chromium implementation; they fail in every browser

animation-worklet/worklet-animation-loca.description: the last two subtests wait for `animation.currentTime > 1000` on an animation whose effect ends at 1000 ms: a worklet animation is an animation, which is finished and whose current time is limited to the end of its effect (https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-1/#update-an-animations-finished-state), so the animator never gets a current time over 1000 and the subtest times out; the worklet animations of the former Chromium implementation never finished

animation-worklet/worklet-animation-with.description: `play()` is expected to throw an InvalidStateError for an effect without keyframes: neither Web Animations nor the Animation Worklet draft make such an effect invalid (a behavior of the former Chromium implementation); fails in every browser

badging/badge-error.https.any.js*.description: expects `setAppBadge([])` to reject with a `TypeError`, but an empty array converts to the number 0 (`ToNumber('')`, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-unsigned-long-long), which clears the badge

badging/setAppBadge_cross_origin.sub.htt.description: calls `postMessage()` on the `iframe` element instead of its `contentWindow`: every subtest throws a `TypeError`

clear-site-data/resource.html.description: the `http resource on a https page` subtest: the https iframe navigates itself to the `http:` URL of `send_report.html`, which is blocked as mixed content (the navigation of a child navigable from a document whose origin is potentially trustworthy, https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-mixed-content/#should-block-fetch), so the report is never posted and the test times out

client-hints/accept-ch/meta/resource-in-.description: the `<meta http-equiv="Accept-CH">` element follows two `script` elements that have executed: the Delegate-CH algorithm of the spec (whose rules the library applies to the `accept-ch` pragma, which is not specified anymore) ignores the element once a `link`, `style` or `script` element has begun to execute; only Chromium applies it

the `<meta http-equiv="Delegate-CH">` element follows two `script` elements that have executed: step 2 of the Delegate-CH algorithm of the spec ignores the element once a `link`, `style` or `script` element has begun to execute; only Chromium applies it

client-hints/accept-ch/permissions-polic.description: the tests load `/client-hints/resources/permissions-policy-navigation.js`, which does not exist (the file is `feature-policy-navigation.js`): `test_frame` is not defined, and the harness reports the unhandled rejection as an error in every browser

the `Permissions-Policy` header that the test expects is in `feature-policy.sub.https.html.headers`, which is not the headers file of the test: without it `Sec-CH-DPR` is sent to the origin of the document and no hint is delegated to the other origin (the test fails in every browser)

client-hints/clear-site-data/clear-site-.description: in step 6, the cross-site iframe navigates its top-level traversable to a cross-site URL without user activation, which the framebusting intervention blocks (as in Firefox and Safari), so the page that reports the client hints never loads; fails in every browser

client-hints/critical-ch/critical-ch.nav.description: the test page is given to the library as the response of a navigation (`BrowsingContext.Navigate(url, response)`): no request is sent, so its `Critical-CH` header cannot restart the navigation and `criticalCHRestart` is 0 (the restart of a fetched navigation is covered by the other `critical-ch` tests)

client-hints/http-equiv-accept-ch-iframe.description: the test loads `resources/permissions-policy-navigation.js`, which does not exist (the file is `feature-policy-navigation.js`): `test_frame` is not defined, and the harness reports the unhandled rejection as an error in every browser

client-hints/meta-equiv-delegate-ch-ifra.description: the test loads `resources/permissions-policy-navigation.js`, which does not exist (the file is `feature-policy-navigation.js`): `test_frame` is not defined, and the harness reports the unhandled rejection as an error in every browser

client-hints/service-workers/intercept-r.description: the test expects the request of the `fetch` event of the service worker to have the `Sec-CH-Device-Memory` and `Device-Memory` headers: the spec appends the client hints in HTTP-network-or-cache fetch, after the service worker handled the request (Chromium, the only browser that passes, adds them to the navigation request before)

clipboard-apis/async-navigator-clipboard.description: the test expects `write()` of an `image/png` representation whose data is a string to reject with a `TypeError` (Chromium): the string is the data of the representation (https://w3c.github.io/clipboard-apis/#dom-clipboard-write), and it is rejected with a `DataError` because it is not a PNG image, as `async-write-image-read-image.https.html` expects for a blob
the `onclipboardchange` event handler attribute of `Clipboard` (the event is fired to the listeners only)
a new `clipboard.write()` does not reject the pending one with `NotAllowedError` (the test waits for the pending promise)

clipboard-apis/async-svg-read-write.tent.description: the single subtest also expects the inline style that the Chromium read-time sanitizer adds to the `<svg>` element (`color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-size: medium; ...`, the computed style of the copied content), which no specification defines

clipboard-apis/async-unsanitized-html-fo.description: inlining the computed style of the elements in the unsanitized `text/html` read (a Chromium-specific expectation)

clipboard-apis/clipboard-copy-selection-.description: dropping `opacity` from the inline style of the copied `text/html` (the tentative behavior of w3c/clipboard-apis#246): the copied `<span>` keeps `opacity: 0.5`; the next subtest then times out

clipboard-apis/detached-iframe/*.description: the tests expect `read()`, `write()`, `readText()` and `writeText()` of the clipboard of a detached iframe to return `undefined` (the Chromium bindings do not run the operations of a destroyed execution context): these operations return a promise (https://w3c.github.io/clipboard-apis/#clipboard-interface), which is rejected with a `NotAllowedError` because the document is not fully active

clipboard-apis/permissions-policy/clipbo.description: the test expects `navigator.clipboard.readText()` to resolve, so it assumes that the system clipboard holds text when the test starts: `readText()` rejects with a `NotFoundError` when the clipboard has no text item (https://w3c.github.io/clipboard-apis/#dom-clipboard-readtext), and the clipboard of the runner is empty (the permission and the policy allow the read)

the test expects `navigator.clipboard.readText()` to resolve, so it assumes that the system clipboard holds text when the test starts: `readText()` rejects with a `NotFoundError` when the clipboard has no text item (https://w3c.github.io/clipboard-apis/#dom-clipboard-readtext), and the clipboard of the runner is empty (the permission and the policy allow the read)

clipboard-apis/permissions/readText-gran.description: the test expects `navigator.clipboard.readText()` to resolve, so it assumes that the system clipboard holds text when the test starts: `readText()` rejects with a `NotFoundError` when the clipboard has no text item (https://w3c.github.io/clipboard-apis/#dom-clipboard-readtext), and the clipboard of the runner is empty (the permission and the policy allow the read)

compat/idlharness.window.js.description: `window.orientation` and the `orientationchange` event handlers must not be exposed on non-mobile user agents (https://compat.spec.whatwg.org/#windoworientation-api); fails in the desktop browsers

compression/decompression-brotli-large-w.description: the large window Brotli format (the Brotli decoder of .NET does not enable it)

compute-pressure/compute_pressure_detach.description: expects the behavior of Chromium: the interface objects of the window of a detached iframe are removed, and `observe()` rejects with a `NotSupportedError`; per the specification the window keeps its interfaces, and a detached document is not allowed to use the `compute-pressure` feature, so `observe()` rejects with a `NotAllowedError`

contacts/contacts-select.https.window.js.description: the subtest of the picker that cannot be opened (`setSelectedContacts(null)`) expects a `TypeError`, as Chromium rejects; the specification rejects with an `InvalidStateError` when launching the contact picker fails (https://w3c.github.io/contact-picker/#dom-contactsmanager-select, step 11.1)

the subtest of the second `select()` while the picker is showing expects an `InvalidStateError`; the first call consumes the user activation (step 5 of https://w3c.github.io/contact-picker/#dom-contactsmanager-select) before the flag of the showing picker is checked (step 6), so the second call has no transient activation and is rejected with a `SecurityError` (step 4)

container-timing/tentative/containertimi.description: reporting from scratch the content of a container root inserted again: its record is reset while it is disconnected, but the paint timing reports each image and text once per document (a reinserted image or text is not painted again), so no new entry is reported

starting a container over when its `containertiming` attribute is removed and set again, or changed, between two rendering updates: the record of the container root is kept (it is only reset when the root has no attribute or is disconnected at a rendering update), so the entry has the `firstRenderTime` of the first paint, before the change

starting a container over when its `containertiming` attribute is removed and set again, or changed, between two rendering updates: the record of the container root is kept (it is only reset when the root has no attribute or is disconnected at a rendering update), so the entry has the `firstRenderTime` of the first paint, before the change

reporting from scratch the content of a container root moved to another parent between two rendering updates (`appendChild()`, `moveBefore()`): its record is kept (it is only reset when the root is disconnected or has no `containertiming` attribute at a rendering update), and its image is not reported again (the paint timing reports each image and text once per document), so no new entry is reported

reporting from scratch the content of a container root moved to another parent between two rendering updates (`appendChild()`, `moveBefore()`): its record is kept (it is only reset when the root is disconnected or has no `containertiming` attribute at a rendering update), and its image is not reported again (the paint timing reports each image and text once per document), so no new entry is reported

reporting from scratch the content of a container root inserted again: its record is reset while it is disconnected, but the paint timing reports each image and text once per document (a reinserted image or text is not painted again), so no new entry is reported

container-timing/tentative/nested-contai.description: reporting from scratch the content of a container root inserted again: its record is reset while it is disconnected, but the paint timing reports each image and text once per document (a reinserted image or text is not painted again), so no new entry is reported

content-security-policy/frame-src/frame-.description: the test expects the violation of the redirect to have the origin of the redirect target as blocked URI, but the blocked URI of a request is the URL of the request, not its current URL (https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#create-violation-for-request); fails in Firefox

content-security-policy/inheritance/inhe.description: the `blob` variant expects a `blob:` document to inherit the policies of the creator of the blob URL, but a document of a local scheme inherits the policy container of the initiator of the navigation (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsers.html#determining-navigation-params-policy-container); fails in Chromium and Firefox

content-security-policy/media-src/media-.description: the test sets the `src` of a `source` element from a script that follows its `video` element in the markup, and expects two violations of `media-src`. The synchronous section of the resource selection algorithm of the `video` element runs once the event loop reaches a stable state (a microtask, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#concept-media-load-algorithm), and the parser performs a microtask checkpoint before it runs the script (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#scriptEndTag): the `source` candidate has no `src` then (the error event of the source is fired), and setting it afterwards has no effect (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/embedded-content.html#the-source-element), so only the violation of the other `video` element is reported and the violation subtest times out. The browsers run the section after the script

content-security-policy/navigation/to-ja.description: the test expects the policies of the target of a `javascript:` URL navigation to block it, but the navigation is checked with the policy container of its source (https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#should-block-navigation-request, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#navigate); Chromium and Firefox also check the policies of the target

content-security-policy/object-src/objec.description: plugins: an `object` or `embed` element without URL whose type is a plugin type falls back without loading anything, so `object-src` reports no violation

content-security-policy/reporting/post-r.description: the test waits for the `csp-violation` reports of a policy without `report-to` (Chromium): CSP generates them only for the `report-to` directive (https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#report-violation, step 3.5), as in Firefox

content-security-policy/reporting/report.description: the test expects the identical violations of the string timers to be reported once (as Chromium does), CSP reports each violation (https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#report-violation)
the violations of the obsolete `block-all-mixed-content` directive (https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-mixed-content/) are not reported; fails in Firefox and Safari

content-security-policy/sandbox/autoplay.description: the test reads the document of an iframe that its `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox` header gives an opaque origin: a `SecurityError` is thrown and the harness reports an error, as in Chromium, Gecko and WebKit

content-security-policy/sandbox/sandbox-.description: the `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox` header of `support/sandboxed-post-message-to-parent.headers` is not applied by wptserve, which only reads `sandboxed-post-message-to-parent.html.headers`: the frame is not sandboxed and its message is logged

content-security-policy/script-src/scrip.description: the test expects a nonce surrounded by whitespace (`nonce="   noncynonce    "`) to match `'nonce-noncynonce'`, as Chromium and WebKit strip the whitespace; the specification compares the values (https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#match-element-to-source-list), as Firefox

a parser-inserted module script allowed by `strict-dynamic` through a policy hash of its `integrity` attribute runs the module of a `modulepreload` entry whose integrity was not verified against that metadata (the module map hit skips the integrity check of the script element); the test expects it to be blocked with a `script-src-elem` violation

content-security-policy/script-src/tenta.description: the URL hash sources of `script-src` (`'url-sha256-…'`, tentative) and their reports

content-security-policy/securitypolicyvi.description: the `redirect` subtest expects the opening handshake of a `WebSocket` to follow the redirect of `/common/redirect.py` to a URL that `connect-src` blocks, and to report its violation: the request of the handshake has the redirect mode `error` (https://websockets.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-websocket-establish), so the redirect is a network error and its location is never fetched nor checked (no browser passes the test)

content-security-policy/wasm-unsafe-eval.description: a `WebAssembly.Module` deserialized by `postMessage()` in a realm whose policy does not allow `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` is not compiled again, so no `wasm-eval` violation is reported: deserializing a module does not compile it (https://webassembly.github.io/spec/web-api/#serialization) and no specification checks the policy there (only Firefox reports a violation; Chromium and Safari fail it too)

content-security-policy/style-src/inline.description: subtests 19 and 20 expect the declarations of a `style` attribute blocked by `style-src` to apply (they fail in every browser), and `non-HTML namespace` expects `getAttribute('style')` to return the empty string for the blocked attribute of an `svg` element (only Firefox does)

content-security-policy/embedded-enforce.description: the subsumption of the Trusted Types directives (`require-trusted-types-for` and `trusted-types`, a tentative extension of https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-cspee/#subsume-policy): the subsumption only compares the source lists, the sandboxing flags and `upgrade-insecure-requests`, so a response that does not enforce the required Trusted Types directives is loaded

cookies/attributes/attributes-ctl.sub.ht.description: a `Secure` attribute followed by a tab sets the cookie from an insecure page, which RFC 6265bis rejects (fails in every browser)

cookies/name/name-ctl.html.description: a line feed or a carriage return in the `Set-Cookie` header ends the header, so the cookie is neither rejected nor modified (fails in every browser)

cookies/origin-bound-cookies/scheme-boun.description: the last check of the http: popup reads the cookie of the https: origin of the same host with a `fetch()`: the request is cross-site (schemeful same-site), and the cookie, set without `SameSite` attribute, is `Lax` by default, so it is not sent; the other checks of scheme-bound cookies pass

cookies/value/value-ctl.html.description: a line feed or a carriage return in the `Set-Cookie` header ends the header, so the cookie is neither rejected nor modified (fails in every browser)

cors/client-hint-request-headers-2.tenta.description: the client hint request headers (`device-memory`, `dpr`, `width`, `viewport-width`...) are not CORS-safelisted request-headers (the Fetch Standard does not list them; only Chrome does), so the request has a preflight, which `cors-makeheader.py` does not allow

cors/simple-requests-ch.tentative.htm.description: the client hint request headers (`save-data`, `device-memory`, `dpr`, `width`, `viewport-width`) are not CORS-safelisted request-headers (the Fetch Standard does not list them; only Chrome does), so the requests have a preflight, which `preflight.py` does not allow

css/compositing/canvas-composite-modes.h.description: `destination` and `plus-darker` are not operators of `globalCompositeOperation` (no browser supports them), and the expected alpha of `lighter` is not clamped to 1

css/compositing/mix-blend-mode/mix-blend.description: the test expects the computed `z-index` not to be `auto` when `mix-blend-mode` creates a stacking context, but `z-index` computes to its specified value (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#propdef-z-index): a stacking context does not change it; Edge fails too (wpt.fyi)

css/css-anchor-position/anchor-name-001..description: expects the last anchor element in tree order; https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position-1/#target now chooses the nearest ancestor of the positioned box that is an acceptable anchor element first (w3c/csswg-drafts#13364)

css/css-anchor-position/anchor-name-in-s.description: expects an `anchor()` reference of a shadow tree not to match the `anchor-name` of its host declared in the outer tree; the tree-scoped names are loosely matched (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping-1/#css-tree-scoped-name: a reference matches a name declared in a shadow-including ancestor tree)

css/css-anchor-position/anchor-position-.description: expects the last anchor element in tree order; https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position-1/#target now chooses the nearest ancestor of the positioned box that is an acceptable anchor element first (w3c/csswg-drafts#13364)

css/css-anchor-position/anchor-scroll-01.description: the end of a scroll as an anchor recalculation point (w3c/csswg-drafts#14112): once scrolling stops, the positioned element is not laid out again with the current scroll offsets (only the default scroll shift is applied). The CSS Working Group resolved it ("Once the UA is confident that the scroll operation has stopped, MUST ensure the layout is consistent with a full relayout"), but the specification is not edited yet (the issue has the Needs Edits label)

css/css-anchor-position/position-area-sc.description: "Reattach at 40,60" expects the boxes reattached in the same animation frame (`display: none`, a forced style update, then `display: block`) to keep the scroll offsets remembered before (the layout at 0,0, e1 at x=100), as its comment says ("there will be no anchor recalculation point" before the ResizeObserver events of an earlier draft); https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position-1/#anchor-recalculation-point now says that an anchor recalculation point occurs "whenever that element begins generating boxes (aka switches from display:none [...]) identical to when it starts running CSS animations", so the boxes are laid out with the remembered scroll offsets 40,60 (e1 at x=80); the subtest also expects `offsetLeft` right after `container.style.display = "flow-root"` (no recalculation point) not to include the default scroll shift that the previous subtest includes at the same scroll position (x=100 instead of 60), Chromium's snapshot of the scroll offsets taken once per frame; tentative, Firefox fails it with the result of the specification (e1 x = 80)

css/css-animations/KeyframeEffect-getKey.description: `getKeyframes()` of a CSS animation returns the specified values of the `@keyframes` rule (`var()` is not substituted, the custom properties are listed) instead of computed values

css/css-animations/dialog-backdrop-anima.description: the animations of `::backdrop` (only `::before`, `::after` and `::marker` have CSS animations and transitions)

css/css-backgrounds/parsing/background-p.description: contradictory expectations, `x-start` alone computes to `x-start` but `0.5em, x-start, x-end` expects `20px, 0%, 100%` (fails in every browser)
contradictory expectations, `y-start` alone computes to `y-start` but `0.5em, y-start, y-end` expects `20px, 0%, 100%` (fails in every browser)

css/css-borders/outline-offset-rounding..description: `outline-offset` is not snapped to device pixels like `outline-width`

css/css-borders/tentative/parsing/border.description: the newer `border-clip` grammar (`normal`, unitless `0` kept); the webref grammar `none | [<length-percentage> | <flex>]+` is used
the newer `border-clip` grammar (`normal` instead of `none`); the webref grammar is used
the newer `border-clip` grammar (`normal`, unitless `0` kept); the webref grammar is used

css/css-borders/tentative/parsing/box-sh.description: expects the unitless `0` of a `<length>` to be kept in the specified value (it is serialized as `0px`, as the browsers do for the other length properties); no browser implements `box-shadow-blur`

expects the named colors of `red, blue` to be serialized as `rgb()` in the specified value, while `red` alone is kept (named colors are kept in the specified value); no browser implements `box-shadow-color`
expects the unitless `0` of `10px 0` and `0 10px` to be kept in the computed value, while `0 0` computes to `0px`; no browser implements `box-shadow-offset`
expects the unitless `0` of a `<length>` to be kept in the specified value (it is serialized as `0px`, as the browsers do for the other length properties); no browser implements `box-shadow-offset`
