css/css-box/margin-trim/computed-margin-.description: the test expects the margins of the flex and grid items that `margin-trim` trimmed in an old draft to compute to `0`: the trimming of the items of the flex and grid containers was removed from the property (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13731: it applies to the block containers and the multi-column containers, and its `inline` values are no longer valid), and a trimmed margin keeps its resolved value (css/css-box/margin-trim/margin-trim-computed-value.html); as in Chrome

css/css-box/margin-trim/block-container-.description: expects the computed `margin-block-end` of the boxes whose margins `margin-trim` truncated to be `0px` (the layout and the heights are as expected): https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box-4/#margin-trim only truncates them in the layout, and css/css-box/margin-trim/margin-trim-computed-value.html expects a trimmed margin to keep its resolved value

css/css-color-hdr/parsing.html.description: expects `dynamic-range-limit-mix()` with a single parameter or with percentages that sum to zero to be invalid, but the spec now takes one or more parameters, like `color-mix()` (w3c/csswg-drafts#14454), and a zero sum computes to the initial value (w3c/csswg-drafts#11678)

css/css-color/parsing/color-computed-pow.description: a computed value with a negative lightness or a hue that serializes as 360 cannot round-trip, as parsing clamps the lightness and normalizes the hue (fails in every browser)

css/css-conditional/container-queries/co.description: `calc()` in an `SVGLength`, and setting the `value` of an `SVGLength` with a CSS unit (it keeps the unit instead of becoming a number)

css/css-conditional/container-queries/sc.description: the queries `(scrollable: var(...))` are not in a `scroll-state()` function: they are unknown features (`<general-enclosed>`), which never match (fails in Chrome too)

css/css-conditional/container-queries/st.description: the first argument of `attr()` written in a `{}` block (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#component-function-commas): `attr({data-untyped})` is not unwrapped, so it never matches

css/css-conditional/match-container.tent.description: `matchContainer()` throwing a `SyntaxError` for an unparsable query (changed upstream): it returns a `ContainerQueryList` that does not match, with an empty `query`

css/css-contain/content-visibility/conte.description: the size containment is expected as soon as the element stops being relevant to the user (before the next rendering update, which determines its proximity to the viewport), and its last remembered size (`content-visibility: auto` implies `contain-intrinsic-size: auto`) is ignored: all the browsers fail these subtests

css/css-easing/linear-timing-functions-s.description: the specified value of `linear(calc(0/0), 1)` is expected in its computed form (`linear(0 0%, 1 100%)`) while the other specified values keep their authored form (`linear(0, 1)`): Chrome and Firefox fail the authored forms, Safari fails this one

css/css-env/env-fallback-braces.html.description: an argument of `env()` written in a `{}` block (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#component-function-commas): the fallback is not unwrapped (a block alone) nor rejected when the block is mixed with other values

css/css-env/env-parsing.html.description: the `<declaration-value>` argument of `env()` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-env-1/#funcdef-env): the name and the indices are validated at parse time (`<custom-ident> <integer [0,∞]>*`) instead of at substitution time, so `env(10px)` or `env(test1 test2, green)` are invalid

css/css-env/indexed-env.tentative.html.description: the `<declaration-value>` argument of `env()` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-env-1/#funcdef-env): the name and the indices are validated at parse time (`<custom-ident> <integer [0,∞]>*`) instead of at substitution time, so `env(10px)` or `env(test1 test2, green)` are invalid

css/css-env/syntax.tentative.html.description: the `<declaration-value>` argument of `env()` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-env-1/#funcdef-env): the name and the indices are validated at parse time (`<custom-ident> <integer [0,∞]>*`) instead of at substitution time, so `env(10px)` or `env(test1 test2, green)` are invalid

css/css-flexbox/intrinsic-size/row-use-c.description: an item that cannot shrink and whose flex basis is `auto` contributes its min-content size to the min-content size of the container (its flex base size under a min-content constraint, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-flexbox-1/#algo-main-item, as WPT css/css-flexbox/intrinsic-size/row-001.html expects); the subtest `no overflow 2` expects its max-content size, from the use cases of a proposed Chrome algorithm ("liberal pass conditions"; Chrome fails 3 of the 6 subtests, Firefox and Safari all of them)

css/css-fonts/animations/font-palette-an.description: the last subtest runs `@keyframes animFrom { from { font-palette: --custom } }` with `animation-fill-mode: forwards` on an element whose `style` attribute sets `font-palette: --custom`, and expects `normal` at the end of the animation: the neutral `to` keyframe is the underlying value (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-animations-1/#keyframes), `--custom`, so the animated value is `--custom`, as in Firefox and Safari (only Chrome returns `normal`)

css/css-fonts/animations/font-palette-in.description: the two subtests that read the computed value directly (`An interpolation to inherit updates correctly on a parent style change.`, `Test additive animations`) expect `palette-mix(in oklab, normal, light)`, with the default color space: the computed value is `palette-mix(normal, light)`, as `css/css-fonts/parsing/palette-mix-computed.html` requires since the color interpolation method of `palette-mix()` is optional (`palette-mix(in oklab, light 30%, dark)` computes to `palette-mix(light 30%, dark 70%)`); the test was not updated with that change of the specification (the interpolated values of the other 112 subtests are compared with the computed value of the expectation, and pass)

css/css-fonts/animations/font-weight-com.description: underlying 200, from add 600 (800) to replace 500 at -0.3 is 800 + 0.3 × 300 = 890, the result of the library; the expected 889.75 is the result of the internal precision of the font weights of Blink, not of the interpolation (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-4/#combine-numbers)

css/css-fonts/calc-in-font-variation-set.description: the specified-value subtest reads the inline `div.style`, but the value is set in a style sheet rule (it fails in every browser)

css/css-fonts/fallback-url-to-local.html.description: the width of the text shaped with the font is measured (fallback to a `local()` font while the remote one loads)

css/css-fonts/font-feature-values-serial.description: the serialization of `@font-feature-values` of w3c/csswg-drafts#14658: on one line (`{ }` when empty), `font-display` first, then the blocks in a fixed order (`@swash`, `@stylistic`, `@ornaments`, `@annotation`, `@character-variant`, `@styleset`, `@historical-forms`); the blocks are serialized on their own lines in the order of the style sheet, as in Firefox and Safari

css/css-fonts/generic-family-keywords-00.description: the `-webkit-generic()` subtests fail in every browser: the function is not a valid `<family-name>`, so the declaration is invalid

css/css-fonts/variations/at-font-face-fo.description: expects an oblique face with an angle of the opposite sign to be preferred over an italic face; https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts-4/#font-style-matching checks the italic faces before the oblique angles of the opposite sign

css/css-forms/appearance-base-cursor.htm.description: the cursors of the controls (`default`, `text`, `not-allowed`, also for a `label` and an `input type=range` without base appearance; csswg-drafts#14251) are not in the Basic Appearance User Agent Stylesheet of the specification, which the library applies: the controls inherit `cursor: pointer` from the body (only Chrome passes)

css/css-forms/input-file-base-appearance.description: the test expects a `border-radius` of 0.5em for `::file-selector-button`; the style sheet of the specification gives the buttons and the button-like controls `border-radius: 4px`

css/css-forms/input-text-base-appearance.description: the test expects no `border-radius`, `align-items: normal` (initial) and `user-select: auto` for a text field with base appearance; the style sheet of the specification gives it `border-radius: 4px` and `align-items: unsafe center`

css/css-grid/alignment/self-baseline/gri.description: the test depends on the non-standard `-webkit-text-orientation: sideways` of Blink and WebKit: it is defined by no specification, nor by the Compatibility Standard (https://compat.spec.whatwg.org/#css-simple-aliases), and Firefox does not support it (it fails 10 subtests); the test passes with the standard `text-orientation: sideways` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes-4/#text-orientation)

css/css-grid/grid-definition/grid-inline.description: expects the resolved value `none` for the implicit tracks of a grid without explicit tracks; all the browsers return the sizes of the implicit tracks

css/css-grid/grid-definition/grid-templa.description: expects the resolved value `none` for the implicit tracks of a grid without explicit tracks; all the browsers return the sizes of the implicit tracks

css/css-grid/grid-lanes/subgrid/grid-lan.description: the non-standard `::-webkit-scrollbar` pseudo-elements: the test makes the scrollbars 16px thick with them, and the classic scrollbars are 15px thick
the non-standard `::-webkit-scrollbar` pseudo-elements: the test makes the scrollbars 16px thick with them, and the classic scrollbars are 15px thick

css/css-grid/parsing/grid-template-colum.description: the expected value of the subtest `[a] repeat(2, [b] 20px [c d] 21px [e f g]) [h i] repeat(auto-fit, [j] auto [k l m] min-content [n o p q]) [r s]` contradicts https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#repeat-auto-fit: with one auto-placed item (N = 1), the first unoccupied track (the 20px track) is considered occupied, so all the tracks of the auto-fit repetition are empty and collapsed (as the same case with fixed sizes in a grid, css/css-grid/parsing/grid-template-columns-computed-withcontent.html). The expected value collapses the first 3 of the 6 repeated tracks (as many as the repetitions) and keeps the last 3, which the item sizes (30px + 158px + 30px): it matches Chromium only (the tentative intrinsic auto repetitions are implemented by Chromium only; Firefox and Safari fail every subtest). The other subtests pass

css/css-grid/parsing/grid-template-rows-.description: the expected value of the subtest `[a] repeat(2, [b] 20px [c d] 21px [e f g]) [h i] repeat(auto-fit, [j] auto [k l m] min-content [n o p q]) [r s]` contradicts https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#repeat-auto-fit: with one auto-placed item (N = 1), the first unoccupied track (the 20px track) is considered occupied, so all the tracks of the auto-fit repetition are empty and collapsed (as the same case with fixed sizes in a grid, css/css-grid/parsing/grid-template-columns-computed-withcontent.html). The expected value collapses the first 3 of the 6 repeated tracks (as many as the repetitions) and keeps the last 3, which the item sizes (30px + 158px + 30px): it matches Chromium only (the tentative intrinsic auto repetitions are implemented by Chromium only; Firefox and Safari fail every subtest). The other subtests pass

css/css-images/idlharness.html.description: `CSS.elementSources` (the element sources of the `element()` function, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images-4/#elementsources); no browser implements it

css/css-inline/baseline-source/baseline-.description: the test depends on overlay scrollbars: in the two `vertical-rl` cases whose line of 100px overflows the inline axis of the `textarea`, the classic scrollbar displayed at its block-start edge shifts its first line by 15px (`offsetLeft` 10 instead of 25); Chrome fails the same way

css/css-inline/inheritance.html.description: the test checks the properties of an old draft of CSS Inline (`initial-letters`, `initial-letters-align`, `initial-letters-wrap`, `initial-sizing`)

css/css-link-params/link-parameters-inva.description: the specification allows a `param()` without value (`param(--foo)` "indicates that the link parameter is using the default value, drawing from the '--foo' custom property on the element", https://drafts.csswg.org/css-link-params-1/#param) and an identifier as `<css-type>` (`<syntax-component>` includes `<ident>`): the test expects `param(--a)`, `param(--a), param(--b)`, `param(--)`, `param(--a` (closed at the end of the input) and `param(--a red)` (a parameter of type `red` with the default value) to be invalid

css/css-link-params/link-parameters-subs.description: the test uses the comma of the former grammar (`param(--color, var(--brand))`), which the specification replaced with a colon (`param(--color: var(--brand))`, w3c/csswg-drafts#14275): the declarations are invalid

css/css-logical/animation-003.tentative..description: `getKeyframes()` returns the logical properties of a keyframe as they are specified, not as the physical properties they map to (`height` for `block-size`)

css/css-logical/animations/logical-short.description: the `logical` keyword of the box shorthands (`margin: logical 300px`, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#logical-shorthand-keyword): the keyframe declaration is invalid, so `margin-top` is not animated

css/css-masking/parsing/mask-valid.sub.h.description: the expected longhands of `mask` do not include `mask-border-mode`, which the shorthand resets with the other `mask-border-*` longhands (https://drafts.fxtf.org/css-masking/#the-mask: "also resets mask-border", whose longhands include `mask-border-mode`; WPT css/css-masking/mask-shorthand-subproperties-reset.html expects it reset); the browsers do not support `mask-border-mode`

css/css-mixins/private/private-cssom-sty.description: the `CSSStyleRule` API of `CSSPrivateRule` (w3c/csswg-drafts#14427: `cssRules`, `insertRule()`, `selectorText`, `style`, `styleMap`): it is a plain `CSSRule`

css/css-multicol/multicol-fill-balance-0.description: a crash test of Blink (crbug.com/1289800) turned into a testharness test that relies on the saturation of the layout units of Blink: the content of the nested multi-column container is 1,234,567,990px tall, more than the largest length of Blink (2^25px), and is expected to fit in the two outer columns of 20,000,000px (`scrollWidth` 100); https://drafts.csswg.org/css-multicol-1/#overflow-columns creates additional columns in the inline direction for the content that does not fit in the columns of the container (`column-fill: auto` with a definite height), and CSS sets no limit to the lengths, so the outer container gets 62 columns (as the library lays it out)

css/css-multicol/scroll-width-height.ten.description: `scrollWidth`/`scrollHeight` of a fragmented box (the scrollable overflow of its fragments stitched together); the first fragment is used

css/css-overflow/parsing/line-clamp-vali.description: `line-clamp: 3 ellipsis auto` (with or without `-webkit-legacy`) is valid with the grammar of https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13670 (`[ <integer [1,∞]> || auto || <'block-ellipsis'> ] -webkit-legacy?`), but the test expects it to serialize as specified: the shorthand serializes its longhands in the canonical order of the grammar and omits the default `ellipsis` (https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#serialize-a-css-value), as the same test expects for `8 ellipsis` (serialized as `8`) and `auto 11` (serialized as `11 auto`), so the value is `3 auto`

css/css-overflow/scroll-markers/scroll-m.description: expects a clicked `::scroll-marker` to match `:focus` in the default (links) mode of `scroll-marker-group`, which contradicts the specification ("If the scroll marker group is in links mode: set the sequential focus navigation starting point to the originating element, losing focus from the scroll marker") and `scroll-marker-activation-retains-focus.html`; the rest of the test (the next Tab focuses the scroll target) works

css/css-paint-api/idlharness.html.description: the test is not served over HTTPS: `CSS.paintWorklet` is only exposed in the secure contexts, as the `Worklet` interface it returns (as in Chromium; the IDL of the specification does not annotate the attribute, although the worklets only exist in the secure contexts); the subtest fails in every browser

css/css-overflow/scrollable-overflow-tra.description: tentative test of the open issue https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/12113 (no resolution): it expects the untransformed border box of an in-flow child not to extend the scrollable overflow of its scroll container; https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow-3/#scrollable includes the in-flow content (with the paddings), as Chrome, Edge and Firefox, which fail the same 2 subtests with the same values (wpt.fyi)

tentative test of the open issue https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/12112 (no resolution): it expects the exact union of the nested rotated boxes (241px); as Chrome, Edge and Firefox, which fail both subtests (wpt.fyi), the scrollable overflow of each box is the bounding rectangle of its descendants, whose transformed bounding rectangle is the contribution of the box (300px)

css/css-page/page-rule-declarations-004..description: a dashed ident (`--a`) is accepted as an `@page` selector, as in Chrome, Firefox and Safari: it is an `<ident-token>`, which the grammar of the page selectors (`<page-selector> = [ <ident-token>? <pseudo-page>* ]!`) accepts

css/css-page/parsing/margin-rules-002.ht.description: the last three subtests read `pagerule.style.paddingLeft`: `CSSPageRule.style` is a `CSSPageDescriptors` (https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#csspagedescriptors), a `CSSStyleDeclaration` whose only attributes are the page descriptors (`margin*`, `size`, `pageOrientation`, `marks`, `bleed`), so `paddingLeft` is undefined (the declaration is kept: `getPropertyValue("padding-left")` returns `10px`); Blink exposes every property there, Gecko fails these subtests

css/css-page/parsing/page-orientation-co.description: the test expects `getComputedStyle(elm).pageOrientation` to be the empty string, but `page-orientation` is only a descriptor of `@page` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-page-3/#page-orientation-prop), and a `CSSStyleProperties` only has the camel-cased attributes of the supported CSS properties (https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#dom-cssstyleproperties-camel_cased_attribute): the attribute is undefined, as in Gecko (Blink implements the descriptor as an internal property)

css/css-position/backdrop-tree-abiding-s.description: `::backdrop` after `::slotted()` (the tree-abiding pseudo-elements of the slotted elements)

css/css-position/position-absolute-perce.description: the image of a `data:` URL is not available synchronously: the layout checked by the script that follows the image has no natural size yet (the browsers decode it before)

css/css-position/sticky/position-sticky-.description: the sticky positioning against the scroll containers of a single axis (`@supports named-feature()` of the proposal)

css/css-properties-values-api/animation/.description: the expected value omits the accumulation of the second item: at the middle of the third iteration of `50%` to `100px` with `iterationComposite: accumulate`, the value is the interpolated `calc(25% + 50px)` plus twice the final value `100px` (https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-1/#effect-accumulation-section), `calc(25% + 250px)`; the first item and the other list tests of the directory (e.g. `<length>#`: `50px` to `100px` gives `275px`) do accumulate it

the interpolation of the `<transform-function>` and `<transform-list>` registered custom properties with a matrix fallback (`mix()`)

css/css-properties-values-api/at-propert.description: a change of the initial value of a `@property` rule does not start a transition

css/css-properties-values-api/font-prope.description: `font-size: var(--x)` with a registered `<length>` `--x` whose value uses a font-relative unit (here in `atan2()` in `calc()`) is a dependency cycle (https://drafts.css-houdini.org/css-properties-values-api/#dependency-cycles-via-relative-units): both are invalid at computed-value time (`--x` is `0px`), as css/css-properties-values-api/unit-cycles.html requires and as in Chromium (Edge gets 0 too); the tentative test expects the parent's font instead (the 5 `font-size ... registered custom property` subtests)

the `<integer>` registered custom properties with `ex` and `cap` are rounded but compared with the unrounded length (0.1 tolerance): they pass only when the x-height and the cap height of the default font are whole numbers of px

css/css-properties-values-api/register-p.description: the test expects `CSS.registerProperty()` to throw a TypeError without the `inherits` member, which has a default value in the IDL of the specification (`boolean inherits = true`, https://drafts.css-houdini.org/css-properties-values-api-1/#dictdef-propertydefinition); the browsers still require it

css/css-properties-values-api/var-refere.description: a registered `<length>` property declared with `red` is invalid at computed-value time, so its computed value is its registered initial value ("the property becomes invalid at computed-value time (and thus resets to the registered initial value)", https://drafts.css-houdini.org/css-properties-values-api/#the-registerproperty-function; css-variables-2: registered custom properties act like non-custom properties when they are invalid at computed-value time), and `var()` substitutes the computed value of a registered property (https://drafts.css-houdini.org/css-properties-values-api/#substitution): `0px`, not the empty string the test expects

css/css-pseudo/events-on-after-before-ma.description: the sub-pseudo-element `::after::marker`: the box of the marker of a `::before`/`::after` list item is a box of its pseudo-element (it has no box quads and is hit as the `::after`)

css/css-pseudo/events-on-pseudo-element..description: the CSS animations and transitions of `::scroll-marker`: the test times out waiting for the `animationstart` event of its animation (the `pseudoTarget` of the animation, transition and focus events is not defined, UI Events only adds it to `UIEvent`)

css/css-pseudo/first-letter-allowed-prop.description: the animation properties on `::first-letter` (the browsers apply them, which https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo-4/#first-letter-styling allows): they are not in the properties that apply to the pseudo-element, so they are ignored

css/css-pseudo/first-line-allowed-proper.description: the animation properties on `::first-line` (the browsers apply them, which https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo-4/#first-line-styling allows): they are not in the properties that apply to the pseudo-element, so they are ignored

css/css-pseudo/idlharness.html.description: the setup calls `window.getPseudoElements()` and uses `CSSPseudoElementList`, which were removed from CSS Pseudo-Elements 4 (they are not in its IDL): the tests of the `CSSPseudoElement` object fail

css/css-pseudo/input-element-pseudo-open.description: clicking a text input with a `datalist` does not show its suggestions (the HTML Standard gives the Text state no input activation behavior, and Chromium does not match `:open` for it either), so `:open` does not match; `showPicker()` shows them, and the pickers of the date, time and color inputs open when they are clicked

css/css-pseudo/parsing/marker-supported-.description: expects the computed `list-style` to include `outside` (it contradicts css/css-lists/parsing/list-style-computed.sub.html)

expects the computed `list-style` to be `outside none disc` instead of its shortest serialization, `outside` (it contradicts css/css-lists/parsing/list-style-valid.html and list-style-computed.sub.html)

css/css-rhythm/computedstyle/inline-leve.description: the 12 other subtests pass; the `object` element without `data` attribute represents its fallback content (HTML, "the object element": no data, no image, plugin or content navigable), and HTML 15.4.1 "Embedded content" says that such an object element is "expected to be treated as an ordinary element in the rendering model": an empty inline box, to which `height` does not apply, so its `font-size: 0` container is 0px tall; the test expects the 20px of the `height` attribute of a replaced element (as the browsers, which render an empty object as replaced)

css/css-ruby/line-spacing-on-edges.tenta.description: the annotations of the first line of a block container use the space before it (its block-start margin, the space after the content of the last line of the previous block), as Chrome does (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/14405): the first line is extended by its annotations, because the stable tests css/css-ruby/ruby-annotation-pairing-001.html, ruby-annotation-with-margin.html and css/css-text-decor/text-emphasis-color-001.xht expect the annotations of a first line inside the paragraph even when it has a margin; the first subtest passes when the block-start margin is used

css/css-scroll-anchoring/contenteditable.description: `Ctrl+Home` does not move the caret to the start of the editing host (nor scroll to it), so the line is not inserted at the top

css/css-scroll-anchoring/history-restore.description: the scroll position of the viewport is not restored when a document is reloaded (the scroll restoration applies to the traversals to the same document)

css/css-scroll-snap/capturing-snap-posit.description: expects a box that is not a scroll container but has a `scroll-snap-type` to capture the snap areas of its descendants, while the snap areas are captured by the nearest scroll container (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scroll-snap-1/#snap-strictness); fails in every browser

css/css-scroll-snap/parsing/scroll-snap-.description: `scroll-snap-stop: before` is not in the grammar of the specification (`normal | always`, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scroll-snap-1/#scroll-snap-stop); fails in every browser

css/css-scroll-snap/scroll-initial-targe.description: compares the `scrollTop` of the scroller with the `offsetTop` of the target, which is rounded to an integer: the target is 127.5px down (after a spacer of 150% of the 85px scrollport) and the scroller is scrolled to 127.5px, `offsetTop` is 128; passes in Chrome only, whose scroll positions are snapped to whole pixels

css/css-scroll-snap/snap-after-relayout/.description: a scroll container without `tabindex` is not focusable (the keyboard-focusable scroll containers of the browsers)

css/css-shadow/has-slotted-functional-ch.description: the expected blue is written `rgb(0, 0,  255)` (two spaces), which never matches a serialized color (fails in every browser)
the expected blue is written `rgb(0, 0,  255)` (two spaces), which never matches a serialized color (fails in every browser)

css/css-sizing/responsive-iframe/respons.description: the cross-origin variant expects a `ResizeObserver` observation of the 150px height the iframe gets when it navigates to another origin, before the new document is measured (400px); this requires a rendering update while the new document is parsed, between its first script and the end of `slow.js` (a script that blocks for 0.5 s), which HTML leaves to the user agent (Chromium's parser yields to rendering after a time budget); the library renders once the document is parsed: `[200, 400]` instead of `[200, 150, 400]`

css/css-sizing/aspect-ratio-affects-cont.description: the image of a `data:` URL is not available synchronously: the layout checked by the script that follows the image has no natural size yet (the browsers decode it before)

css/css-syntax/non-ascii-codepoints.html.description: a missing comma in the ranges array (`[0x203f, 0x2040] [0x2070, 0x218f]`) makes an entry undefined and the script throws (fails in every browser)

css/css-tables/bounding-box-computation-.description: expects an empty row group before a non-empty one to be 0px wide (fails in every browser)

css/css-tables/height-distribution/perce.description: expects the percentage width of a form control in a zero-width table to resolve as `auto` in the measure of the columns (fails in every browser)

the subtest of the percentage heights of the replaced elements expects `height: 100%` of the `input` to resolve as `auto` (15px); the table has a length `height` (`0px`), so its cell has an explicit height and the percentage resolves against the used height of the cell in the second pass (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#table-cell-content-layout-second-pass), which the strut of the 16px font of the cell makes 18px

css/css-tables/html-to-css-mapping-2.htm.description: expects the mapping of an old draft of CSS Tables 3 (`table { border-color: gray }`, a 1px border for `frame=box`, the `inset` cell borders of `border` winning over `rules`); the rendering section of HTML (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#tables-2), which the library implements, has no gray border color (the tables with a `rules` or `frame` attribute and their cells get `border-color: black`), maps `border=0` to a 0px border width, and gives `rules=groups` (`border-style: none` on the cells) precedence over the cell borders of `border` (the later presentational hint wins); Firefox gets the same values (13/25) and Chrome and Safari pass fewer subtests

css/css-tables/html5-table-formatting-3..description: expects a cell that spans two empty explicit rows to share its height between them; CSS Tables 3 does not define it (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#row-layout runs "the same algorithm as the column measurement", with an EDITORIAL note; that algorithm gives the excess to the row where the cell originates), and every browser gives it to the last row (Safari to the first), as the library does and as WPT css/css-tables/tentative/rowspan-height-redistribution.html expects

css/css-tables/tentative/baseline-table..description: `.container 11` expects the rows of a table without column to size it; a table whose grid has no slot is an empty table, laid out with its computed width and height only (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#table-layout-algorithm, step [B]); fails in Firefox too

css/css-tables/tentative/table-height-re.description: tables 11, 12 and 25 expect the `height` of the rows and row groups of a table without column (no slot) to size it or to be distributed; an empty table is laid out with its computed width and height only (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#table-layout-algorithm, step [B]); fail in Firefox too

css/css-tables/tentative/tbody-height-re.description: tables 10 and 11 expect the `height` of a row group of a table without column (no slot) to size it; an empty table is laid out with its computed width and height only (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#table-layout-algorithm, step [B]); fail in Firefox and Safari too

css/css-text/animations/hyphenate-limit-.description: the values interpolated below 0 are clamped to 0 (the range of `<integer [0,∞]>`, as CSS Values requires for the interpolated values): at -0.5 the test expects the computed value of its invalid expected values (`-1 -1 -2`), the initial value `auto`; this engine gives `0 0`. Chrome and Safari fail these subtests too, Firefox passes them

css/css-text/i18n/ja/css-text-line-break.description: the test fails in every browser: UAX #14 allows a break between an ideograph and a prefix (ID ÷ PR), and CSS Text has no tailoring that forbids it
the test fails in every browser: UAX #14 allows a break between an ideograph and a prefix (ID ÷ PR), and CSS Text has no tailoring that forbids it

css/css-text/i18n/zh/css-text-line-break.description: the test fails in every browser: UAX #14 allows a break between an ideograph and a prefix (ID ÷ PR), and CSS Text has no tailoring that forbids it
the test fails in every browser: UAX #14 allows a break between an ideograph and a prefix (ID ÷ PR), and CSS Text has no tailoring that forbids it

css/css-text/parsing/text-align-last-com.description: the test expects the computed value of `text-align-last: match-parent` to be `match-parent`; it "computes as defined" for `text-align` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#text-align-last-property): to the computed value of the parent, `auto` here (fails in every browser: Chrome and Firefox do not support the value, Safari returns `auto` too)

css/css-text/parsing/text-spacing-comput.description: the `normal` keyword combinations of `text-spacing` (`normal normal`, `normal trim-start`, `trim-start normal`) are invalid: the grammar of CSS Text 4 is `none | auto | <spacing-trim> || <autospace>`, and `normal` is a `<spacing-trim>`, not an `<autospace>` (the `normal` of `text-autospace` is not part of `<autospace>`); no browser supports the shorthand

`fade()` takes a single `<length-percentage>` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow-4/#funcdef-text-overflow-fade): `fade(1px, 50%)` is invalid, where the test expects it to be a valid value

css/css-values/calc-size/animation/calc-.description: two subtests expect the expansions of Chrome, which the test itself says are "not fully specified": `0px` to `calc-size(calc-size(min-content, size + 20px), 2 * size)` keeps the nested basis, but preparing a `calc-size()` for interpolation always replaces a `calc-size()` basis with its own basis and substitutes its calculation (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#calc-size-prepare-for-interpolation: `calc-size(min-content, 0px + (1.5 * (20px + size)))`); and `calc-size(min-content, size * 4)` to the same value expects `size` for the product `1 * size`, which the simplification of a product keeps (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-4/#calc-simplification: only the numbers are multiplied together); Safari fails both subtests too (with the same `(1 * size)` for the second)

css/css-values/calc-size/calc-size-list-.description: 2 of 10 subtests: the test compares the widths with `assert_equals`, which relies on the exact arithmetic of the fixed-point layout units of the browsers (1/64px); CSS does not define the precision of the used values. The label of the controls is in a 13.333px font (10pt), so the min-content and max-content widths of the list box and of the drop-down box are not binary fractions (95.15364397949219px), and the library computes `calc-size(min-content, size)` and `calc-size(max-content, size + 25px)` by adding the paddings and borders to the resolved content width in another order than the reference `min-content`/`max-content` and the `+ 25` of the script: the widths differ by 6e-14px (95.15364397949213px, 121.15364397949213px instead of 121.15364397949219px)

css/css-values/calc-size/calc-size-typed.description: the test expects the root product of the calculation of `calc-size(max-content, size / 2)` in parentheses (`(0.5 * size)`), but not the root products of `calc-size(min-content, size * 2)` (`2 * size`) and `calc-size(10px, sign(size) * size)`: the calculation of `calc-size()` is serialized like the one of `calc()`, whose outer parentheses are removed (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-4/#serialize-a-calculation-tree), and the products nested in a sum keep theirs (`30px + (0.5 * size)`, as expected by the test); Chrome and Safari fail this subtest the same way (`0.5 * size`)

css/css-values/lh-rlh-on-root-001.html.description: the root line height is measured with the height of an absolutely positioned box

css/css-values/sign-in-keyframes-with-re.description: the first subtest expects the `1em` of the `font-style`, `font-weight`, `font-palette` and `font-variation-settings` keyframes to be the font size of the element (8px, so `sign(1em - 10px)` is -1): in the font-affecting properties, the font-relative lengths resolve against the metrics of the parent (16px, so the sign is 1 and `font-style` is `oblique 1.75deg`; https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-4/#font-relative-lengths), as `css/css-values/using-font-relative-units-in-font-properties.html` expects (Chrome and Safari pass it for `font-style`, `font-weight` and `font-variation-settings`); the non-font properties of the keyframes (`scale`, `rotate`, `text-size-adjust`) use the font size of the element, as expected

the test expects the interpolated `font-palette` as `palette-mix(in oklab, palette-mix(in lch, ...), palette-mix(in lch, ...))`, with the default color space: the computed value omits it (`palette-mix(palette-mix(in lch, ...), palette-mix(in lch, ...))`), as `css/css-fonts/parsing/palette-mix-computed.html` requires; the second subtest only fails for this

css/css-values/tree-counting/calc-siblin.description: the nested pseudo-element subtest calls `getComputedStyle(element, '::before::marker')`: `getComputedStyle()` parses its argument as a single `<pseudo-element-selector>` and returns an empty declaration block when it fails to parse (https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#dom-window-getcomputedstyle), and `::before::marker` is two pseudo-elements; the test acknowledges that it requires the unresolved https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/4456, and fails in every browser the same way (`""`)

css/css-values/tree-counting/sibling-fun.description: the `sibling-count()` rule of the test has a `negative: linear-gradient(green, green)` descriptor that the test expects to be dropped, but an `<image>` is a valid `<symbol>` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-counter-styles-3/#typedef-symbol), as `css/css-counter-styles/counter-style-at-rule/prefix-suffix-syntax.html` expects; the descriptors with `sibling-index()` and `sibling-count()` are dropped; the browsers pass because they do not support the image symbols

css/css-values/tree-counting/sibling-ind.description: the `--color` subtests expect the `from` keyframe value (`color(srgb 0 0.6 0)`) of a `step-end` animation to `red`: the step easing gives a transformed distance of 0, and the value is the interpolation at p = 0 (https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-1/#the-effect-value-of-a-keyframe-animation-effect), which is in the Oklab interpolation space when a color is not a legacy color (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-4/#interpolation-space), as `css/css-color/animation/color-interpolation.html` expects with the same `steps(1, end)` easing (`color(srgb 0 0 0)` to `color(srgb 1 1 1)` at 0 is `oklab(0 0 0)` in every browser); Safari fails these subtests the same way (Chrome and Firefox do not interpolate a color with a tree-counting function and keep the keyframe value)

css/css-values/tree-counting/tree-scoped.description: the test expects `sibling-index()` and `sibling-count()` in a `::part()` rule of the outer tree to be 1: they are tree-scoped references that fail to match an element of a descendant shadow tree, so they return 0 ("If the reference fails to match (because the element is, for example, in a descendent shadow tree from the stylesheet), the function returns 0", and the `::part(my-part)` example "Returns 0px", https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#tree-counting); Safari returns 0 too (Chrome and Firefox return 1, an earlier resolution)

css/css-values/viewport-units-scrollbars.description: the fractional values expect the used height rounded down to 1/64 px (the layout unit of Blink and WebKit, e.g. `1dvw` = 1.84375px instead of 1.85px): the specification does not round the used values

css/css-variables/variable-presentation-.description: the test expects legacy SVG 1.1 values (`visiblePainted`, `lr-tb`, `before-edge`, `Times New Roman`, empty defaults) that no current engine returns

css/css-variables/var-fallback-braces.ht.description: an argument of `var()` written in a `{}` block (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#component-function-commas): the fallback is not unwrapped (a block alone) nor rejected when the block is mixed with other values

css/css-view-transitions/navigation/no-v.description: the cross-origin redirects of a navigation are not tracked ("was created via cross-origin redirects"): a same-origin navigation through a cross-origin redirect has a view transition

css/css-view-transitions/navigation/two-.description: the two-phase view transitions (a preview transition started by the `navigate` event, tentative) and `NavigateEvent.deferPageSwap()`

css/css-view-transitions/scoped/auto-nam.description: the test expects the pseudo-elements of the names generated by `view-transition-name: auto` to be named `match-element` (`::view-transition-group(match-element)`): the specification generates a unique name starting with `-ua-` for each element (here `-ua-id-item1`...), and no browser returns `match-element` (Chrome fails the test too)

the test expects the pseudo-elements of the name generated by `view-transition-name: auto` on the root element of the scoped view transition to be named `match-element` (`::view-transition-group(match-element)`): the specification generates a unique name starting with `-ua-` (here `-ua-id-container`), and no browser returns `match-element` (Chrome names the group `root` and fails the test too)

css/css-view-transitions/scoped/collisio.description: the test expects the transition started on the inner element to be skipped when an element it captures is already captured by the active transition of the outer element (as Chrome does); the specification skips the other transition instead ("if any other active view transition contains element in its captured elements, then [...] skip that view transition with an AbortError"), so the `ready` promise of the second transition is fulfilled

css/css-view-transitions/unhandled-rejec.description: the test expects an `unhandledrejection` event for the `ready` and `finished` promises when the update callback rejects (Chrome only): the specification marks them as handled ("Mark as handled transition's ready promise", the finished promise is "marked as handled"), as Firefox and Safari do, so the third subtest times out

css/css-view-transitions/window-resize-a.description: the popup is resized by `resizeTo()` (its `innerWidth` is 150 after `resizeTo(150, 150)`), but the `resize` event that the test waits for is not fired at its window while its view transition is animating, so the test times out before checking that the transition is skipped (the `-before-ready` variant, which resizes before the transition is ready, passes)

css/cssom-view/elementFromPosition.html.description: the points on the right and bottom edges of the box are not in the box: the subtests fail in every browser

css/cssom-view/offsetTopLeft-inline-offs.description: expects `offsetLeft` relative to the border edge of an inline `offsetParent` that has a border; https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view-1/#dom-htmlelement-offsetleft subtracts the padding edge of the first box of the `offsetParent`

css/cssom-view/range-bounding-client-rec.description: expects `Range.getBoundingClientRect()` to include the boxes of the children of the selected `display: contents` elements; CSSOM View (https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view-1/#dom-range-getclientrects) only includes the border areas of the selected elements whose parent is not selected (a `display: contents` element has none) and the font ascent and descent of the selected texts, so the range is as tall as the texts (47px), not as the 30px boxes (60px); Chrome and Safari fail it too

css/cssom-view/scrollParent-quirks-mode..description: the tests call `scrollParent()` as a method, while the library (like the CSSOM View IDL used by idlharness) defines `scrollParent` as an attribute

css/cssom-view/scrollParent-shadow-tree..description: the tests call `scrollParent()` as a method, while the library (like the CSSOM View IDL used by idlharness) defines `scrollParent` as an attribute

css/cssom-view/scrollParent.html.description: the tests call `scrollParent()` as a method, while the library (like the CSSOM View IDL used by idlharness) defines `scrollParent` as an attribute

css/cssom-view/subpixel-sizes-and-offset.description: the remaining subtests (fractional `scrollTop`) fail in every browser

css/cssom-view/window-scroll-promise-int.description: the scroll promises resolve with a result object (`interrupted`) proposed in w3c/csswg-drafts#12495; the specification (and the library) resolve them with `undefined`

css/cssom-view/window-scroll-promises.ht.description: the scroll promises resolve with a result object (`interrupted`) proposed in w3c/csswg-drafts#12495; the specification (and the library) resolve them with `undefined`

css/cssom/flex-serialization.html.description: `flex: 0` is expected to serialize as `flex: 0 1 0px`, while every browser serializes it as `flex: 0 1 0%` (the omitted `flex-basis` is `0%`)

css/mediaqueries/display-mode.tentative..description: the `unframed` value of the `display-mode` media feature

css/selectors/parsing/parse-has-slotted..description: the functional `:has-slotted(<compound-selector>)` form (tentative); only the argument-less `:has-slotted` is parsed

custom-elements/element-internals-aria-e.description: the tentative ARIA element reflection of `ElementInternals` returning the elements of the custom element's own shadow tree and of another shadow tree of the document

custom-elements/parser/parser-sets-attri.description: the `document.anchors` subtest of the empty `name`: the test expects the parser to move the first `<a is=named-anchor>` out of `#anchor-container`, where its constructor inserted it, but HTML's "insert an element at the adjusted insertion location" returns without inserting an element whose parent is non-null, so it stays before the second anchor (also appended to `#anchor-container` by its constructor), and `document.anchors` is `[parser-anchor, empty]` in tree order

custom-elements/registries/CustomElement.description: the subtests that read `clone.elementInternals.shadowRoot`: DOM's "clone a single node" creates the copy of `<some-host>` with the synchronous custom elements flag unset, so it is `undefined` (its upgrade is only enqueued) when "clone a node" attaches its shadow root, and "attach a shadow root" only sets "available to element internals" for a `precustomized` or `custom` element: `ElementInternals.shadowRoot` is null, and `upgrade(null)` throws a TypeError

density-size-correction/density-correcte.description: WebGL (`getContext("webgl")` returns null): the 2 subtests of the 2D context pass (the source rectangle of `drawImage()` is in the density-corrected pixels), the 3 WebGL subtests fail

document-policy/experimental-features/ne.description: the tentative `network-efficiency-guardrails` configuration point of Document Policy (a report for each text resource that is not compressed), which only Chromium implemented behind a flag

document-policy/required-policy/separate.description: uses the `lossless-images-max-bpp` and `font-display-late-swap` (`no-font-display-late-swap`, the former syntax of a disabled boolean) configuration points, which no browser supports anymore (Chromium removed them): they are ignored, so no required policy is sent; `required-document-policy.html` says that no configuration point with a numeric value is defined anymore

dom/events/relatedTarget.window.js.description: 3 subtests contradict the dispatch algorithm of the DOM Standard: a target that is its retargeted `relatedTarget` is not dispatched to (so `target` stays null), and `target`/`relatedTarget` are only cleared when the last shadow-adjusted target or its `relatedTarget` is in a shadow tree (they fail in Chrome and Safari, Firefox passes 1)

dom/events/scrolling/scrollend-event-fir.description: the last subtest relies on the zoom of `pinchZoomIn()`, which its helper says the tests should not do: the library zooms by the ratio of the distances of the fingers (2x, without touch slop), so the visual viewport has room for the 200px pan and the window does not scroll (no `scrollend` event at the window); the smaller zoom of Chromium leaves less room

dom/lists/DOMTokenList-coverage-for-attr.description: `relList` on the MathML `<a>` element: the `MathMLAnchorElement` interface of MathML Core (https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#the-a-element) only has `href`, `target` and the members of `HyperlinkElementUtils`; reflecting `rel`, `relList`, `ping` and `referrerPolicy` is only proposed (w3c/mathml-core#325)

dom/nodes/Document-createEvent.https.htm.description: the `TouchEvent` aliases: as the desktop browsers, the library does not expose the legacy touch event APIs, so the subtests report a failed precondition

dom/nodes/ParentNode-querySelector-escap.description: the test predates the restriction of the non-ASCII ident code points of CSS Syntax (U+00A0 and U+2003 are not ident code points, so `#` followed by one of them is not a valid selector); the browsers still accept them

dom/nodes/insertion-removing-steps/Node-.description: `<meta http-equiv=default-style>` selects the alternate style sheet set once the style sheet is loaded, but the test reads the style right after the `link` element is parsed: the alternate style sheet of the `data:` URL is fetched asynchronously (it does not block the scripts, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#contributes-a-script-blocking-style-sheet), so it is not in `document.styleSheets` yet; the test relies on the synchronous loading of `data:` style sheets of Chromium (Firefox and Safari fail it too)

3 subtests expect the style sheet of a `<link rel=stylesheet>` with a `data:` URL to be created synchronously by its insertion steps (as in Chrome), while the HTML Standard creates it when the fetch completes (they fail in Firefox and Safari)

dom/nodes/moveBefore/selection-preserve..description: 5 of 6 subtests: the test selects with a drag of the pointer and, as its own comment says, relies on an internal of Chromium: `getSelection()` is recomputed from the visible selection after `moveBefore()`, so it expects the boundary points to have moved to the closest text that did not move (`notMove.firstChild`). The library keeps the live range of the selection, which the DOM specification updates when a node is moved: its boundary points are in the old parent (`<div id=old_parent>`).

dom/nodes/processing-instruction-attribu.description: the 24 subtests of the `xml-parser` source parse `<?t data?>` with `DOMParser` as `application/xml`: a document without a root element is not well-formed (https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#NT-document), so `parseFromString()` returns a document whose only child is a `parsererror` element (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#dom-domparser-parsefromstring: "Assert: document has no child nodes"), and its first child is not the processing instruction (only Chromium keeps the nodes parsed before the error)

dom/ranges/Range-cloneContents-around-sh.description: the tentative test contradicts the Selection API, whose `getRangeAt()` throws an `IndexSizeError` when the focus is not in the document tree (a selection whose range ends in a shadow tree), as in Safari

dom/ranges/Range-deleteContents-around-s.description: the tentative test contradicts the Selection API, whose `getRangeAt()` throws an `IndexSizeError` when the focus is not in the document tree (a selection whose range ends in a shadow tree), as in Safari

dom/ranges/Range-extractContents-around-.description: the tentative test contradicts the Selection API, whose `getRangeAt()` throws an `IndexSizeError` when the focus is not in the document tree (a selection whose range ends in a shadow tree), as in Safari

domparsing/XMLSerializer-serializeToStri.description: 3 subtests contradict the DOM Parsing specification, which keeps the prefix of an attribute when the local prefixes map does not contain it (instead of generating `ns1`), and ignores a default namespace declaration (`xmlns=""`) equal to the inherited namespace

domparsing/innerhtml-05.xhtml.description: outdated test: the `data:` URL iframe has an opaque origin, so reading `window[0].document` throws (as in the browsers)

domparsing/stream-html-reentrancy.html.description: 6 subtests: the upgrade of a customized built-in `template` element by the backup element queue (at a microtask checkpoint) when it is streamed: the streaming parser runs the custom element constructors synchronously when it creates the elements, so the constructor runs before the declarative shadow root is attached or before the content of `<template for>` is patched (the proposal creates the elements of a fragment parser without running their constructor, whatwg/html#12758)

domparsing/stream-insertion-logic.html.description: 4 subtests (one per method with a reference child): a `script` element streamed into a `replaceWithChildrenElements` element that is foster-parented before a table, which the script moves out of the target: the script ends up after the nodes inserted before the reference child instead of before them (the location of the replaced element is not kept when its table is moved)

editing/edit-context/*.description: the EditContext API (`EditContext`, `TextFormat`, `HTMLElement.editContext`, the `textupdate`/`textformatupdate`/`characterboundsupdate` events): `EditContext is not defined`; these tentative tests only pass in Chrome

editing/event.html.description: 5 of the 8 failing subtests fail in every browser: the test expects an `input` event for commands that do nothing because their value is invalid (`createLink`, `fontSize` and `formatBlock` with an empty value, `fontSize` with `quasit`), and `Changing selection from handler` expects the event at the second editing host although nothing changes the selection; per the specification no event is fired when the action of the command returns false

`fontSize` with the value `15px` is expected to fire `input`: the browsers parse the value with the legacy font size rules (the leading digits, `15`), but the specification returns false for a value that is not a valid floating-point number, and editing/data/fontsize.js (editing/run/fontsize.html) expects `2em`, `20pt` and `1.` to do nothing and return false, which the library passes; accepting the value here would fail these subtests

2 of the 8 failing subtests, that only Chrome passes: `formatBlock` with `quasit` and `insertImage` with an empty value are expected to fire `input`, but their actions return false (formatBlock: "If value is not a formattable block name, return false"; insertImage: "If value is the empty string, return false"), and execCommand() fires no `input` event when the action returns false; Firefox and Safari fire none either

editing/other/copy-elements-with-css-var.description: the `text/html` data written by the copy action is the plain serialization of the selection, without the computed styles inlined: the `<span>` and the table styled through custom properties are pasted as elements without a `style` attribute (`span.style.getPropertyValue("font-size")` is the empty string, expected `18px`; `color: rgb(0, 0, 255)`, `padding: 12px`...). Only Chrome passes.

editing/other/copy-paste-before-non-edit.description: the copy and the paste work (`Select` is inserted before `something` in the Text node and no child node is lost), but the expected markup hard-codes the `style` attribute of the untouched non-editable span as Blink re-serializes it (`style="border: 1px solid gray;"`, with a trailing semicolon) while the source attribute is `style="border: 1px solid gray"`, which the library leaves as is. Firefox and Safari fail the same assertion.

editing/other/editable-state-and-focus-i.description: 4 of 29 subtests, that Chrome and Firefox pass (Safari fails): the Select All shortcut with the focus in a shadow tree of a document in design mode. The test reads `getSelection().getRangeAt(0)`, but as the Selection API specifies, the selection of the document does not expose a range in a shadow tree (`rangeCount` is 0; `getComposedRanges()` does), and the selectAll command selects the children of the body ("call selectAllChildren(target)" with the body element), so the range is `(<body>, 0) - (<body>, 11)` where the test expects the children of the shadow root or of its editing host

editing/other/editing-style-of-range-aro.description: 2 of 8 subtests: `bold` on a range from a text node appended to `` to the middle of the following text is expected to remove the style of the `` (`bar`), an expectation "based on Chromium" for an edge case according to the test itself. The library, as the specification, only makes the non-bold selected text bold and keeps the attribute (`bar`); Firefox fails the same subtests.

editing/other/empty-elements-insertion.h.description: 1 of 5 subtests, that fails in Chrome, Firefox and Safari: a click on an empty `<strong>` without border, padding nor generated content is expected to put the caret in it, so that `insertText` inserts in the element. The element has no width, so the hit test gives the position of the paragraph (as in every browser) and the text is inserted next to the empty element

editing/other/end-key-with-wbr.html.description:
the 2 failing subtests pass only in Chrome: in `
12
` the End key is expected to move the caret from `(div, 0)` to the last position of the host `(div, 8)`, and Home from `(div, 8)` to `(div, 0)`; the library stops at the edges of the content of the line, before the trailing `` elements (`(div, 6)`) and after the leading ones (`(div, 2)`), positions that are rendered at the same place. No specification defines the boundary point of a line boundary movement (`Selection.modify()` is not specified); Firefox and Safari fail too

editing/other/exec-command-with-text-edi.description: 30 of the 68 failures (10 per variant): the test expects `styleWithCSS` and `defaultParagraphSeparator` to be disabled (and to return false, their state staying unchanged) while an `<input>` or a `<textarea>` that is not in editable content is focused; only Firefox does that, the library sets the state of the document whatever is focused, as Chrome and Safari do and as the specification says (the miscellaneous commands are always enabled). 6 more expect `queryCommandValue("defaultParagraphSeparator")` to be `p` after the command although the test also expects the command to fail (they fail in every browser).

12 failures: `queryCommandEnabled("undo")` and `queryCommandEnabled("redo")` are expected to be true before the test has edited the value (the value was just set by a script, which clears the undo history of the control, as the test itself says). `undo` passes in Chrome and Safari only, which always enable it in a text control; `redo` fails in every browser. The undo and the redo themselves work (the value, the selection and the `historyUndo`/`historyRedo` input events pass).

20 failures of the `password` variant: the test expects `cut` and `copy` to be enabled and to cut or copy the selected text of an `<input type=password>`, and the following `paste` to insert the text that was copied. No browser copies the text of a password field (the subtests on the value and on the `deleteByCut` event fail in the three browsers); the library does not enable the commands there.

editing/other/exec-command-without-edita.description: the 20 failures: in a document without editable element the test expects `execCommand("styleWithCSS")` and `execCommand("defaultParagraphSeparator")` to return false and to leave the state of the document unchanged; only Firefox does that. The library sets the state, as Chrome and Safari do and as the specification says (the miscellaneous commands are always enabled); 2 of them (`queryCommandValue("styleWithCSS")` expected to be the string `true`) fail in every browser.

As Chrome and Safari, the library inserts the text at the end of the text that precedes an inline void element, after the empty inline elements and the collapsed white space between them, or before the void element when no text precedes it. 3 subtests fail in every browser: `{in }` is expected to give the text before the empty span (`abc`, the library gives `abc`), and with a space between the empty span and an `` or a `` the text is expected before the space (`abcdef `), where the library inserts it after the space, which is rendered (a white space node is only collapsed before a block or a br): `abc def`. 2 pass only in Chrome: `{in or }`, expected `abc`. 1 passes only in Firefox: `abc\n{in

3 of 14 subtests, that only Firefox passes: with the caret set by script in a ``). These elements are not single-line containers, so insertParagraph goes up to the enclosing `

editing/other/mathml-html-serializtion-o.description: the copied `<math>` tree is pasted as MathML elements, with the white space Text nodes that the source has between its elements (`<math ...>\n    <mrow>\n      <mi>x</mi>...`); the test expects the `innerHTML` of the pasted `<math>` without any white space (`<mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo>...`), which is the serialization of the copy of Chrome (only Chrome passes the test).

editing/other/merge-span-with-style-afte.description: the two headings are joined and the style of the moved span is preserved, but the expected markup requires the moved `` to lose its `id` attribute, an artifact of Blink and WebKit that rebuild the element from its style. The library moves the node itself, as the specification and Firefox do, and gets `...space`.

Enter then Backspace in `Back[]space` gives the expected structure, but the expected markup requires the `style` attribute of the second span to be re-serialized by the style engine (`background-color: red;` with a space) as Blink and WebKit do; the library clones the attribute of the split span verbatim (`style="background-color:red;"`), as the specification and Firefox do.

editing/other/paste-clipboard-change.ten.description: the test expects a paste to be aborted (nothing is pasted) when a listener of its `paste` or `beforeinput` event writes other content to the clipboard; only Chrome does that. The library has no such check and the text of the clipboard is pasted: in the `<input>` of the `id=text` variant (`Original text` in the first subtest, `New text` in the second one) and in the editing host of the `id=contenteditable` variant (`New text`, then `Original text`).

editing/other/paste-in-list-with-inline-.description: the `text/html` data written by the copy action is the serialization of the selected range, without the formatting of its ancestors: selecting the text of `copy this` copies `copy this`, which is pasted in the list item as text, where the test expects `copy this` (the computed style that Chrome inlines in the copied HTML; only Chrome passes).

editing/other/paste_text_with_text_trans.description: the test asserts at load that `window.testRunner`, the internal test API of WebKit and Blink, is defined ("This test requires testRunner to read/write clipboard") and uses the non-standard `pasteAndMatchStyle` command: the harness errors before any subtest, as in Chrome, Firefox and Safari on wpt.fyi.

editing/other/selectall-in-editinghost.h.description: 1 of 4 subtests: when the editing host is focused but the selection has no range, `selectAll` is expected to select only the content of the focused editing host; the library selects the content of the body, text before the host included, which is what the specification says for `selectAll`. Chrome and Safari fail this subtest too (only Firefox passes).

editing/other/shadow_root_iteration_in_b.description: `removeFormat` with the selection inside the nested editing host `world` is expected to clear the `style` attribute of that span (`style=""`), which only Chrome does. The span is the editing host of the selection, hence not editable, and the specification never modifies it: the library keeps `style="color:red"`, as its reference implementation, Firefox and Safari do.

element-timing/idlharness.window.js.description: the test does not load the IDL of `paint-timing` (a dependency), so `PaintTimingMixin` is undefined for idlharness (`idl_test setup` fails the same way in Chrome, Firefox and Safari on wpt.fyi; `paintTime` and `presentationTime` are implemented, see `paint-timing/idlharness.window.js`)

event-timing/TapToStopFling.html.description: there is no fling: a touch pan scrolls instantly and ends when the touch is released, so the second tap stops nothing and is an interaction (its `pointerdown` has an `interactionId`, the test expects 0; the first `pointerdown`, canceled by the pan, has 0). Chrome fails the same assertion on wpt.fyi

event-timing/event-click-visibilitychang.description: the pending event timing entries are not dispatched when the document becomes hidden (the specification only dispatches them in the rendering updates; the browsers end the duration of the events when the page is hidden): the duration of `pointerup` ends at the rendering update that follows, after `minimize()` has resolved, so `startTime + duration` is later than the time the test reads after the visibility change (the runner hides the window in about 1 ms, less than the 8 ms granularity of the duration)

event-timing/modal-dialog-interrupt-pain.description: `alert()` returns at once (no modal dialog is shown), so the duration of the `click` entry ends at the rendering update that follows the listener instead of when the dialog is shown (`startTime + duration` is after `processingEnd`); this end point is not in the specification, and the test is an ERROR (unexpected alert) in Chrome, Firefox and Safari on wpt.fyi

event-timing/selection-autoscroll.html.description: the autoscroll of a selection that the pointer drags past the edge of a scroll container: no `scroll` event is fired, which the test waits for (it also times out in Chrome and Firefox on wpt.fyi)

event-timing/target-selector.tentative.h.description: the tentative path format of `targetSelector` (e.g. `BODY > DIV:nth-child(1)`), which `querySelectorAll()` must accept: the algorithm of the specification gives `IMG[src=/images/green.png]` for an image without id, whose attribute value is not quoted (an invalid selector); the 4 other subtests pass (no browser implements `targetSelector` on wpt.fyi)

fetch/api/abort/serviceworker-intercepte.description: the iframe of the test navigates to the scope of `sw-intercept-abort.js`, whose fetch event of the navigation request waits for the abort of its signal: the iframe never loads, so `with_iframe()` never resolves and the test times out (as in the browsers on wpt.fyi, 10 of 12 subtests with a TIMEOUT). The signal of the request of the fetch event is aborted with the serialized abort reason of the fetch

fetch/api/policies/referrer-origin-when-.description: the service worker (an `https:` context) fetches `HTTP_REMOTE_ORIGIN`, an `http:` URL: the request is blocked as mixed content (https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-mixed-content/#should-block-fetch), so `fetch()` rejects

fetch/api/redirect/redirect-origin.any.j.description: the test expects no `Origin` header for a same-origin POST redirected (307/308) to the same origin: the method stays POST, and "append a request `Origin` header" (https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#append-a-request-origin-header, step 4) appends the serialized origin to a request whose method is neither GET nor HEAD unless the referrer policy prevents it (the default `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` does not for a same-origin request); `fetch/origin/assorted.window.js` expects this header for a same-origin POST

fetch/api/request/destination/*.description: `<link rel=preload as=json>`: `json` is a potential destination (`link.as` reflects it) but not a preload destination of the specification (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#preload-destination), so nothing is fetched and no event is fired: `fetch-destination.https.html` times out there, before its next subtests (the browsers preload it)
the external resource of the SVG `use` element is not fetched (`fetch-destination-no-load-event.https.html` times out there)

fetch/api/request/request-bad-port.any.j.description: the proxy of the WPT server is not emulated (the request fails)

fetch/api/request/request-consume-empty..description: the FormData subtest ("Consume empty FormData request body as text") expects an empty `FormData` to be serialized as an empty body, which the test itself marks as unclear (FIXME, web-platform-tests/wpt#3950). The multipart/form-data encoding (RFC 7578) writes the close delimiter `--boundary--` even without entries, which `fetch/api/response/response-form-data.html` ("Empty form data") and the round trips of `fetch/api/body/formdata.any.js` require: the two expectations cannot both be met

fetch/api/response/response-consume-empt.description: the FormData subtest ("Consume empty FormData response body as text") expects an empty `FormData` to be serialized as an empty body, which the test itself marks as unclear (FIXME, web-platform-tests/wpt#3950). fetch/api/response/response-consume.html.description: `from FormData to blob` and `from URLSearchParams to blob` expect the type of the blob to be the `Content-Type` of the body as is (lowercased by the test): the type of the blob of `blob()` is the serialized MIME type of the `Content-Type` of the body (https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-body-package-data), which is `multipart/form-data;boundary=…` (without the space) and `application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8` (https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-bodyinit-extract); the browsers pass them because they keep the header and lowercase the type, and fail the subtests of `fetch/content-type/response.window.js` and `mimesniff/mime-types/parsing.any.js` that expect the case of the parameters to be kept

fetch/compression-dictionary/dictionary-.description: the `compression-dictionary` request destination of the `<link rel=compression-dictionary>` requests (https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/pull/1854): the library fetches them with the empty destination, so a dictionary whose `match-dest` is `("compression-dictionary")` does not match them

fetch/compression-dictionary/fetch-desti.description: the `compression-dictionary` request destination of the `<link rel=compression-dictionary>` requests (https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/pull/1854): the library fetches them with the empty destination

fetch/content-encoding/zstd/big-window-z.description: the WPT loader decodes the `zstd` content coding of the served files without limiting the window size, so the body whose window is larger than 8 MiB (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9659#section-3) is not rejected

forced-colors-mode/forced-colors-mode-40.description: the non-standard `-webkit-tap-highlight-color` property and the `-webkit-text-emphasis-color` alias of `text-emphasis-color` (`computedStyleMap().get()` throws for an unknown property); the computed values of the 15 other properties are not forced, as expected

html-aam/accname-computation-by-element/.description: the `from title` and `to be empty` subtests: `html-aam-accname-utils.js` sets `alt="Mapped image alt attribute value"` on every tested `<area>` (its special context), so the `alt` of the area itself is its name (HTML-AAM uses `alt` before `title`)
