html/browsers/browsing-the-web/back-forw.description: the `unload` subtest: as in Chromium (desktop) and Firefox, a document with an `unload` event listener is not kept in the back/forward cache (the specification lets the user agent decide, and lists `unload-listener` as a user-agent specific blocking reason), so the BFCache executor reports a failed precondition

html/browsers/browsing-the-web/history-t.description: the navigation of the opener's `location` during the load of the popup is a replace (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#navigate, the history handling of a navigation before the load event), so `history.back()` cannot reload the first document; the test only passes when the first document of the popup is restored from the back/forward cache, which does not keep the documents of a popup that its opener can script (as in Chromium)

the navigable target name saved in the document state of a session history entry is not restored on traversal (fails in every browser): the browsers keep the target name of the navigable on traversals, which `browsing_context_name.html` expects (a same-origin traversal keeps the name set by the later document), while the HTML Standard restores the name of the document state of the entry
the step log stringifies the cross-origin `contentWindow.location`, which throws a SecurityError (as in browsers); restoring the target name on traversal is not implemented either
the step log stringifies the cross-origin `contentWindow.location`, which throws a SecurityError (as in browsers); restoring the target name on traversal is not implemented either

the `location.reload()` subtest: as in Chrome and Firefox, a reload is initiated by the document it reloads, not by the initiator origin and the referrer stored in the document state (`Sec-Fetch-Site` is same-origin); the SameSite cookie tests expect it (`cookies/samesite/*-reload.https.html` send the SameSite=Strict cookies)
scroll restoration (scripted scrolling and scrolling to a fragment have no effect, scroll positions are 0)

the popup is opened with an opener, and the HTML Standard keeps the navigable target name of an auxiliary browsing context whose opener browsing context is non-null when it navigates to another origin (finalize a cross-document navigation, step 4): `window.name` is still `test`; the message handler never calls `done()` either (fails in every browser)

html/browsers/browsing-the-web/navigatin.description: `href.html` does not exist next to the test (only `resources/href.html`), and the onclick's `document.write()` posts "write" first, so the test cannot pass

`window.stop()` after the parsing, while a style sheet still delays the load event, is expected to fire no `load` event and to set `readyState` to `complete` (only Chrome does it; the HTML Standard fires the load event once the fetches are canceled)

the test expects the URL of the new document in the `unload` event of the previous document of the iframe (`iframe.contentWindow` is the old window then): the previous document is unloaded before the new entry is activated (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#deactivate-a-document-for-a-cross-document-navigation); the test reproduces a Servo crash, and Chrome, Firefox and Safari fail it

the first subtest compares the message of the `SecurityError` thrown by the cross-origin `location.href` getter with the text of Blink (`Failed to read a named property 'href' from 'Location': Blocked a frame with origin ... from accessing a cross-origin frame.`), which no specification defines; the library throws a `SecurityError` with another message, the assertion fails in the `message` handler, so the subtest times out and the next ones are not run
plugin documents (a PDF loaded in an iframe creates an accessible Document; `contentWindow.document` must throw)

the test expects a popup navigated to a `data:` URL (directly or through a redirect) to be closed; the HTML Standard navigates it, and the browsers that block the top-level `data:` navigations keep the popup open on its initial `about:blank` document (fails in every browser)

html/browsers/browsing-the-web/overlappi.description: the test expects the new navigation of the iframe (`frames[0].location.href = ...`) not to delay the load event of the parent, so that the window `load` event fires before the iframe `load` event: in the navigate algorithm, every navigation of a child navigable sets its "is delaying `load` events" (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#navigate), so the parent's load event waits for the new navigation, after the load event of the iframe; Chrome and Firefox fail too

the test expects the new navigation of the grandchild not to delay the load events of its parent and grandparent: in the navigate algorithm, every navigation of a child navigable sets its "is delaying `load` events" (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#navigate), so the grandchild `load` event fires first, then the ones of its ancestors; Chrome and Firefox fail too
the test waits until the hash is `#1` after the traversal, then asserts that it is `#2`

html/browsers/browsing-the-web/scroll-to.description: scrolling to the fragment (scroll positions are always 0)

html/browsers/browsing-the-web/unloading.description: expects the `pagehide` and `unload` handlers of the parent document to run before the ones of its iframe; the spec unloads the child navigables first (fails in Chrome and Safari too)
expects the `pagehide` and `unload` handlers of the parent document to run before the ones of its iframe; the spec unloads the child navigables first
`document.open()` in a `click` handler is expected to unload the document and its iframe (fails in Chrome, Firefox and Safari)

the test expects the parent document to be unloaded (its `pagehide` and `unload` events, `34`) before the `pagehide` event of its iframe (`5`): the child navigables are unloaded first (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#unload-a-document-and-its-descendants), and the `parent.document.open()` call of the iframe's handler then removes the iframe (its `parent` becomes null); only Firefox passes
the test closes its own top-level window (`window.close()`) and completes in its `unload` handler; no result is collected once the test window is destroyed

html/browsers/history/the-history-interf.description: `history.forward()` in the `load` handler of the page loaded again by `history.go(-1)` traverses forward to the next page (pages [3,2,3], as in every browser); the test expects [3,2,2]
the test expects the obsolete behavior where `document.open()` adds a session history entry (history.length 2); the spec now replaces the entry
`start_test_wait()`, which completes the test, is never called (it times out in every browser)
`start_test_wait()`, which completes the test, is never called (it times out in every browser)

html/browsers/history/the-location-inter.description: the [[Prototype]] cycles through a Location object (its [[GetPrototypeOf]] is not the ordinary one, so OrdinarySetPrototypeOf allows them): the engine only stops the cycle check at a Proxy, as its ordinary [[Get]] would loop forever on a cycle through a host object (3 subtests of 4); Chrome and Safari also reject these cycles
the iframe navigates to `resources/resources/iframe_location_replace2.html`, which does not exist; the test also counts `pageshow` events across a traversal (back/forward cache)
the test expects the obsolete reload override (reloading the content written by `document.write()` in the load handler); the specification and every browser fetch the URL of the document again
expects a push for a `location.assign()` during load without user activation (a scripted click); the spec (and the replace-before-load tests) require a replace

html/browsers/origin/cross-origin-object.description: `window.scroll()`, `scrollTo()` and `scrollBy()` return a promise (CSSOM View), so calling them with a cross-origin this value rejects the promise with the SecurityError instead of throwing it, as the test expects from the browsers that do not return a promise yet; the rejection is not handled (a harness error) (3 subtests of 102)

html/browsers/sandboxing/window-open-bla.description: the executor window is sandboxed by its `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts allow-popups allow-same-origin allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox` header: its sandboxed navigation browsing context flag is set, so it is not allowed by sandboxing to navigate the popup that the test window opened (it is neither an ancestor, the opener nor the one permitted sandboxed navigator of the popup, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#allowed-to-navigate); its `window.open("about:blank", name)` throws a SecurityError and the popup never fires the `load` event that the test waits for (a regression test of Chrome; Firefox and Safari time out too)

html/browsers/the-window-object/accessin.description: the `object` and `embed` elements of the test are in a `display: none` subtree: they are not being rendered, so they have no content navigable and `window.length` is 1, not 3 (2 subtests of 3; they fail in Chrome and Safari too, Firefox fails one)

the `object` element of the test is in a `display: none` subtree: it is not being rendered, so it has no content navigable (`contentWindow` is null) and `window[0]` is the window of the `iframe` (fails in every browser)

html/browsers/the-window-object/named-ac.description: as in the browsers, a cross-origin caller gets the child navigable named `frame1` from the WindowProxy of its parent (`window.parent.frame1`) even when the document of that child is cross-origin with the parent; the HTML Standard only exposes the names of the document-tree child navigable target name property set (the children that are same origin with the window) and throws a SecurityError for the others. Other web-platform-tests rely on the behavior of the browsers (`web-animations/timing-model/timelines/sibling-iframe-timeline.html`, `document_domain_access_details.sub.html`). 2 subtests of 3: Firefox and Safari fail them too, Chrome fails the first one

html/browsers/the-window-object/security.description: `window.onmousewheel`, a non-standard event handler attribute of Blink and WebKit that no specification defines (1 subtest of 124; Firefox fails it too)

html/browsers/the-window-object/window-o.description: the test expects `noopener` and `noreferrer` to always open a tab, as Chrome and Safari do; the HTML Standard removes `noopener` and `noreferrer` from the tokenized features, then checks if a popup window is requested with the remaining ones (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#window-open-steps), so e.g. `resizable=yes,scrollbars=yes,status=yes,noopener` is a popup (26 subtests of 51; Firefox fails the same ones)

html/browsers/the-window-object/window-r.description: the test is outdated, as it says (https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/3267#issuecomment-2788132131): it expects the `load` event of an iframe without `src` (or with `src=""` or `about:blank`) not to be fired while the iframe is inserted (6 subtests of 7; fails in every browser)

`window.open("about:blank", name)` keeps the initial `about:blank` document of the new popup (the window open steps only run the URL and history update steps for an `about:blank` URL), so the first navigation away from it reuses its Window object as specified; the tentative test expects the Window not to be reused, as in the browsers (1 subtest of 2)

html/browsers/the-window-object/open-clo.description: the tentative `split` window feature of `window.open()` (https://github.com/mfreed7/split-tabs): `split` does not disable the legacy "any other feature means popup" heuristic, so the window is a popup and its `BarProp`s are not visible

html/browsers/windows/consume-user-activ.description: as in the browsers, the source document of `window.open()` called from a promise job (after an `await`) is the document of the window of the method, not the associated document of the entry global object, so the user activation of the entry global object is not consumed. the tentative rule that the `touchend` of a touch that scrolled does not trigger the activation: `touchend` is always an activation triggering input event, as in the HTML Standard (`navigator.userActivation.isActive` is true after the scroll gesture)

html/webappapis/dynamic-markup-insertion.description: the HTML Standard does not ignore `document.write()` on a document that is no longer active (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#document-write-steps checks only the unload and ignore-destructive-writes counters before the implicit `document.open()`), and `opening-the-input-stream/active.window.js` expects the implicit `document.open()` to replace the children of a document that was navigated away from; fails the same way in Chrome, Firefox and Safari

html/webappapis/scripting/processing-mod.description: the Window agent's [[CanBlock]] is not false, so `Atomics.wait()` does not throw a `TypeError` on the main thread

input-events/input-events-range-exceptio.description: the tentative validation of `targetRanges` by the `InputEvent` constructor (an `IndexSizeError` for a `StaticRange` whose offsets are greater than the length of its nodes), and the tentative clamping of the ranges when the event is dispatched

intersection-observer/v2/delay-test.html.description: the frames of the virtual clock are exactly 1/60 s apart: the time between two notifications is exactly the delay (100ms), the test expects more

intersection-observer/v2/svg-text-filter.description: the second subtest expects a `filter` on a `tspan` element to occlude the target, but the filter property does not apply to the text content child elements (https://drafts.fxtf.org/filter-effects/#FilterProperty applies to the container elements, the graphics elements and `use`): the library does not paint it, so nothing covers the target and the subtest waits for a notification that never comes (the filter on the `text` element occludes)

is-input-pending/tentative/*.description: the test driver dispatches the input of `test_driver.Actions` from timers of the event loop, and the runner does not report these pending actions to `isInputPending()` (`BrowsingContextOptions.PendingInput` is not set, so it returns false); the security tests, which expect false, pass

jpegxl/hdr-pq-intensity-target.html.description: 1 of 2 subtests: the `intensity_target` of a PQ image as the peak of its tone mapping: Meziantou.Framework.Imaging reads it but does not report it, so the PQ images without content light level are tone mapped from the peak of PQ (10,000 cd/m2), and the image that states a peak of 600 cd/m2 is not brighter than the one that states 10,000 cd/m2

js/builtins/weakrefs/*.description: `FinalizationRegistry.prototype.cleanupSome`: a TC39 proposal that is not part of ECMA-262 (Chromium, Firefox and Safari fail these tests too)

largest-contentful-paint/animated/observ.description: the first frame of an animated image is not painted before the whole image is received (the image is available once it is completely loaded), so `renderTime` is after the 2 s delay of the second frame; the same assertion fails in Chrome, Firefox and Safari on wpt.fyi

the frames of a video are not candidates of the largest contentful paint (only Chromium reports them)

largest-contentful-paint/video-data-uri..description: the frames of a video are not candidates of the largest contentful paint (only Chromium reports them)

largest-contentful-paint/web-font-styled.description: the paints are only computed once a script observes or reads the paint timing entries: the test observes them (`buffered`) after the web font is loaded, so the text painted with the fallback font is not reported and there is 1 entry instead of 2; the same assertion fails in Chrome, Firefox and Safari on wpt.fyi

long-animation-frame/conditional-*.description: the conditional user timing of the long animation frames (`performance.markConditional()`, `performance.measureConditional()` and `userTimingEntries`), a Chromium experiment that the specification does not define

long-animation-frame/loaf-congested-mome.description: the long animation frames of the dedicated workers (the congested moments), a Chromium experiment (`LongAnimationFrameWorker`) that the specification does not define

long-animation-frame/loaf-first-ui-event.description: `test_driver.send_keys()` dispatches the key events synchronously, while the script that calls it runs: the `keydown` listener runs in the script entry point of that script (https://w3c.github.io/long-animation-frames/#create-script-entry-point records nothing while a script is pending), so no `INPUT.onkeydown` script is reported; a browser dispatches them from the task of the user interaction

long-animation-frame/loaf-forced-layout-.description: the subtest `forcedLayoutDuration and forcedStyleAndLayoutDuration are strictly positive after heavy forced layout work`: the library does not measure the time it spends on the styles and the layout: `styleDuration`, `layoutDuration` and the `forced*Duration` of the scripts are 0 (with the virtual clock of the runner, which only advances when it is read, they would be 0 anyway)

long-animation-frame/loaf-forced-style-d.description: the subtest `forcedStyleDuration and forcedStyleAndLayoutDuration are strictly positive after heavy forced style work`: the library does not measure the time it spends on the styles and the layout: `styleDuration`, `layoutDuration` and the `forced*Duration` of the scripts are 0 (with the virtual clock of the runner, which only advances when it is read, they would be 0 anyway)

long-animation-frame/loaf-layout-duratio.description: the subtest `Heavy render-phase layout produces strictly positive layoutDuration`: the library does not measure the time it spends on the styles and the layout: `styleDuration`, `layoutDuration` and the `forced*Duration` of the scripts are 0 (with the virtual clock of the runner, which only advances when it is read, they would be 0 anyway)

long-animation-frame/loaf-paint-mixin.ht.description: the library has no presentation time: the `presentationTime` of the frames is null (https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#dom-painttimingmixin-presentationtime), and the test expects it after `paintTime`

long-animation-frame/loaf-pause-duration.description: a synchronous request of a window blocks the thread that advances the virtual clock: the runner answers `delay.py?ms=180` without delay, so the synchronous `XMLHttpRequest` does not pause the script (`pauseDuration` is 0) and the script does not last 360 ms

long-animation-frame/loaf-script-block.h.description: the subtest of the module imported by `import()`: the engine evaluates the imported module in a reaction of the promise of the import, without a host hook, so its evaluation is reported in the `resolve-promise` script of the import (`import.then`), not as a `module-script`

long-animation-frame/loaf-script-count.t.description: `scriptCount`, a Chromium experiment (`LongAnimationFrameWorker`) that the specification does not define

long-animation-frame/loaf-stream-source-.description: the promises of the platform have no creation-time attribution (optional, https://w3c.github.io/long-animation-frames/#webidl-monkey-patches): the reactions of the promises of the streams are reported as `Promise.then`, without source location, not as `StreamPromise.resolve.then`

long-animation-frame/loaf-style-duration.description: the subtest `Heavy render-phase style recalculation produces strictly positive styleDuration`: the library does not measure the time it spends on the styles and the layout: `styleDuration`, `layoutDuration` and the `forced*Duration` of the scripts are 0 (with the virtual clock of the runner, which only advances when it is read, they would be 0 anyway)

long-animation-frame/performance-bind.te.description: `performance.bind()` (the `user-entry-point` scripts), a Chromium experiment that the specification does not define

longtask-timing/containerTypes.html.description: `observe({ entryTypes: ['longtask'], buffered: false })`: the `buffered` member cannot be used with `entryTypes`, so `observe()` throws a `TypeError` (https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#observe-method, step 4); Chromium ignores it

longtask-timing/longtask-sync-xhr.html.description: a synchronous request of a window blocks the thread that advances the virtual clock: the runner answers it without delay, so the `XMLHttpRequest` of `delay-css.py?delay=100` does not last 50 ms

magnetometer/Magnetometer-iframe-access..description: the `UncalibratedMagnetometer` subtests create the `magnetometer` virtual sensor instead of `uncalibrated-magnetometer` (https://w3c.github.io/magnetometer/#uncalibrated-magnetometer-automation): the sensors fail to start with a `NotReadableError`

magnetometer/Magnetometer.https.html.description: the `UncalibratedMagnetometer` subtests create the `magnetometer` virtual sensor instead of `uncalibrated-magnetometer` (https://w3c.github.io/magnetometer/#uncalibrated-magnetometer-automation), so `start()` fails with a `NotReadableError`, and `get_sensor_reading_properties()` of the helpers does not know `UncalibratedMagnetometer`

mathml/presentation-markup/operators/ope.description: `support/operator-dictionary.json` gives the infix `/` an lspace and an rspace of 4/18em; the operator dictionary of MathML Core puts it in the category K (0)

mathml/presentation-markup/operators/siz.description: the result depends on the default math font: with the bundled STIX Two Math, the inner fences around `x + y` (the descender of `y`, stretched symmetrically around the math axis) need a size variant, the ones around `x` do not

mathml/presentation-markup/operators/str.description: the result depends on the default math font: the display size variant of U+2AFC in the bundled STIX Two Math is taller but not wider than its base glyph

mathml/presentation-markup/scripts/under.description: tentative: the overscripts are accents because of the `accent` property of the operator dictionary of MathML 3; MathML Core only uses the `accent`/`accentunder` attributes

mathml/relations/css-styling/display-2.h.description: the math layout of an `mrow` whose children are `display: inline-block` boxes in a multi-column container: the browsers lay them out as the `div` of the reference (they wrap in the columns)

mathml/relations/css-styling/lengths-vi-.description: the test expects the `vi`/`vb` of the `width` attribute of an `mspace` to follow the writing mode of the root element (`vertical-rl`), but they resolve against the writing mode of the element itself (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-4/#viewport-relative-lengths, WPT `css/css-values/viewport-units-writing-mode.html`: "The writing-mode of the document element does not matter"), which MathML Core forces to `horizontal-tb` on every MathML element (https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#user-agent-stylesheet, WPT `mathml/relations/css-styling/writing-mode/force-horizontal-tb.html`): `vi` is the width and `vb` the height of the viewport in both cases

mathml/relations/html5-tree/a-ping.html.description: the `ping` IDL attribute of `MathMLAnchorElement`, which is not in its interface in MathML Core (https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#the-a-element, proposed in w3c/mathml-core#325); the pings of the `ping` content attribute are sent

mathml/relations/html5-tree/a-rel-getter.description: the `rel`/`relList` IDL attributes of `MathMLAnchorElement`, which are not in its interface in MathML Core (https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#the-a-element, proposed in w3c/mathml-core#325)

mathml/relations/html5-tree/a-referrerpo.description: the `referrerPolicy` IDL attribute of `MathMLAnchorElement`, which is not in its interface in MathML Core (https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#the-a-element, proposed in w3c/mathml-core#325)

measure-memory/detached.https.window.js.description: the test waits for the messages of the same-origin popups opened by the cross-site and cross-origin frames (`same-origin-11`, `same-origin-13`), whose `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` response switches them to another browsing context group, which removes their opener (as `window-open.mix.https.window.js`): the test times out
the realms of the detached frames and of the replaced documents that the scripts keep alive: the measurement only lists the documents of the navigables of the browsing context group

measure-memory/main-frame-and-worker.htt.description: the measurement of the JavaScript heap: the sizes are a deterministic estimate of the objects of the library (a base size per realm, the nodes and the text of the documents), so the 10 MB `Uint8Array` that the worker allocates is not counted, and `bytes` is below the 10 MB the test expects

measure-memory/window-open.mix.https.win.description: the test waits for the messages of the same-origin popups opened by the cross-origin frames (`same-origin-5`, `same-origin-7`): the initial `about:blank` document of a popup created by a frame whose origin is not the origin of its top-level document has the `unsafe-none` opener policy, so the `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` response of the popup switches it to another browsing context group (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsers.html#check-browsing-context-group-switch-coop-value), which removes its opener: its messages never reach the frame that opened it, and the test times out

media-capabilities/decodingInfo-webrtc.a.description: WebRTC: the script calls `RTCRtpReceiver.getCapabilities()` at the top level in a window, which throws a ReferenceError after the subtests are defined (harness ERROR)
the codecs of the test runner (`WptMediaCodecBackend`) have no VP9 decoder, so `video/VP9` is not supported (in the worker)

media-capabilities/decodingInfoEncrypted.description: 2 subtests expect the `cbcs` and `cbcs-1-9` encryption schemes with WebM content (`video/webm; codecs="vp09.00.10.08"`, `audio/webm; codecs="opus"`): the WebM encryption is AES-CTR only (https://www.webmproject.org/docs/webm-encryption/), so Clear Key supports the `cbcs` schemes for MP4 only

media-capabilities/encodingInfo-webrtc.a.description: WebRTC: the script calls `RTCRtpSender.getCapabilities()` at the top level in a window, which throws a ReferenceError after the subtests are defined (harness ERROR)

media-source/SourceBuffer-abort*.description: the `video/mp4` subtest requires `MediaSource.isTypeSupported('video/mp4')` (a type without codecs) to be true, while `mediasource-is-type-supported.html` requires it to be false for `video/webm`: as in Chromium (which fails these subtests too), a type that allows the `codecs` parameter is only supported with its codecs

media-source/mediasource-append-buffer.h.description: `Test appendBuffer events order.` expects the `loadeddata` event before the `updateend` event of the append of the media segment: as in the browsers (Chromium, Firefox and Safari fail the same assertion), the ready state of the media element rises asynchronously, after the events of the append

media-source/mediasource-correct-frames*.description: the tests draw the frames of the video on a canvas and read the color of their pixels to identify the frame that is played: the media backend of the tests decodes nothing (its frames are black)

media-source/mediasource-preload.html.description: the two `preload=none` subtests with a `blob:` URL that references no media source (revoked or corrupted) expect an `error` event: the URL is then fetched as any resource, and `preload=none` defers the fetch as specified, so no event is fired (Firefox and Safari time out too; Chromium resolves the URL at once)

media-source/mse-for-webcodecs/*.description: WebCodecs (`SourceBuffer.appendEncodedChunks()`, `addSourceBuffer()` with a decoder configuration, `EncodedVideoChunk`): the tentative MSE for WebCodecs extension

mediacapture-fromelement/src-reset.html.description: the tracks of the stream captured from the element are not removed (no `removetrack`) when its source is reset after the playback of an audio file: the test times out

mediacapture-insertable-streams/VideoTra.description: WebRTC (`RTCPeerConnection`): the subtests that send the track over a peer connection fail

mediacapture-insertable-streams/idlharne.description: the object of `MediaStreamTrackProcessor` is `new MediaStreamTrackProcessor({ track: new VideoTrackGenerator() })`, whose `track` is the generator instead of its track: the conversion of the `MediaStreamTrackOrHandle` union throws a TypeError (https://w3c.github.io/mediacapture-transform/#dom-mediastreamtrackprocessorinit-track), so the subtests of the object fail

mediacapture-insertable-streams/legacy/M.description: the legacy `MediaStreamTrackGenerator` of Chromium is exposed in the windows and the dedicated workers only, as `MediaStreamTrack` (https://w3c.github.io/mediacapture-extensions/): the service workers have no `MediaStreamTrackGenerator`

the legacy `MediaStreamTrackGenerator` of Chromium is exposed in the windows and the dedicated workers only, as `MediaStreamTrack` (https://w3c.github.io/mediacapture-extensions/): the shared workers have no `MediaStreamTrackGenerator`
WebRTC (`RTCPeerConnection`): the subtests that send the track over a peer connection fail

the virtual clock of the runner advances at each read of the clock, so the 40 ms interval that writes the frames drifts behind the 120 ms timeout of the sink of `pipeTo()`: the read that follows the timeout gets the third frame, written before it, instead of the fourth one

mediacapture-insertable-streams/tentativ.description: WebRTC (`RTCPeerConnection`): the subtests that send the track over a peer connection fail

mediacapture-streams/BrowserCaptureMedia.description: Region Capture and Element Capture (`BrowserCaptureMediaStreamTrack`: `cropTo()`, `restrictTo()`, `RestrictionTarget`): the capture backend captures no tab of the library, so the capture of the current tab cannot be cropped

mediacapture-streams/MediaDevices-enumer.description: the identifiers of the devices are not rotated when the storage of the origin is cleared (`Clear-Site-Data`): they are hashes of the identifiers of the backend and of the origins

after a camera capture, the test expects the identifiers of the microphones to stay hidden although the `microphone` permission is granted: the 'set the device information exposure' steps extend the exposure to the microphones when their permission is granted ('device exposure can be extended')

mediacapture-streams/MediaStreamTrack-if.description: the test posts the track to the frame without a transfer list (`iframe.contentWindow.postMessage(track)`): `MediaStreamTrack` is transferable, not serializable (https://w3c.github.io/mediacapture-extensions/), so `postMessage()` throws a `DataCloneError` (in the `load` listener of the audio test, which then times out)

mediacapture-streams/MediaStreamTrack-tr.description: the test calls `getDisplayMedia()` without a user activation (it does not call `test_driver.bless()`), so the promise is rejected with an `InvalidStateError` (https://w3c.github.io/mediacapture-screen-share/#dom-mediadevices-getdisplaymedia)

mediasession/media-session-artwork-fetch.description: the images of the artwork of the media session are not fetched (the host gets their URLs, `MediaSessionOptions.SessionChanged`), so the service worker sees no request

mimesniff/mime-types/parsing.any.js.description: the `(Blob/File)` subtests expect the type of a `Blob` and of a `File` to be the parsed and serialized MIME type, as proposed by w3c/FileAPI#43; the File API Standard converts the type to ASCII lowercase, and makes it empty when it contains a character outside U+0020-U+007E (Chromium, Firefox and Safari fail them too). 2 `(Request/Response)` subtests (`x/x;,=x;bonus=x`, `x/x;x=,;bonus=x`) expect the whole header value to be parsed: extracting a MIME type (https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-extract-mime-type) splits the `Content-Type` at the commas, which gives `x/x` (the browsers fail them too)

navigation-api/navigate-event/defer/tent.description: `NavigateEvent.deferPageSwap()` (tentative): the handler and the restore callback are not called, so the events of the page restored from the back/forward cache are only `pageshow` and `dispose`

navigation-api/navigate-event/intercept-.description: the first subtest expects the focus reset of `intercept()` not to move the focus into a cross-origin iframe whose `focus-without-user-activation` policy is denied: "potentially reset the focus" runs the focusing steps without the allow focus steps (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#potentially-reset-the-focus); the subtest fails in Chrome and Firefox (the second subtest passes)

navigation-api/navigate-event/intercepte.description: the test expects an intercepted same-document navigation to survive a cross-document navigation of its traversable (started by a cross-origin iframe, so no navigate event fires at the document): the navigate algorithm sets the ongoing navigation, which informs the navigation API about aborting navigation (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#set-the-ongoing-navigation), so the ongoing navigate event is aborted and `navigation.navigate()` rejects with an `AbortError` before the page enters the back/forward cache; Firefox and Safari fail it too

navigation-api/navigation-methods/forwar.description: expects the promises of a `forward()` whose target entry is removed by a push started before the traversal is applied to reject with an AbortError (as Chromium and WebKit do); "performing a navigation API traversal" (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#performing-a-navigation-api-traversal) rejects them with an InvalidStateError when no session history entry has the key, which is what the library does; Firefox fails the same way (`InvalidStateError`)

navigation-api/navigation-methods/reload.description: the test runs over HTTP: `navigator.serviceWorker` is only exposed in the secure contexts; it fails in Chrome, Firefox and Safari with the same TypeError (`navigator.serviceWorker` is undefined)

navigation-api/ordering-and-transition/c.description: expects `popstate` to be fired before the `finished` promise of an intercepted `navigation.back()` is fulfilled; "update the navigation API entries for a same-document navigation" cleans up after running script (a microtask checkpoint, which fulfills `finished` for an `intercept()` without handler) after it fired `currententrychange`, and "update document for history step application" fires `popstate` afterwards: the code after `await back_result.finished` runs between the two events; the test fails in Chrome and Firefox

navigation-api/per-entry-events/dispose-.description: the maximum number of session history entries (tentative, not specified: 50 in Chromium, the only browser that passes): the oldest entry is never removed, so its `dispose` event is not fired

navigation-timing/response-start-after-c.description: the test expects a `redirectCount` of 0 for a popup navigated through two redirects of the origin of its opener that have `Timing-Allow-Origin: *`, to a document of another origin whose opener policy switches the browsing context group; the redirect count of a navigation is exposed when the navigation TAO check passes (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#initialise-the-document-object: "If navigationParams's response's redirect taint is same-origin, or [...] navigation TAO check given navigationParams's response and navigationParams's origin returns success, then set redirectCount to navigationParams's request's redirect count"), which it does since every redirect allows `*` (https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#navigation-tao-check), and the browsing context group switch does not change it: the library reports 2. Upstream, the counterpart `response-start-after-coop-bcg-switch-no-tao.tentative.https.html` says that this test exposes the redirect data because the chain opts into TAO. The other assertions pass

the time origin of a document reached through cross-origin redirects that fail the navigation TAO check, after a browsing context group switch, is the start of the navigation: the tentative test expects it not to include the redirects (`responseStart` includes the 2 s of `slow-redirect.py`; the redirect data is hidden as expected)

notifications/icon-fetch.tentative.https.description: the fetch steps of the notifications: the library does not display the notifications, so it does not fetch their icon, image and badge (the host fetches them if it displays them)

notifications/instance.https.window.js.description: the window subtests construct a `Notification` with `actions`, which the constructor rejects with a `TypeError` (only the persistent notifications have actions); the `notificationclose` subtests of the service worker wait for a `notificationclose` event after `close()`, which the specification only fires when the user closes a persistent notification (the test notes that it times out in Blink and Gecko)

performance-timeline/back-forward-cache-.description: the `back-forward-cache-restoration` entry type (`BackForwardCacheRestoration`): no entry is queued when a document is restored from the back/forward cache

performance-timeline/buffered-flag-with-.description: the tentative `buffered` option with `entryTypes`: `observe()` throws a `TypeError` when `entryTypes` is used with another member, as specified

performance-timeline/navigation-id-reset.description: the test does not wait for the reload: `location.reload()` navigates from a task, so the `waitForPageShow` and the mark of the next scripts still run in the document restored from the back/forward cache, and the second navigation id is the one of that document (the restoration does regenerate it, which the first assertion checks)

performance-timeline/not-restored-reason.description: `PerformanceNavigationTiming.notRestoredReasons` (the `NotRestoredReasons` interfaces), and `RTCPeerConnection`, which most tests use to make a page ineligible for the back/forward cache

permissions-policy/experimental-features.description: the test reads the policy with the legacy `document.featurePolicy` (only `document.permissionsPolicy` is specified, and `permissions-policy/historical.html` checks that `featurePolicy` is not exposed); fails in every browser

the test expects the default allowlist `*` for `focus-without-user-activation` (a cross-origin iframe is allowed); HTML defines `'self'` (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/infrastructure.html#policy-controlled-features); fails in every browser

the test expects the focused-frame heuristics of an experimental implementation of Chromium (a frame that has the focus, or an ancestor of the focused frame, may move the focus although its `focus-without-user-activation` policy is denied, and the policy of the document that calls `focus()` is checked instead of the one of the target); the allow focus steps of HTML only check the policy and the transient activation of the document of the target (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#allow-focus-steps). The stable browsers do not enforce the policy at all: the subtests that expect a focus to be blocked fail in them

the test reads the policy with the legacy `document.featurePolicy` (only `document.permissionsPolicy` is specified, and `permissions-policy/historical.html` checks that `featurePolicy` is not exposed); fails in every browser

the test expects the focused-frame heuristics of an experimental implementation of Chromium (a frame that has the focus, or an ancestor of the focused frame, may move the focus although its `focus-without-user-activation` policy is denied, and the policy of the document that calls `focus()` is checked instead of the one of the target); the allow focus steps of HTML only check the policy and the transient activation of the document of the target (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#allow-focus-steps). The stable browsers do not enforce the policy at all: the subtests that expect a focus to be blocked fail in them
`test_driver.click()` on an `iframe` element does not give a transient activation to the window of the iframe, so the sanity check of the first subtest fails (the second subtest passes)
Private State Tokens (the `privateToken` member of `RequestInit`): only the policy of the `private-state-token-redemption` feature is computed
the `vertical-scroll` feature (an experimental policy of Chromium without specification): `scrollIntoView()` in the iframe scrolls the main frame; fails in every browser

permissions-policy/payment-extension-all.description: the subtest without the `allow="payment"` attribute: a cross-origin iframe without `allow="payment"` may use neither `publickey-credentials-create` nor `payment` (the alternative create permissions policy of `public-key`, https://w3c.github.io/secure-payment-confirmation/#sctn-permissions-policy), so `create()` rejects with a `NotAllowedError` (https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#algorithm-create, step 9.3: "If document is not allowed to use permission, return a promise rejected with a NotAllowedError"); the test expects the `NotSupportedError` of Chromium

permissions-policy/reporting/midi-report.description: the test expects `requestMIDIAccess()` to reject with a `SecurityError` (Chromium) in a document that is not allowed to use the `midi` feature; the specification rejects with a `NotAllowedError` (https://webaudio.github.io/web-midi-api/#dom-navigator-requestmidiaccess, steps 4 and 11), and the violation report is generated

permissions-policy/permissions-policy-he.description: the test expects `getAllowlistForFeature()` to return the declared origins although the feature is not allowed for the origin of the document (the header does not list `self`); the method returns an empty list in that case (https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-permissions-policy/#dom-permissionspolicy-getallowlistforfeature, step 4); the other subtests pass

permissions-policy/permissions-policy-op.description: the `'src'` keyword of the `allow` attribute of a sandboxed iframe matches every opaque origin, as in Chromium (where the test fails too): the document that the iframe navigates to still gets the feature, although it is not the document of the `src` attribute

permissions-policy/private-state-token-i.description: Private State Tokens (the `privateToken` member of `RequestInit`): only the policy of the `private-state-token-issuance` feature is computed

permissions-policy/reporting/geolocation.description: the test expects a position but does not grant the `geolocation` permission (`test_driver.set_permission()`): the report is checked, then `getCurrentPosition()` fails with `PERMISSION_DENIED`

permissions-policy/reporting/payment-rep.description: the test rethrows the rejection of `show()` after checking the report, so it passes only when the user accepts a payment with `https://example.com/pay`, a payment method that the user agent does not support (`NotSupportedError`, https://w3c.github.io/payment-request/#show-method); Chromium fails it too

permissions-policy/shared-worker-permiss.description: the `allow` member of `SharedWorkerOptions` (a tentative proposal to delegate permissions policy features to a shared worker): the option is ignored, so a shared worker is created even when the creator cannot delegate the features

the `allow` member of `SharedWorkerOptions` (a tentative proposal to delegate permissions policy features to a shared worker): the option is ignored, so connecting to an existing shared worker with a different `allow` value succeeds instead of firing `error`

pointerevents/bugs/events_after_lostpoin.description: the expected log (`lostpointercapture@target0, pointerup@button, pointerup@button`) is produced by no browser (Chrome, Firefox and Safari fail the test): the library logs `lostpointercapture@target0` twice, then `pointerup@button`

pointerevents/coalesced_events_attribute.description: the moves of a pointer are never coalesced: each move injected in the input devices fires its own `pointermove`, whose coalesced events list has one event, even while the main thread is busy (optional test; Chrome, Firefox and Safari fail it too)

pointerevents/compat/pointerevent_mouse-.description: a press of the mouse on an `<object>` element does not capture the mouse: once the pointer is dragged out of the element, its `pointermove` and `pointerup` events are fired at the element under the pointer, and the test expects them at the `<object>` (only Blink passes)

pointerevents/pointerevent_after_target_.description: the touch subtests contradict the Pointer Events specification and the touch sequences of the test itself: the implicit pointer capture of a touch pointer (https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#implicit-pointer-capture) fires `pointerup` at the `pointerdown` target, not at the child appended under the touch; the expected `pointerenter` events of the second touch are fired from the child to the parent (they are fired from the outermost ancestor); and the subtests at `pointerup` and of the moved child expect the sequences of a pointer that hovers (no `pointerout`/`pointerleave` after `pointerup`, no `pointerenter` at the parent for the next touch). Chrome, Firefox and Safari each fail some of these subtests

the expected lists of the tentative test contain `click` events, but the test only logs the events whose type starts with the tested prefix (`mouse`): Chrome, Firefox and Safari fail every subtest too

the `remove-filler` subtests expect the events after the removal of the slotted element at the `<slot>` (`pointerover@slot`, `pointerup@slot`, ...) without the same events at the shadow host: an event dispatched at a node of the shadow tree is at the target phase at the host too (DOM retargeting), so the listener of the host logs it as for the other subtests (`pointerover@parent`, `pointerover@host`). Chrome and Firefox fail these subtests too

the expected lists of the tentative test contain `click` events, but the test only logs the events whose type starts with the tested prefix (`mouse`): Chrome, Firefox and Safari fail every subtest too

pointerevents/pointerevent_contextmenu_i.description: the touch variant: the long press of a touch does not fire `contextmenu` (the test also times out in Chrome, Firefox and Safari)

pointerevents/pointerevent_multiple_poin.description: the two mouse input sources of the action sequence are the mouse of the user agent (one pointer, as in Chrome and Safari), so the boundary events of the layout change are fired once, not once per input source (only Firefox passes)

pointerevents/pointerevent_touch-action-.description: the in-view center point of the scrolled content is on the horizontal scrollbar of the scroll container (classic scrollbars), where a touch does not pan: `scrollLeft` stays 0, as in Chrome, Firefox and Safari, which fail the test the same way

pointerevents/pointermove_after_pointero.description: the tentative rule that `pointermove` is not fired when a listener of the preceding `pointerover` removed its target: the library fires it at the parent of the removed target

preload/onerror-event.html.description: expects the `as=video` and `as=audio` preloads to fire an `error` event: they are not preload destinations, so nothing is fetched (fails in every browser)

preload/onload-event.html.description: expects the `as=video` and `as=audio` preloads to fire a `load` event: they are not preload destinations, so nothing is fetched (fails in every browser)

preload/preload-resource-match.https.htm.description: the two font subtests that expect the preload to be discarded do not use the font (an empty paragraph), so the font face is not fetched and there is a single resource timing entry (also fails in Chromium and WebKit)

proximity/ProximitySensor-iframe-access..description: calls `run_generic_sensor_iframe_tests()` with the name of the sensor instead of the sensor data object that the current helpers expect, so `validate_sensor_data()` throws a `TypeError`

proximity/ProximitySensor.https.html.description: calls `runGenericSensorTests()` with the arguments of a former version of the helpers and an undefined `verifyProximitySensorReading` function: the page throws a `ReferenceError`

quirks/line-height-calculation.html.description: the image of a `data:` URL is not available synchronously: the height of the line of an image with borders or paddings is checked before the image has a natural size (the browsers decode it before)

quirks/percentage-height-calculation.htm.description: the nested body case (`<body><body><div id="test"/></body></body>` in XHTML) expects 200px, where the simple case `<body><div id="test"/></body>` expects 184px: the outer body is the document's body element in both cases (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#the-body-element-2) and the percentage height resolves against the height it gets from the body element fills the html element quirk (184px); every browser fails it (Firefox 184px like the library, Chrome and Safari 168px)

quirks/table-cell-width-calculation.html.description: the `data:` images of `object`, `embed` and the `poster` of `video` are not rendered with their natural size (they are rendered with the default object size)

quirks/unitless-length/excluded-properti.description: `column-span: 1234` is valid: `column-span` accepts an `<integer>` in CSS Multicol 2 (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-multicol-2/#column-span), the test expects it to be invalid

referrer-policy/generic/inheritance/popu.description: the assertion reads `document.referrer` of the test page (empty: the test page is loaded without a referrer), not the one of the popup opened by the form submission (`window_opened_from_form`), and expects the URL of the iframe

reporting/crashReport-test.html.description: the Crash Reporting API (`window.crashReport`, `CrashReportContext`, https://wicg.github.io/crash-reporting/), implemented by Chromium only

reporting/document-reporting-default-end.description: `deprecation` reports triggered by non-standard APIs: the tests call `webkitRequestAnimationFrame()` (the prefixed alias of Chromium and WebKit) or read `window.fullScreen` (a Gecko property) to make the browser report a deprecated feature; no specification (not even the Compatibility Standard) defines them, and the library only exposes the members that a specification defines (it reports the deprecated standard features it implements, e.g. a synchronous `XMLHttpRequest` in a window), so no report reaches the endpoint

reporting/document-reporting-destroy-aft.description: `deprecation` reports triggered by non-standard APIs: the tests call `webkitRequestAnimationFrame()` (the prefixed alias of Chromium and WebKit) or read `window.fullScreen` (a Gecko property) to make the browser report a deprecated feature; no specification (not even the Compatibility Standard) defines them, and the library only exposes the members that a specification defines (it reports the deprecated standard features it implements, e.g. a synchronous `XMLHttpRequest` in a window), so no report reaches the endpoint
