resource-timing/iframe-failed-commit.htm.description: the `csp` attribute of the iframes (CSP Embedded Enforcement): the two same-origin responses that do not comply with it are loaded, so their entries are not opaque; the other subtests pass

resource-timing/initiator-type/link.html.description: `<link rel="manifest">` is not fetched (the manifest is only fetched when the user agent needs it); the style sheets, the preloads, the module preloads, the prefetches and the icons pass

resource-timing/initiator-type/svg.html.description: the external resources of the SVG `use` elements are not fetched; the `image` subtest passes

resource-timing/render-blocking-status-l.description: a Chrome-only test (Firefox and Safari do not implement `renderBlockingStatus`) of the behavior of Chrome: `renderBlockingStatus` is `blocking` for the style sheets that are render-blocking when their fetch starts, but the test also expects `blocking` for a style sheet preloaded by a `link rel=preload` and used immediately by a render-blocking style sheet link (the entry is the one of the preload request, which is not render-blocking), for the style sheets imported by a render-blocking style sheet, and for a `blocking=render` link inserted once the body element exists, which the specification does not make render-blocking (the document does not allow adding render-blocking elements)

resource-timing/render-blocking-status-s.description: a Chrome-only test (Firefox and Safari do not implement `renderBlockingStatus`) of the behavior of Chrome: `renderBlockingStatus` is `blocking` for the scripts that are render-blocking when they are prepared, but the test also expects `blocking` for a `blocking=render` script inserted into the head by a script of the body (`script-head-blocking-render-dynamic-dom`): the body element exists, so the document does not allow adding render-blocking elements and, per the specification, the script is not render-blocking (the render-blocking of its request is only set when it is "currently render-blocking")

resource-timing/tentative/initiator-url/.description: 1 subtest: the task attribution of a module evaluated by `import()`: the JavaScript engine evaluates it, so the script element that it inserts is attributed to the classic script that called `import()` (the document) instead of the imported module; the modules run by a script element and the imports of a module are attributed to their module

1 subtest: the resource timing entries of the static imports of a module worker are added to the performance timeline of the worker instead of the timeline of the document that created it (the client of the fetches of a module worker script graph is the settings object of the document), so the observer of the document never sees the entry

sanitizer-api/sethtml-xml-document.html.description: `createElement("div")` in an `application/xml` document creates a null-namespace element, on which `attachShadow()` throws `NotSupportedError` as specified

screen-capture/delegate-request.https.su.description: the capability delegation of `display-capture` (`postMessage()` with `delegate`): a subframe without user activation cannot call `getDisplayMedia()`

screen-orientation/fullscreen-interactio.description: the second subtest expects the lock request of an iframe to be rejected with a `SecurityError` when the page exits fullscreen (the error of Chromium, whose lock requires fullscreen): exiting fullscreen runs the fully unlock the screen orientation steps (https://w3c.github.io/screen-orientation/#interaction-with-fullscreen-api), which reject the pending lock requests of the documents of the tab with an `AbortError`

screen-orientation/hidden_document.html.description: the cleanup of the third subtest calls `screen.orientation.unlock()` while the document is still hidden (the cleanup that restores the window is asynchronous and runs concurrently): the common safety checks throw a `SecurityError` for a hidden document (https://w3c.github.io/screen-orientation/#dfn-common-safety-checks), so the harness reports an error and the last subtest does not run

screen-wake-lock/wakelock-screen-type-on.description: `WakeLock` is only exposed to the windows (`Exposed=Window`): `navigator.wakeLock` is undefined in a dedicated worker, so the test throws a `TypeError` instead of rejecting with a `NotAllowedError`

scroll-animations/css/scroll-timeline-mu.description: the stale timelines created by the resize observers (after the first style and layout update of the frame) are not updated by an additional style and layout pass (whatwg/html#11613)

scroll-animations/css/scroll-timeline-on.description: the named scroll progress timelines declared by pseudo-elements (a pseudo-element has no scrolling box)

scroll-animations/css/scroll-timeline-wi.description: the percentage delays of the effects (`delay: CSS.percent()`), a proposal of Web Animations 2

scroll-animations/css/view-timeline-anim.description: the last step expects a `fill: none` animation to apply its effect when its view progress timeline is at 100% (the end of the cover range, `scrollTop` 200 of 250): the scroller is not at its maximum scroll offset, so the active-after boundary is not "at timeline boundary" (https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#at-timeline-boundary: the minimum and maximum timeline times are the ones of the minimum and maximum scroll offsets) and it is exclusive, as `view-timelines/block-view-timeline-current-time.tentative.html` and `range-boundary.tentative.html` expect ("Effect is in the after phase at effect end time"); Chromium fails it too

scroll-animations/css/view-timeline-pseu.description: the `::before` pseudo-element is at the start of the horizontal scroller, so the end of its cover range (100%) is the minimum scroll offset: at `scrollLeft` 0, the local time of the `fill: none` animation is its active-after boundary, which is exclusive when playing forwards because the end of the range is not aligned with the maximum scroll offset (https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#at-timeline-boundary, `range-boundary.tentative.html` expects no effect when the end of the range is at the minimum offset), so the background stays red; Chromium fails it too

scroll-animations/css/view-timeline-with.description: the percentage delays of the effects (`delay: CSS.percent()`), a proposal of Web Animations 2

scroll-animations/view-timelines/view-ti.description: the test passes strings ("auto") in the `inset` sequence, whose type is `sequence<(CSSNumericValue or CSSKeywordValue)>`

scroll-animations/view-timelines/zero-in.description: the percentage delays of the effects (`delay: CSS.percent()`), a proposal of Web Animations 2

scroll-to-text-fragment/scroll-to-text-f.description: 1 subtest (`text=Element,This`, a range that spans two blocks) expects the target element (`:target`) to be the element of the start of the range, as in Firefox; the specification makes it the first common ancestor of the start and the end of the range (here `body`), as in Chrome, where the subtest fails too (css/css-contain/content-visibility/content-visibility-048.html expects the common ancestor)

selection/caret/move-around-contentedita.description: an empty editable block (without line box) has no caret position: the caret moving out of an empty paragraph skips the position before the non-editable content that starts the next paragraph

selection/fire-selectionchange-event-on-.description: `execCommand("delete")` in a focused `<input>` of a shadow tree deletes the character and fires `selectionchange` at the input, as the Selection API specifies for a text control (the event bubbles and is composed to the document, retargeted to the shadow host). The test expects no event at the input and one event whose target is the document, which only Chrome does.

selection/script-and-style-elements.html.description: expects the line breaks of Gecko's serializer (a leading line break for a range starting before a block, two line breaks between the `<script>` block and the `<pre>`); the Selection API defines `toString()` as "the rendered text" without more details, and the library uses the rendered text of HTML (the `innerText` algorithm: no leading or trailing required line break, one line break between two blocks); Chrome and Safari fail it too

selection/selection-range-in-shadow-afte.description: the tentative test selects the text of a shadow tree and reads the range with `getRangeAt(0)` before it removes the host: the Selection API returns null from `anchorNode` and `focusNode`, 0 from `rangeCount` and throws an `IndexSizeError` from `getRangeAt()` when the anchor or the focus is not in the document tree (https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#dom-selection-rangecount), and `addRange()` ignores a range whose root is not the document

selection/shadow-dom/cross-shadow-bounda.description: the test expects `rangeCount` to be 1 after `extend()` moves the focus into a shadow tree: the Selection API returns null from `anchorNode` and `focusNode`, 0 from `rangeCount` and throws an `IndexSizeError` from `getRangeAt()` when the anchor or the focus is not in the document tree (https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#dom-selection-rangecount), and `addRange()` ignores a range whose root is not the document

selection/shadow-dom/selection-at-nodes-.description: 11 of 24 subtests: the test expects `containsNode()` to return false for a child of a shadow host that is not assigned to a slot, while the selection contains it in the node tree (https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#dom-selection-containsnode compares the boundary points of the range with the node, the flat tree is not involved), and reads `getRangeAt(0)` of a selection in a shadow tree (the slot fallback content): the Selection API returns 0 from `rangeCount` and throws an `IndexSizeError` from `getRangeAt()` when the anchor or the focus is not in the document tree (https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#dom-selection-rangecount)

selection/shadow-dom/tentative/Range-isP.description: 1 of 2 subtests: the tentative test reads `getRangeAt(0)` of a selection collapsed in a shadow tree (`setBaseAndExtent()` with the focus in the shadow tree, after the anchor): the Selection API returns null from `anchorNode` and `focusNode`, 0 from `rangeCount` and throws an `IndexSizeError` from `getRangeAt()` when the anchor or the focus is not in the document tree (https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#dom-selection-rangecount)

selection/shadow-dom/tentative/Selection.description: 16 of 21 subtests: the tentative test ("for investigation only", https://github.com/w3c/selection-api/issues/361) expects `anchorNode` and `focusNode` of a selection in a shadow tree to be rescoped to the parent of the shadow host, as `getComposedRanges()` does; the Selection API returns null from `anchorNode` and `focusNode`, 0 from `rangeCount` and throws an `IndexSizeError` from `getRangeAt()` when the anchor or the focus is not in the document tree (https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#dom-selection-rangecount); the test says that no browser passes it

1 of 31 subtests: the tentative test reads `getRangeAt(0)` of a selection whose focus is in a shadow tree: the Selection API returns null from `anchorNode` and `focusNode`, 0 from `rangeCount` and throws an `IndexSizeError` from `getRangeAt()` when the anchor or the focus is not in the document tree (https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#dom-selection-rangecount), and `addRange()` ignores a range whose root is not the document

the tentative test reads `getRangeAt(0)` of a selection whose focus is in a shadow tree: the Selection API returns null from `anchorNode` and `focusNode`, 0 from `rangeCount` and throws an `IndexSizeError` from `getRangeAt()` when the anchor or the focus is not in the document tree (https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#dom-selection-rangecount), and `addRange()` ignores a range whose root is not the document

6 of 9 subtests: the tentative test expects `anchorNode` and `focusNode` to return the nodes of a shadow tree after `addRange()` or a change of the live range of the selection: the Selection API returns null from `anchorNode` and `focusNode`, 0 from `rangeCount` and throws an `IndexSizeError` from `getRangeAt()` when the anchor or the focus is not in the document tree (https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#dom-selection-rangecount), and `addRange()` ignores a range whose root is not the document

2 of 4 subtests: the tentative test expects `anchorNode` and `focusNode` to return the nodes of a shadow tree: the Selection API returns null from `anchorNode` and `focusNode`, 0 from `rangeCount` and throws an `IndexSizeError` from `getRangeAt()` when the anchor or the focus is not in the document tree (https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#dom-selection-rangecount), and `addRange()` ignores a range whose root is not the document

selection/stringifier_editable_element.t.description: the tentative behavior of selection-api#83: `select()` does not focus the text control (the active element stays the previous control, so `toString()` does not return the selected text of the control), and a click does not move the selection (the last subtests do not run: the harness stops on the error of a click handler)

service-workers/cache-storage/cache-add..description: "Cache.addAll should succeed when an entry matches an earlier entry only under its own vary header": `vary.py` sets the `Vary` header from the cookie with `str()` of bytes (Python 3), i.e. `Vary: b'x-shape'`, a header that neither request has: the two requests match under the `Vary` of the first response, so `addAll()` rejects with an `InvalidStateError` (https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#batch-cache-operations)

service-workers/service-worker/about-bla.description: the document that replaces the initial about:blank document of an iframe or a popup reuses its Window, but its client has the id of the reserved client of the navigation (`FetchEvent.resultingClientId`) instead of the id of the environment of the initial document, which the window keeps (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#initialise-the-document-object). Keeping the id of the initial document breaks `clients.get(resultingClientId)` in clients-get-resultingClientId.https.html, clients-get.https.html and navigation-redirect.https.html, whose iframes navigate away from their initial about:blank document (Chrome and Safari fail the same three subtests of this test); the other subtests pass

service-workers/service-worker/claim-wor.description: the test expects `clients.claim()` to claim a worker created from a blob: URL; the creation URL of that worker is its blob: URL, which does not match the scope of the registration (https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#clients-claim), so the worker keeps the controller of its creator. Firefox fails the same three subtests

service-workers/service-worker/client-na.description: the `Frame location should not update on failed mixed-content navigation` subtest: a navigation of `WindowClient.navigate()` that is blocked as mixed content gets a network error, so the navigable loads an error document whose origin is opaque (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#populating-a-session-history-entry), and `navigate()` is rejected with a TypeError; the test expects the frame to keep its document, as the browsers cancel the navigation (unspecified): reading `location.href` of the error document throws a SecurityError. The other subtests pass

service-workers/service-worker/client-ur.description: the iframe posts a message to its parent while it is parsed (`client-url-creation-url-iframe.html`), and the test adds its message listener only after the `load` event of the iframe (`with_iframe()`): the HTML Standard queues the `DOMContentLoaded` and `load` events in tasks of the DOM manipulation task source at the end of the parsing (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#the-end), after the task of the message (posted message task source), and the order in which the event loop runs the tasks of different task sources is implementation-defined (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#event-loop-processing-model, step 2.1): the test relies on the browsers firing the events of a small document in the task that ends its parsing, so the message is lost and every subtest times out

service-workers/service-worker/clients-m.description: the windows are opened by `window.open()`, so they are auxiliary browsing contexts whose `frameType` is `auxiliary` (https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#dom-client-frametype), not `top-level`; their `lifecycleState` is correct (`frozen` for the window frozen by `test_driver.freeze()`)
the three subtests of the uncontrolled windows expect the window of the WPT harness (`/testharness_runner.html`) among the clients; the subtests of the controlled windows pass

service-workers/service-worker/controlle.description: the service worker calls `clients.get(event.resultingClientId)` while it handles the navigation, and only starts the timer that resolves its `respondWith()` once `get()` settles: the Service Workers specification waits for the client to be execution ready (https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#clients-get, step 2.1.2), i.e. for the document that the response creates, so the frame would never load (Chrome fails these subtests); the library resolves `get()` with undefined at once for a reserved client, and Firefox and Safari resolve it with the reserved client and queue its messages

service-workers/service-worker/fetch-can.description: the `range responses from single origin with both opaque and non-opaque responses` subtest expects a load error: the opaque (no-cors) first response and the CORS range responses that the service worker fetches from the same cross-origin URL are patched together, as verify a media response specifies for the responses of one origin whatever their CORS mode (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#verify-a-media-response, step 9), and the video taints the canvas; Edge (the only browser of wpt.fyi with results) fails this subtest too; the other subtests pass

service-workers/service-worker/fetch-eve.description: the subtest fetches an http: URL from an https: document and expects the service worker to answer it: the request is blocked as mixed content before the service workers are consulted (https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-main-fetch). Chrome, Firefox and Safari fail the subtest in the same way

the `Service Worker responds to fetch event with an existing client id` subtest expects `event.clientId` to be the empty string for the navigation request of an iframe; Create Fetch Event and Dispatch (https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#create-fetch-event-and-dispatch, step 8) initializes it to the id of the client of the request, which for a navigation is the environment of the document that starts it (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#create-navigation-params-by-fetching), as speculation-rules/prefetch/tentative/service-worker expects; Chrome, Firefox and Safari give the empty string; the other subtests pass

service-workers/service-worker/fetch-req.description: the bodies are not streamed: cancelling `event.request.body` does not cancel the body of the request

service-workers/service-worker/navigate-.description: the subtest of the uncontrolled windows expects the window of the WPT harness (`/testharness_runner.html`) and the test window as an auxiliary window among the clients; the subtest of the controlled windows passes

service-workers/service-worker/navigatio.description: `setHeaderValue()` normalizes the value before checking it (https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#dom-navigationpreloadmanager-setheadervalue): a leading carriage return is removed, the test expects a TypeError as in the browsers

service-workers/service-worker/next-hop-.description: `resources/empty.h2.js` is fetched from the origin of the test, the HTTP/1.1 server of port 8443: the `.h2.` of a resource name does not select the HTTP/2 server of wptserve (only the flags of the test file do), so `nextHopProtocol` is `http/1.1`, as the test comment anticipates (Edge passes only the H1 subtest on wpt.fyi)

service-workers/service-worker/resource-.description: the test expects the `decodedBodySize` and `encodedBodySize` of a CORS response without `Timing-Allow-Origin` to be 0: the body sizes are CORS-protected, not TAO-protected (https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/, `resource-timing/body-size-cross-origin.https.html`). The `Server-Timing` metrics of the response are not exposed, as the test expects

the test expects the connection times of an entry whose timing allow check fails to equal `fetchStart`; they are 0 (https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/). Chrome, Firefox and Safari fail the two subtests on `domainLookupStart`

service-workers/service-worker/tentative.description: the downloads (`<a download>`), and the service worker script of the test is not fetched
the downloads (`<a download>`), and the service worker script of the test is not fetched
the downloads (`<a download>`), and the service worker script of the test is not fetched
the downloads (`<a download>`), and the service worker script of the test is not fetched

service-workers/service-worker/unregiste.description: the fetch of the iframe (`frame.contentWindow.fetch()`) rejects with a `TypeError` of the realm of the iframe, as its relevant realm is the one of the iframe, while `promise_rejects_js(test, TypeError, ...)` expects an instance of the `TypeError` of the test page: "expected instance of function TypeError()". The fetch does fail: `Clear-Site-Data` clears the registration and terminates the worker whose `respondWith()` never settles

service-workers/service-worker/update-af.description: the test needs a registration whose last update check is older than 24 hours and cannot age it (it relies on a testing hook that the browsers do not expose): it times out in Chrome, Firefox and Safari too

service-workers/service-worker/update-re.description: the test expects that the iframe of a navigation that fails with a network error (the service worker rejects the request) fires no load event; the iframe fires it for the error document, as in Chrome and Firefox, which fail the test in the same way

service-workers/service-worker/windowcli.description: the subtest expects the frame type of a window opened with `window.open()` to be "top-level"; its browsing context is an auxiliary browsing context, whose frame type is "auxiliary" (https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#get-frame-type). Firefox fails the subtest in the same way; the other subtests pass

shadow-dom/MouseEvent-prototype-offsetX-.description: the test expects `offsetX`/`offsetY` of an event targeted at an inline box (`<span id=target>`) relative to the padding edge of its containing block (21, 17: the Blink and WebKit behavior); CSSOM View defines them relative to the padding edge of the target (https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#dom-mouseevent-offsetx), which gives 6 and 7, as in Firefox (wpt.fyi: Firefox fails both subtests with the same "expected 21 but got 6")

shadow-dom/declarative/tentative/shadowr.description: the `shadowrootadoptedstylesheets` attribute of `<template>` (declarative `adoptedStyleSheets` from CSS module specifiers)

shadow-dom/execcommand-insertList-in-sha.description: the editing commands on a selection in a shadow tree: the drag selects the list of the shadow tree (`getComposedRanges()` returns its range), but the selection has no range in the document tree (`rangeCount` is 0), so there is no active range: `execCommand("insertUnorderedList")` is not enabled and the list is not removed (passes in Chrome and Firefox)

shadow-dom/focus-navigation/menu/tentati.description: the `<menubar>`/`<menulist>`/`<menuitem>` elements (focus navigation skipping the other menu items)

shadow-dom/imperative-slot-api-cross-sha.description: the test expects a `slotchange` at a slot whose assigned nodes do not change: `slotB.assign(nodeN)` with a node that is not a child of the host of `slotB` ("slotB slotchange should fire because it gained its assigned node (even if not rendered)"); the DOM Standard only signals a slot change when the assigned nodes of the slot change (https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#assign-slotables), as Safari does (wpt.fyi: Safari fails this subtest with the same assertion, "expected 1 but got 0"; Chrome and Firefox fire the event). The `slotchange` at the previous slot of the node, in the other shadow tree, is fired

shadow-dom/leaktests/selection.html.description: the press puts the caret in the text of the closed shadow tree (`getComposedRanges()` returns it) and `getSelection().anchorNode` is null, as the Selection API specifies for an anchor that is not in the document tree; the test expects the parent of the shadow host, the node that Chrome and Safari rescope the selection to (it fails in Firefox too)

shadow-dom/untriaged/elements-and-dom-ob.description: tests `ShadowRoot.getSelection()` of the first Shadow DOM draft (not in the Selection API; implemented as an alias of the selection of the document) with a selection inside a shadow tree: `addRange()` ignores a range whose root is not the document (https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#dom-selection-addrange), so the selection stays empty. Only Chrome passes (wpt.fyi: Firefox and Safari fail with "s.getSelection is not a function")

shadow-dom/untriaged/user-interaction/ra.description: A_07_01_02_T01 tests `ShadowRoot.getSelection()` of the first Shadow DOM draft (not in the Selection API; implemented as an alias of the selection of the document) with a selection inside a shadow tree: `addRange()` ignores a range whose root is not the document (https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#dom-selection-addrange), so the selection stays empty. Only Chrome passes (wpt.fyi: Firefox and Safari fail both subtests with "s.getSelection is not a function")

shadow-dom/wheel-event-related-target.ht.description: the test expects `relatedTarget` of the `wheel` events to be the element under the pointer (retargeted to the shadow host); UI Events defines no related target for the wheel events, and the attribute is null in every browser (wpt.fyi: Chrome, Firefox and Safari fail with the same "relatedTarget before mouse is over shadow host expected Element node <div id=\"container\"> but got null")

shape-detection/*.description: Shape Detection API (`BarcodeDetector`, `FaceDetector`, `TextDetector`), which needs barcode, face and text detection backends; the detection tests also need the Chromium Mojo mocks of `/resources/chromium` (elsewhere, `/resources/test-only-api.js`, inserted again by each test, throws a SyntaxError on its second `const` declaration)

soft-navigation-heuristics/detection/ten.description: the text of the form controls (the value of an `<input type=button>`) is not a contentful paint of the paint timing (it is never a largest contentful paint candidate), and the changes of the value of a form control are not recorded as modifications of the interaction: changing it paints no interaction contentful paint (2 subtests)
the frames of a video are not candidates of the largest contentful paint (only Chromium reports them): the new video paints no interaction contentful paint

soft-navigation-heuristics/icp/tentative.description: the text of the form controls is not a contentful paint of the paint timing, and the changes of the value of a form control are not recorded as modifications of the interaction: typing in a `<textarea>` paints no interaction contentful paint

soft-navigation-heuristics/smoke/tentati.description: the frames of a video are not candidates of the largest contentful paint (only Chromium reports them): the test waits for the largest contentful paint of the video

speculation-rules/activation-header/*.description: the `on-prefetch-activation` response header of the tentative tests (a beacon sent when the prefetched or prerendered document is activated): a Chromium experiment that no specification defines

speculation-rules/inline-speculation-rul.description: the test expects an `error` event at the script element and a `TypeError` reported to the window for speculation rules that are not valid JSON (Chromium); the specification only reports the exception of the parsing, a `SyntaxError`, to the window ("register speculation rules"): nothing is fired at the element

speculation-rules/prefetch/clear-prefetc.description: the network partitioning of the `"prefetchCache"` type of `Clear-Site-Data` (tentative): `NavigationalPrefetch.ProcessClearSiteData` discards the prefetch records of every document of the origin of the response in the browsing context group, so the response of a cross-site iframe also discards the prefetch of the top-level document, and its navigation is not prefetched (`Sec-Purpose` is undefined)

speculation-rules/prefetch/tentative/coo.description: the `Cookie-Indices` response header (a prefetch is not discarded when the cookies it names changed since); the test also fails in Chromium
the redirect variants request `prefetch/tentative/resources/random_redirect.py`, which does not exist (the handler is in `prefetch/resources`)

speculation-rules/prefetch/user-pass.htt.description: the executor window is opened with credentials in its URL (`https://user:pass@…`), which the URL of the document keeps: `fetch()` of the dispatcher URL resolved against it throws a `TypeError` (a URL that includes credentials), so the executor never answers. The browsers do not expose the credentials in the URL of the document

speculation-rules/prerender-until-script.description: the `prerender_until_script` rule type of the tentative test (a Chromium experiment); the test also times out in Chromium

speculation-rules/prerender/activation-b.description: the `form_submission` key of the speculation rules (a Chromium extension): as specified, a rule with an unknown key is ignored, so nothing is prerendered

speculation-rules/prerender/cross-origin.description: the nested cross-origin iframes of a prerendered page whose responses opt in with `Supports-Loading-Mode: prerender-cross-origin-frames`: the test never gets the message of the innermost frame; it also times out in Chromium (`Supports-Loading-Mode: prerender-cross-origin-frames` is not specified)

speculation-rules/prerender/csp-form-act.description: the `form_submission` key of the speculation rules (a Chromium extension): as specified, a rule with an unknown key is ignored, so nothing is prerendered

speculation-rules/prerender/no-vary-sear.description: variant 17: the test calls its helper without the `noVarySearchHint` argument (the test says so: crbug.com/499027745), so `shouldUse` is undefined and the test expects the prerender to be discarded although the URLs are equivalent; it also fails in Chromium

variant 17: the test calls its helper without the `noVarySearchHint` argument (the test says so: crbug.com/499027745), so `shouldUse` is undefined and the test expects the prerender to be discarded although the URLs are equivalent; it also fails in Chromium

speculation-rules/prerender/protocol-han.description: the registration of the prerendering page is deferred until its activation, but the test sets the `registerProtocolHandler()` automation mode of the document of the test page only (`test_driver.set_rph_registration_mode()`); the automation mode is a state of each `Document` (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/system-state.html#registerprotocolhandler()-automation-mode), so the prerendered page asks the user, who does not accept it, and the modified handler is never registered (Chromium keeps the mode for the whole browser)

speculation-rules/prerender/restriction-.description: the API that the test expects to be restricted or delayed while prerendering: Background Fetch, Background Sync, Idle Detection, File System Access, Media Capture (`getUserMedia()`, `enumerateDevices()`, `getDisplayMedia()`), Notifications, Push, Web Speech, Web Share or WebXR

the lock request is deferred until the activation, then rejected with a `NotAllowedError`: the prerendered page is not fullscreen, which the library requires to lock the screen orientation (https://w3c.github.io/screen-orientation/#interaction-with-fullscreen-api); the test expects the lock to succeed, as in the test environment of Chromium, which does not require fullscreen

the non-standard `screen.availLeft` and `screen.availTop` (implemented by the browsers, not in CSSOM View): they are undefined, so the primary page moves its window to `NaN` and expects `screenX` to be `NaN`; `moveTo()` and `moveBy()` of a prerendering page are ignored

speculation-rules/prerender/restrictions.description: the test uses `RemoteContext` without including `/common/dispatcher/dispatcher.js` (a `ReferenceError`); it fails in every browser

speculation-rules/prerender/scroll-into-.description: `focus()` of an element of a cross-origin iframe of a prerendering page does not update `document.activeElement` of the iframe; the test also times out in Chromium

speculation-rules/prerender/workers.http.description: the resource timing entries of the scripts of the shared workers: the 2 shared worker subtests read the `startTime` of the entry of the worker URL, which is not reported (a shared worker may already run when a document connects to it); the dedicated worker subtest passes (the workers of a prerendering page start when it is activated)
the second subtest calls `t.text()` (the test object) on the response of `fetch()`: the promise rejects without handler, so the harness status is ERROR

speculation-rules/speculation-measuremen.description: `performance.speculations` (the tentative Speculation Measurement API of Chromium), and the early hints (`103` responses) of the `.h2` tests

storage-access-api/requestStorageAccess-.description: 1 subtest: expects a document to keep its storage access when its same-site parent navigates it to its own origin (Chromium); the specification only keeps the storage access of a navigation initiated by the active document of the navigable (the environment id of the source snapshot params, https://privacycg.github.io/storage-access/#navigation)

1 subtest: the control expects the WebSocket handshake of the frame to `wss://{{hosts[alt][]}}:{{ports[wss][0]}}` to send the unpartitioned cookie, but the port of the WebSocket server is not the port of the frame: the request is not same origin with the frame, so it is not eligible for storage access (https://privacycg.github.io/storage-access/#determine-the-initial-storage-access-eligibility)

2 subtests: the third-party context of a shared worker: the requests of a shared worker created by a cross-site frame are first-party for the cookies, so the cookie jar does not block its unpartitioned cookies

1 subtest: the control expects the WebSocket handshake of the frame to `wss://{{hosts[alt][]}}:{{ports[wss][0]}}` to send the unpartitioned cookie, but the port of the WebSocket server is not the port of the frame: the request is not same origin with the frame, so it is not eligible for storage access (https://privacycg.github.io/storage-access/#determine-the-initial-storage-access-eligibility)

1 subtest: expects the WebSocket handshake to `wss://{{hosts[alt][]}}:{{ports[wss][0]}}` to send the unpartitioned cookie of the frame that has storage access, but the port of the WebSocket server is not the port of the frame: the request is not same origin with the frame, so it is not eligible for storage access (https://privacycg.github.io/storage-access/#determine-the-initial-storage-access-eligibility)

storage-access-api/storage-access-beyond.description: the storage access of the dedicated workers: the blob URLs are partitioned by storage key, and a dedicated worker created by the third-party frame after its storage access was granted does not get it, so it cannot fetch the blob URL that `StorageAccessHandle.createObjectURL()` created in the first-party partition

the blob URLs of `StorageAccessHandle.createObjectURL()` as the script of a shared worker: the third-party frame cannot fetch the blob URL of the first-party partition, so `new SharedWorker()` fires an `error` event, and the test then waits for the message of a shared worker created by the handle, which is not relayed (the test times out)

the `sameSiteCookies` option of `SharedWorker` (https://privacycg.github.io/saa-non-cookie-storage/#shared-workers, an incubation that the HTML Standard does not have): the option is ignored, so `StorageAccessHandle.SharedWorker()` does not throw for `sameSiteCookies: 'all'` in a third-party context, the shared workers are not keyed by it, and the requests of a worker created with `none` send the SameSite cookies; the shared workers are also keyed by the top-level site only, so the partitioned worker of the frame (same site with the top-level document, embedded by a cross-site frame) is the relay worker of the top-level document

storage/estimate-usage-details*.description: the `usageDetails` member of `StorageEstimate` (the usage per storage endpoint), an extension of Chromium that is not in the Storage Standard

storage/partitioned-estimate-usage-detai.description: the `usageDetails` member of `StorageEstimate` (the usage per storage endpoint), an extension of Chromium that is not in the Storage Standard; the storage is not partitioned by top-level site either

svg/embedded/attr-image-fetchpriority.op.description: `fetchPriority` of SVG `<image>`: not in SVG 2 (an open proposal, w3c/svgwg#925; optional test)

svg/idlharness.window.js.description: the `ShadowAnimation` interface of SVG 2 (https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/struct.html#InterfaceShadowAnimation), the read-only mirrors of the animations of the referenced elements on their element instances: the `use` elements have no shadow tree of element instances (the referenced content is rendered in place), so the 7 subtests of the interface fail (no browser implements it)

svg/interact/scripted/tabindex-focus-fla.description: `audio[controls]`, `video[controls]` and `canvas[tabindex]` are children of an SVG `g` element: SVG 2 does not render HTML elements outside of a `foreignObject` (https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/render.html#Rendered-vs-NonRendered), and an element is a focusable area only when it is being rendered, delegates its rendering to its children or is relevant canvas fallback content (HTML §6.6.2 Data model), so they are not focusable; the test expects them focusable (the `iframe` passes because focusing it focuses its document)

svg/scripted/attr-script-fetchpriority.o.description: `fetchPriority` of SVG `<script>`: not in SVG 2 (an open proposal, w3c/svgwg#916; optional test)

svg/struct/scripted/switch_reentrant_rem.description: the test requires an `unload` event fired in the document of an iframe while its ancestor is removed by `removeChild()`, after the removal: HTML's destroy a child navigable (run by the removing steps of the iframe) destroys the document without unloading it (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#destroy-a-document-and-its-descendants), and the library fires `unload` before the removal, so `child.parentNode` is still the `switch` in the handler (the harness reports the uncaught assertion as an error)

svg/struct/scripted/use-load-error-event.description: the tests that change the reference of a `use` element to a local one "while loading" from a timer: the resource is already loaded when the timer runs (the loader of the runner answers in the same task), so the `load` or `error` event is fired

svg/types/scripted/SVGAnimatedEnumeratio.description: `SVG_FECOMPOSITE_OPERATOR_LIGHTER` is not a constant of `SVGFECompositeElement` in Filter Effects (https://drafts.csswg.org/filter-effects-1/#InterfaceSVGFECompositeElement), which only lists `UNKNOWN` to `ARITHMETIC`; the `lighter` operator of the `operator` attribute is rendered (no browser passes the test)

svg/types/scripted/SVGGraphicsElement-pa.description: `getScreenCTM with padding-left, scale` expects 47; with the `transform-origin` at the center of the border box (`50% 50%` for an `svg` element child of a `foreignObject`) and the user space at the content box, the inverse of the CTM maps x = 50 to 41, as the rotation subtests of the same file require (no transform origin satisfies both the rotation and the scale expectations); Chrome and Safari get 41 too

svg/types/scripted/SVGGraphicsElement.ge.description: the `markers` and `clipped` options of `getBBox()` (https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/coords.html#BoundingBoxes): the bounding boxes do not include the content of the markers, and are not intersected with the clip path bounding box (of the `clipPath` elements, with their `clip-path` and their `objectBoundingBox` units, and of the `clip` property of the images)

touch-events/idlharness.window.js.description: the `ontouchstart`, `ontouchend`, `ontouchmove` and `ontouchcancel` event handlers of `GlobalEventHandlers` are not exposed: "expose legacy touch event APIs" is false, as in the desktop browsers (Chrome, Firefox and Safari fail these subtests too)

touch-events/mouseevents-after-touchend..description: a tap of two fingers: a `touchend` is fired per touch, and the compatibility mouse events and the click of the primary touch are fired; the tentative test expects one `touchend` with both touches and no mouse event (only Gecko passes)

touch-events/touch-globaleventhandler-in.description: the `ontouchstart`, `ontouchend`, `ontouchmove` and `ontouchcancel` event handlers of `GlobalEventHandlers` are not exposed: "expose legacy touch event APIs" is false, as in the desktop browsers (the precondition of the test)

trusted-types/TrustedTypePolicyFactory-g.description: the SVG animation event handler content attributes (`onbegin`, `onend`, `onrepeat`)

web-animations/interfaces/Animatable/get.description: the test expects the animation of a `.pseudo::part(test)` rule on a div without shadow tree: `::part()` only matches the elements of the shadow tree of its originating element (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-shadow-parts/#part), so the rule matches nothing and no animation is created; the pseudo-element is valid (https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-1/#pseudo-element-parsing), so `getAnimations()` returns an empty list (Firefox fails it too: functional pseudo-elements are not supported for the animations, bug 1935557)

web-locks/bfcache/contention.https.windo.description: the owner set of the shared workers: a shared worker lives until it calls `close()` or its browsing context group is disposed, so the shared worker of the page in the back/forward cache keeps its lock when the page is evicted, and the `request()` of the next page waits forever (the `shared-worker` / `request` variant; in a browser the eviction ends the shared worker). The other variants pass: the contention evicts the page, which releases the locks of its window and of its dedicated workers

web-locks/storage-buckets.tentative.http.description: the test uses `StorageBucket.locks`, which the Storage Buckets specification does not define (its IDL has no `locks` attribute)

webaudio/the-audio-api/media-playback-wh.description: the `interrupted` state of an `AudioContext` whose document is not visible when the `media-playback-while-not-visible` feature is disallowed (the context keeps running)

webaudio/the-audio-api/the-audiocontext-.description: `setSinkId()` checks the identifier of the device (`NotFoundError`) before the state of the context (`InvalidStateError` for a stopped context or a detached document), and a pending `setSinkId()` is not rejected when the context is closed
the capture backend of the runner has no audio output device: the test waits for the change of the output to a device listed by `enumerateDevices()` and times out

`testMultiContextInput`: a `MediaStreamAudioSourceNode` of a suspended context does not buffer the audio of its track: once the context resumes, the test expects the frames produced while it was suspended
the test needs two audio output devices listed by `enumerateDevices()`: the capture backend of the runner has none

webaudio/the-audio-api/the-audioparam-in.description: the test has no limits for the `makeupGain` parameter of `DynamicsCompressorNode` (https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-dynamicscompressornode-makeupgain), which it finds by enumerating the `AudioParam` attributes: its branch for a parameter without limits reads `clippingTested`, which is not defined in its scope, so the subtest of `createDynamicsCompressor` fails with a `ReferenceError`

webaudio/the-audio-api/the-audioworklet-.description: `process()` is expected to read the `invalidParam` getter defined on `Object.prototype` (as the Chromium implementation does), and the node to output silence when it returns an array of an invalid size: the members of the `parameters` object are created with CreateDataProperty, which ignores the getter, so the processor outputs 1

webaudio/the-audio-api/the-convolvernode.description: the deviation is the largest difference with the reference divided by the reference value at its frame: the convolution is exact (no difference at all), so the test computes 0/0 (NaN dB) and fails; it only passes with rounding errors

webaudio/the-audio-api/the-mediaelementa.description: the media backend does not decode the audio of the media resources: a `MediaElementAudioSourceNode` outputs silence, and the test checks the audio of a file

webcodecs/image-decoder-image-orientatio.description: the orientations other than top-left expect `drawImage()` of a `VideoFrame` to ignore its rotation and flip when the canvas has `image-orientation: none` (a behavior of Chromium): a `VideoFrame` is rendered with its rotation and flip (https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#videoframe-rendering), and `image-orientation` does not apply to the images drawn on a canvas

webcodecs/image-decoder.https.any.js*.description: the YUV pixel formats (`I420`, `I422`, `I444` and their 10 and 12 bits variants) and the color spaces of the codecs: the image decoders of the rendering backend output RGBA pixels, so the frames are `RGBA`
the AVIF images with several tracks: the decoders of Meziantou.Framework.Imaging decode the image sequence of an AVIF image that also has a still image, so the image has one track

`new ImageDecoder({ type: 'junk/type' })` is expected not to throw and its `decode()` and `tracks.ready` to reject with a NotSupportedError, but the constructor throws a TypeError when the type is not a valid image MIME type (https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#valid-imagedecoderinit, step 1); `Test ReadableStream of gif` expects `type` to be the empty string after `close()`, but the Close ImageDecoder algorithm does not change [[type]] (https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#imagedecoder-close-imagedecoder), so the subtest fails before it handles its pending decode promise, rejected by `close()` (harness ERROR: unhandled rejection)

webauthn/createcredential-extensions.htt.description: the `appid` subtests expect `create()` to reject an `appid` extension input with a `NotSupportedError`, as Chromium does; `appid` is an authentication extension, and [[Create]] skips the extensions that are not registration extensions (https://w3c.github.io/webauthn/#CreateCred-process-extensions), so the credential is created

webauthn/createcredential-minpinlength.h.description: the `minPinLength` extension of CTAP 2.1, which WebAuthn Level 3 does not define: the virtual authenticators do not support it, so `test_driver.add_virtual_authenticator()` fails with an `unsupported operation` error

webauthn/createcredential-nested-frame.h.description: the three subtests that create the credential with a script of the frame pass an empty `user.id`, which [[Create]] rejects with a TypeError (the user handle has 1 to 64 bytes, https://w3c.github.io/webauthn/#sctn-createCredential step 5)

webauthn/credblob-*.description: the `credBlob` and `getCredBlob` extensions of CTAP 2.1, which WebAuthn Level 3 does not define (they are not members of `AuthenticationExtensionsClientInputs`): the virtual authenticators do not support `credBlob`, so `test_driver.add_virtual_authenticator()` fails with an `unsupported operation` error, and the client outputs have no `credBlob`

webauthn/getcredential-extensions.https..description: `credProps` is a registration extension, which [[DiscoverFromExternalSource]] skips (https://w3c.github.io/webauthn/#sctn-discover-from-external-source, step 7) instead of rejecting with a `NotSupportedError` as Chromium does

webauthn/getcredential-ui-mode-immediate.description: the `immediate` UI mode of `navigator.credentials.get()` (a proposal of Credential Management that WebAuthn Level 3 does not define for `PublicKeyCredential`): the request is rejected with a TypeError, as for an interface that does not support it

webauthn/remote-desktop-client-override..description: the `remoteDesktopClientOverride` extension input of a Chromium proposal (WebAuthn Level 3 defines the `remoteClientDataJSON` extension instead): it is not a member of `AuthenticationExtensionsClientInputs`, so it is ignored and the ceremonies succeed

webidl/current-realm.html.description: the platform objects that are not nodes (`NodeList`, `Event`, `Range`, `NodeIterator`, `TreeWalker`, `ImageData`, `HTMLCollection`) are wrapped in the current realm (the realm of the called function, e.g. `Document.prototype.querySelectorAll` of the top-level window called on the document of the iframe), with one wrapper per realm, instead of once in their relevant realm (the realm of the iframe): 11 subtests get an object of the top-level realm, and `getElementsByTagName()` called through the two realms returns two different wrappers of the same collection

webidl/ecmascript-binding/allow-shared.h.description: the test expects `new ImageDecoder({ data, type: "invalid" })` not to throw, but the constructor throws a TypeError when the type is not a valid image MIME type (https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#valid-imagedecoderinit, step 1)

websockets/back-forward-cache-*.description: the tentative tests expect the behaviors of Chromium: a page served with `Cache-Control: no-store` is kept in the back/forward cache, and an open WebSocket is closed when its page enters it. As in the other browsers, a document whose response has `Cache-Control: no-store` is not cached, and a WebSocket that is still connecting or open once the `pagehide` event handlers ran makes the document unsalvageable (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#unloading-document-cleanup-steps), so the BFCache executor reports a failed precondition

websockets/binary/001.html.description: the `?wpt_flags=websocket-h3` variant: the runner does not emulate the WebSocket over HTTP/3 server of wptserve, whose port `websocket-h3-https` is not in the ports of `WptServer`, so `{{ports[websocket-h3-https][0]}}` of `constants.sub.js` is not substituted and the URL `wss://web-platform.test:{{ports[websocket-h3-https][0]}}/echo` is invalid

websockets/constructor/option-bag.any.js.description: the options dictionary of the constructor (`new WebSocket(url, { protocols })`), a proposal that is not in the WebSockets Standard

websockets/constructor/target-address-sp.description: the options dictionary of the constructor and its `targetAddressSpace` member (Local Network Access)

websockets/cookies/cross-origin-cookie-s.description: the cookie without `SameSite` attribute set by the response of a cross-site WebSocket handshake is `Lax` by default, so it is not stored (fails in Chrome and Safari, which also treat the cookies as `Lax` by default)

websockets/unload-a-document/002.html.description: the test expects the popup to be restored from the back/forward cache by `history.back()`; the popup is opened without `noopener`, and the back/forward cache does not keep the documents of a popup that its opener can script (as in Chromium), so it is loaded again and reports that the document was discarded

websockets/unload-a-document/004.html.description: the test expects the document of the iframe to be restored from the back/forward cache by `history.back()`; as in the browsers, only the documents of the top-level traversables are kept in the back/forward cache, so the document of the iframe is loaded again and reports that it was discarded

websockets/Create-blocked-port.any.js*.description: `META: pac` (the proxy auto-config `resources/https-proxy.sub.pac`) is not supported: `bad-port-<port>.wpt` is not routed to the WPT server, so the `Basic check` WebSocket to an allowed port fails

workers/same-site-cookies/*.description: the `sameSiteCookies` option of `SharedWorker`: the worker always gets and sets the cookies of the `all` value in a first-party context, and starts in a third-party context

workers/shared-worker-partitioned-cookie.description: the partitioned cookies (CHIPS): the third-party iframe gets the partitioned cookie of the top-level site over HTTP

worklets/idlharness.https.any.js*.description: the test fetches `/interfaces/worklets.idl`, which does not exist in the web-platform-tests (the Worklets specification was merged into the HTML Standard, whose IDL is tested by html/dom/idlharness)

xhr/open-url-multi-window-4.htm.description: the test (whose comment says the pass condition is unclear and follows a proposal, whatwg/xhr#3, that was not merged) expects `error` and `loadend` events for an XHR of an iframe removed during the request: the document is destroyed, its fetch group is terminated, and the tasks of the terminated fetch do not run (the document is not fully active), so no event is fired, as in Firefox

xhr/open-url-multi-window-6.htm.description: Web IDL creates the exception thrown by an operation in the current realm (the realm of the `open()` function, the realm of the iframe: https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-throw); the test expects an exception of the realm of the caller. xhr/send-authentication-cors-setrequesth.description: the synchronous request whose CORS preflight rejects the `Authorization` header expects `error` and `loadend` events: the request error steps of a synchronous request throw the `NetworkError` before the events are fired (https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#request-error-steps, step 4)

css/cssom/rule-restrictions.html.description: the `@page` subtest expects the declaration of `transform` (which does not apply to the page context) dropped from `CSSPageRule.style`, as Gecko does; as in Blink and WebKit, and as css/css-page/cssom/margin-001.html and margin-002.html expect, the declarations of all the properties are kept in `@page` and in the margin rules (the cascade of the page context ignores them; css-page-3 leaves the properties that are not in CSS 2.1 undefined)

css/css-view-transitions/scoped/scope-be.description: the test expects a scoped transition to be skipped (`ready` rejected with an `InvalidStateError`) when its root element becomes the document element (`replaceChild()` of the document element) before the capture or during the update callback, as Chrome does; the specification has no such step (the skip conditions are an element without a box, or of a box type that does not qualify for layout containment), so the transition runs and `ready` resolves

css/css-writing-modes/forms/text-input-s.description: `setSelectionRange()` on a focused text field does not scroll its value to reveal the caret (only the arrow keys, `Home` and `End` do), so `scrollLeft`/`scrollTop` is still 0 before the blur; the scroll back to the start of the value when the field loses the focus is not implemented either

html/browsers/browsing-the-web/back-forw.description: the dedicated workers of a document in the back/forward cache are not suspended (only the tasks and timers of its window are): the lock released by the test window is granted to the worker of the cached page, whose callback runs and posts `granted` to the `BroadcastChannel` before the page is restored

html/browsers/the-window-object/open-clo.description: the tentative `windowfeatures` attribute of `a`, `area` and `form` (https://github.com/mfreed7/split-tabs): a link with `windowfeatures` and no `target` navigates the test window itself instead of opening a new one, so the harness times out

html/canvas/element/manual/filters/svg-f.description: the SVG filters of a canvas (`url()`) that use the color of a visited link (`flood-color`, `lighting-color` set by a `:visited` rule) do not taint the canvas: the canvas stays origin-clean

html/canvas/element/manual/wide-gamut-ca.description: the HDR settings of the canvases (`toneMapping` in `CanvasRenderingContext2DSettings`)

html/canvas/element/text/2d.text.shape.a.description: the test compares the positions of the canvas text, which has the `letter-spacing` after each character (the `width` of `TextMetrics` includes the last one), with the ones of a DOM text of the same spacing, which the library lays out without the spacing after the last character of the line (it "is not applied at the beginning or end of a line", https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#letter-spacing-property); Chrome applies it at the end of the line, so the variants with `10px` of spacing pass there

html/canvas/element/text/2d.text.shape.s.description: the test compares the positions of the canvas text, which has the `letter-spacing` after each character (the `width` of `TextMetrics` includes the last one), with the ones of a DOM text of the same spacing, which the library lays out without the spacing after the last character of the line (it "is not applied at the beginning or end of a line", https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#letter-spacing-property); Chrome applies it at the end of the line, so the variants with `10px` of spacing pass there

html/document-isolation-policy/reporting.description: Document-Isolation-Policy violation reports (`dip` reports): the worker's `ReportingObserver` never gets the two reports it waits for, so the test times out

the test calls `toJSON()` on the reports: `Report` and the report bodies are dictionaries since w3c/reporting#284 (https://w3c.github.io/reporting/#dictdef-report), so the reports given to the observers are plain objects without `toJSON()` (the browsers still implement the former `Report` interface)

html/semantics/embedded-content/the-obje.description: the test waits for an `error` event when the `<object>` falls back because its `data:image/png,invalid` image cannot be rendered; the HTML Standard jumps to the fallback steps without firing `error` for an image that cannot be rendered (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/iframe-embed-object.html#the-object-element: only a failed load fires `error`), which is what the library does, so the test times out

navigation-api/navigate-event/intercept-.description: the test expects the `finished` promise of the first `navigate()`, a navigation to another document that is not intercepted, to be rejected with an `AbortError` when the intercepted `navigate("?intercepted")` stops it; the API method tracker of such a navigation is cleaned up once its `navigate` event is committed ("If endResultIsSameDocument is false and apiMethodTracker is non-null, then clean up apiMethodTracker", https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#commit-a-navigate-event), so aborting the navigation does not reject its promises: they stay pending, as `ordering-and-transition/navigate-cross-document-double.html` and `navigate-204-205-download-then-same-document.html` expect, and the test times out waiting for `firstFinished`. The library also commits the first navigation as soon as the headers of its delayed response arrive (the runner sends the headers of `blank.html?pipe=trickle(d1)` at once, as wptserve does), so the iframe has a new document before the second navigation starts. Edge (the only browser of wpt.fyi with results) fails the test too
