css/css-masking/hit-test/clip-path-eleme.description: the hit testing of a `clipPath` element ignores its text: `SvgClipping.Contains` gets the layout of a `text` child with `SvgTextLayout.Get(child, viewport)` without `inResource: true`, and the text of a clipPath element is not rendered, so the layout is null and a point on a glyph (10,40 in the first M) is clipped out (`elementFromPoint` returns the svg element)

intersection-observer/v2/first-line-occl.description: 1 of 4 subtests: `box-shadow` does not apply to `::first-line` (it is not in the properties that apply to it, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo-4/#first-line-styling, which lets user agents apply other properties; the test expects the shadow of the first line to occlude the target, as in Chromium): the target stays visible and no notification is queued

css/cssom/caretPositionFromPoint-svg-tex.description: `caretPositionFromPoint()` on an element of an SVG document fragment returns the start of the element (`CaretPosition.FromPoint`): the position in the characters of an SVG `text` element under the point is not resolved, so the offset node is the `text` element instead of its text node

css/css-animations/display-none-animatio.description: a CSS animation whose keyframes keep the element rendered (`display: block`) is not started on an element whose own style sets `display: none` at the same time (the exit animation pattern of https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display-4/#display-animation): `CssAnimationUpdater` starts no animation when the unanimated display is none (`ComputedStyle.IsDisplayNoneForAnimations`), so `getAnimations()` is empty

css/css-transitions/display-none-transit.description: 5 of 7 subtests: right after `dialog.close()` or `hidePopover()`, `getAnimations({ subtree: true })` returns 4 of the 5 closing transitions (`display`, `opacity`, `overlay` and `scale` of the element, `opacity` of its `::backdrop`): the style update of `getAnimations()` (`Document.FlushAnimationStyles`, `StyleEngine.RecalculateStyles`) computes the styles of the `::marker`, `::before` and `::after` pseudo-elements only, so the `::backdrop` transition is not started yet

css/css-properties-values-api/at-propert.description: 35 of 68 subtests: the `@property` descriptors are optional since https://github.com/w3c/css-houdini-drafts/commit/e1f11c5e6fffef319bcdc0f0fe25034d1a6a4b3f (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13211, Aug 2026): a missing `syntax` defaults to `"*"`, a missing `inherits` to true, and a missing `initial-value` is the guaranteed-invalid value even for a non-universal syntax; the rules without `syntax`, `inherits` or `initial-value` are still dropped as invalid, so no `CSSPropertyRule` is found for them

48 of 107 subtests: the `@property` descriptors are optional since https://github.com/w3c/css-houdini-drafts/commit/e1f11c5e6fffef319bcdc0f0fe25034d1a6a4b3f (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13211, Aug 2026): a missing or invalid `syntax` defaults to `"*"`, a missing or invalid `inherits` to true, and a missing `initial-value` is the guaranteed-invalid value even for a non-universal syntax; the rules without one of them (or with an invalid `syntax` or `inherits`) are still dropped as invalid, so the rule is not found and the property is not registered

css/css-properties-values-api/determine-.description: 3 of 15 subtests: the `@property` descriptors are optional since https://github.com/w3c/css-houdini-drafts/commit/e1f11c5e6fffef319bcdc0f0fe25034d1a6a4b3f (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13211, Aug 2026): a later rule without `syntax`, `inherits` or `initial-value` is still dropped as invalid, so the earlier registration (`1px`) wins instead of the later one

css/css-scroll-snap/snap-events/scrollsn.description: the `?include=wheel` variant: "scrollsnapchanging doesn't fire if scroll doesn't reach different snap targets" (now awaited, it passed before because its promise was not) wheel-scrolls the scroller by 10px in both axes and expects `scrollLeft` to snap back to 0, but the scroller has `scroll-snap-type: y mandatory`: the x axis does not snap (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scroll-snap-1/#scroll-snap-type), so `scrollLeft` stays 10 (the `both mandatory` scroller of the scrollsnapchange variant passes); fails in Edge too

css/css-ui/accent-color-accentcolor-is-p.description: 2 of 4 subtests: `accent-color: AccentColor` under a parent with the default accent color (`auto`) computes to the default color `rgb(0, 117, 255)`, and `AccentColorText` of the element is then the contrast color of that color (black, `CssValueComputer.GetAccentColor` and `ComputeContrastColor`) instead of the default `AccentColorText` (white) that the test expects for the system accent color (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui-4/#widget-accent)

css/css-values/attr-security-if.html.description: 4 of 20 subtests: the new subtests expect `image-set()` to be invalid at computed-value time when the resolution of an option is chosen by an `if()` whose condition uses an attr()-tainted value; https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#attr-security makes a declaration invalid only when an attr()-tainted value is used as or in a `<url>` ("using attr() for other purposes is fine, even if the usage is near a url"), and the URLs of the options are not tainted; fails in Edge too

css/css-values/attr-security-image-set.h.description: 10 of 16 subtests: the test expects `image-set()` to be invalid at computed-value time when the resolution or the `type()` of an option comes from `attr()`; https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#attr-security makes a declaration invalid only when an attr()-tainted value is used as or in a `<url>` ("using attr() for other purposes is fine, even if the usage is near a url"), and the URLs of the options are not tainted; fails in Edge too

css/css-values/ident-function-substituti.description: 1 of 14 subtests: `ident("")` substitutes an empty value instead of the guaranteed-invalid value (so `var(--empty, PASS)` is empty instead of its fallback): a result that cannot be represented as an ident returns the guaranteed-invalid value since https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/commit/923794988c1e691633a4528f4ce28f2d2b2f305b (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/14399); `CssSubstitution.ReplaceIdent` serializes the empty identifier

css/css-values/ident-function-taint-anim.description: 1 of 3 subtests: the animation taint of custom properties (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-variables-1/#animation-tainted): `var()` of a custom property derived from an animated one (here an inherited `--source` animated on the parent, through `ident()`) in a property that is not animatable (`animation-name`) is substituted (`foo`) instead of being the guaranteed-invalid value that makes it use its fallback (`none`); fails in Edge too

css/css-values/random-item-nested.html.description: 1 of 5 subtests: the random cache name of `random-item(auto, ...)` is built from the key and the number of items (`ua-random-item-auto-2` in `CssSubstitution.ReplaceRandomItem`), not from the property and the index of the function (`auto` is `element-scoped property-index-scoped`, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#random-caching), so nested `random-item(auto, ...)` with the same number of items share their random base value and only `one` is produced

css/css-mixins/private/css-private-lexic.description: 2 of 11 subtests: a `var()` in a `@private` rule of a nested style rule does not see the private properties of the enclosing style rules (`CssPrivateScope`: "the initial values of the @private rules only see the private properties of their own scope"), the behavior the test expected before; https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/14790 (Nov 2026) resolved that private names are visible in all the nested rules, `@private` declarations included

css/css-mixins/private/css-private-mixin.description: 1 of 7 subtests: a `var()` in a `@private` rule of a nested style rule of a mixin does not see the private properties of the enclosing rule (`CssPrivateScope`: "the initial values of the @private rules only see the private properties of their own scope"); https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/14790 (Nov 2026) resolved that private names are visible in all the nested rules, `@private` declarations included

accname/name/comp_content_visibility.ten.description: 3 of 6 subtests: the tentative test expects the `SPEC_AMBIGUOUS_LOG_VALUE` placeholder as the accessible name of the heading, button and link in a skipped `content-visibility: auto` subtree (an open spec ambiguity), which no engine returns; the roles pass

container-timing/tentative/containertimi.description: recording the container roots added after an input until the next input: as for the largest contentful paint, every new paint is ignored once an input or scroll event was dispatched, so the root added after the first input (and the root that `take()` adds to wait for the pending paints) is never reported and the test times out

the test expects the keys of `toJSON()` without `id`, but `PerformanceContainerTiming` inherits the `id` attribute of `PerformanceEntry` (https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceentry-id), which the default `toJSON()` includes

content-security-policy/inheritance/hist.description: 1 of 2 subtests: `Same-document navigation in parent frame during pending history navigation preserves child FrameNavigationEntry` times out (the same-document navigation of the iframe while its traversal back to the first entry is pending, followed by a navigation away and back of the child `b1`); the cause was not found, the first subtest with the same pending traversal passes

custom-elements/registries/adoption-glob.description: 1 of 17 subtests: an element with the global registry adopted into a document without registry keeps a "registry of its document" state, so it gets the global registry of the next document it is adopted into; the adopt steps (https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-adopt) set its registry to null in the first document, then to the effective global registry of the registry looked up from its parent, a shadow root with a scoped registry, which is null

custom-elements/registries/scoped-regist.description: 1 of 17 subtests: an element with the global registry adopted into a document without registry (an inert template contents owner document) keeps a "registry of its document" state, so it gets the global registry of the iframe document it is then appended to; the adopt steps (https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-adopt) set its registry to null, then to the effective global registry of its parent's scoped registry, which is null (the test was changed to match the specification)

domparsing/stream-html-pending-text.html.description: 22 of 26 subtests: the coalescing of the parser's text insertions (whatwg/html#13199): the streaming parser appends a chunk of text to the existing Text node without DOM's "replace data", so no `characterData` MutationRecord is queued

html/syntax/parsing/parser-text-node-coa.description: 14 of 29 subtests: the coalescing of the parser's text insertions (whatwg/html#13199): the parser appends the text of a later run (after an ignored token, a `document.write()`, a self-removing script, foster parenting, a network chunk...) to the existing Text node without DOM's "replace data", so no `characterData` MutationRecord is queued, and the first chunk of a streamed `text/plain` document is not flushed into its `<pre>` before the next one arrives

html/canvas/offscreen/manual/context-att.description: the HDR settings of the canvases (`toneMapping` in `getContextAttributes()`, whatwg/html#11734)

longtask-timing/container-attributes-cro.description: 1 of 3 subtests: the attribution of a `self` long task reports `window` and no container, while the algorithm keeps the culprit settings for `self` (https://w3c.github.io/longtasks/#report-long-tasks), so the attribution of a same-origin iframe observing its own long task has the `iframe` container type and the `id`, `name` and `src` of the iframe

longtask-timing/longtask-in-childiframe-.description: the attribution of a `cross-origin-descendant` long task reports `window` and no container (as the former version of the test expected), while the algorithm keeps the culprit settings for a cross-origin descendant (https://w3c.github.io/longtasks/#report-long-tasks): the test now expects the `iframe` container type and the `id`, `name` and `src` of the iframe

long-animation-frame/loaf-promise-cross-.description: the long animation frame in which the same-origin iframe streamed by the test runs its 80 ms script (which detaches the cross-origin iframe through the adoption agency algorithm) is not reported to the observer of the parent document: no entry covers `detachReferenceTime`, so the test times out

resource-timing/content-type-failed-subf.description: 2 of 13 subtests: the resource timing entry of an iframe whose navigation response is a 204 or 205 (which does not replace the document of the iframe) has the `responseStatus` 0 instead of the status of the response

html/semantics/forms/the-input-element/c.description: 18 of 21 subtests: the `defaultindeterminate` content attribute of checkboxes and the `defaultIndeterminate` IDL attribute, with the dirty indeterminateness flag used by cloning and form reset (proposal whatwg/html#13224)

svg/animations/begin-end-accesskey-keypr.description: 2 of 4 subtests: the tentative test expects a key press not to begin or end an animation whose `begin` or `end` is `accessKey(a)`, but SVG Animations still defines the accessKey-value (https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/specs/animations/#AccessKeyValueSyntax), which the library implements (a `keydown` of the key adds an instance time); its removal is only proposed (w3c/svgwg#1262, no browser implements it). The lowercase `accesskey(a)` subtests pass

svg/animations/begin-end-accesskey-not-e.description: 2 of 7 subtests: only the SVG spelling `accessKey(` is recognized as an accessKey-value (case-sensitive), so the lowercase `accesskey(a)` (the SMIL spelling) is parsed as an event-value whose event name is `accesskey(a)`, and a script event of that type begins or ends the animation; the test expects neither spelling to be an event name (https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/specs/animations/#EventValueSyntax)

svg/animations/syncbase-offset-overflow..description: the SMIL times are integer microseconds (`SmilTime`, at most about 9.2e12 s): a clock value beyond that (`300000000000000000000000000000000000000s`) is clamped to `indefinite` instead of a large finite time, so `a` and `c` get no finite begin or end, and `b` (`a.begin+3e38s`) and `d` (`c.end`) get no current interval (`getStartTime()` throws `InvalidStateError`) where the test expects resolved finite times

svg/interact/scripted/embedded-document-.description: 2 of 4 subtests: the root `svg` element of an SVG document (in an `iframe` and in an `object`) is not focusable: without `tabindex`, only the SVG `a` elements with a link are focusable areas (`Focus.IsFocusableByDefault`), so `focus()` on the document element does not focus it, and no `focus` event is fired (https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/interact.html#Focus)

svg/path/arc-tiny-radii.html.description: 2 of 6 subtests (`A 1e30 1e-30` and `A 1e-30 1e30`): the out-of-range radii are scaled up by √Λ (https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/implnote.html#ArcCorrectionOutOfRangeRadii) to 5e60 and 5, so the arc is half of an ellipse about 1e61 user units long; the length, computed in double precision, overflows the `float` returned by `getTotalLength()` (Infinity), where the test expects a finite length and end point

svg/render/never-rendered-element-descen.description: 4 of 74 subtests: the bounding box of a `g` (`getBBox()`) includes the shapes inside a child `symbol` or `clipPath` element, with or without `display: inline !important`: `SvgBoundingBox.GetBox` recurses into `symbol` and `clipPath` children like into a `g`, although these are never-rendered elements whose descendants do not contribute to the bounding box of an ancestor (https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/render.html#TermNeverRenderedElement)

svg/text/scripted/shaped-text-metrics.ht.description: 1 of 7 subtests: `getComputedTextLength()` of `fiat` with `letter-spacing: 10px` is 112.55, 10px more than the width of the same HTML span (102.55): the SVG text adds the letter spacing after its last character, which the inline layout does not apply at the end of a line (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#letter-spacing-property); the position of `a` matches

svg/text/scripted/text-query-ligature-dx.description: the `dx` of a character that is not the first one of its typographic character (the `i` of the `fi` ligature of Lato) is ignored: `SvgTextLayout` reads the `x`, `y`, `dx`, `dy` and `rotate` values of the cluster starts only, while the text layout algorithm adds `resolve_dx[i]` of every character to the shift (https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/text.html#TextLayoutAlgorithm), so the `a` after the ligature is not moved by 20px

svg/text/scripted/textpath-textlength-te.description: the anchored chunk of a `textPath` is always anchored as left-to-right text (`Anchor` gets a progression sign of 1 for text paths): with `direction: rtl`, `text-anchor: start` and `startOffset="100%"`, the text starts at the end of the path and is hidden (its bounding box is empty, x 0), where the start of right-to-left text is its right edge (https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/text.html#TextAnchoringProperties), so the text should span 75 to 100 (the left-to-right variant, 001, passes)

svg/text/scripted/typographic-character-.description: 6 of 11 subtests: the character queries of a character that is not the first one of its typographic character (a combining mark, a Devanagari vowel sign) return its own zero-advance cell at the start of the typographic character: `getEndPositionOfChar()` returns the start and `getExtentOfChar()` has a zero width, where they return the values of the whole typographic character (https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/text.html#TermFindTypographicCharacterForCharacter); the point 1px before the end of the second Devanagari cluster then falls in the first one for `getCharNumAtPosition()`

svg/types/scripted/SVGLength-invalid-val.description: 68 of 108 subtests: after a script writes a negative radius or size through the `baseVal` SVGLength (`value`, `valueAsString`, `newValueSpecifiedUnits()`, `valueInSpecifiedUnits`), `baseVal` keeps the written value (-20), while the same value in markup is ignored and reads back as the initial value (0, or 100% for `svg`): the content attribute written by the SVGLength is not parsed again into `baseVal` (https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/types.html#SynchronizingReflectedValues, w3c/svgwg#1210); the computed values and `animVal` get the initial value

ai/*.description: built-in AI APIs (Prompt, Summarizer, Translator, Language Detector...)

bluetooth/bidi/idl/idlharness.tentative..description: the advertisements (`BluetoothAdvertisingEvent`, `BluetoothManufacturerDataMap` and `BluetoothServiceDataMap`; `watchAdvertisements()` rejects with a `NotSupportedError`), and `BluetoothPermissionResult` (the `bluetooth` permission of `navigator.permissions.query()`, which Chromium does not implement either)

bluetooth/bidi/server/maxWriteWithoutRes.description: `BluetoothRemoteGATTServer.maxWriteWithoutResponseSize` and the `maxwritewithoutresponsesizechanged` event, which are not in the IDL of the specification (`BluetoothRemoteGATTServer` is not an `EventTarget`)

connection-allowlist/tentative/iframe-co.description: 2 subtests: the iframes whose `src` is `about:` (or ` about:`) navigate to `about:`, which is not `about:blank`: its fetch is a network error (https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#scheme-fetch, "about"), so the frame has an error document of an opaque origin, whose `contentWindow.document` the test cannot access (Chromium loads `about:blank`)

connection-allowlist/tentative/payment-r.description: the just-in-time installation of the payment handlers of a payment method manifest (its `default_applications`): `canMakePayment()` of a URL payment method without an installed payment handler is false, and `show()` rejects with a `NotSupportedError`, so the manifests that the allowlist allows cannot be observed (the `*-blocked` variants pass)

connection-allowlist/tentative/service-w.description: 2 subtests: the shared worker whose `Connection-Allowlist` is `()` calls `importScripts('shared-worker-onconnect.js')`, which its own allowlist blocks (an imported script is fetched with the policy container of the worker, https://w3c.github.io/connection-allowlists/#should-request-be-blocked-by-connection-allowlists): the worker throws a `NetworkError` and never answers, and the error of the script of a shared worker is not reported to the `SharedWorker` object, so the test times out (the next subtest does not run)

connection-allowlist/tentative/web_auth_.description: 1 subtest: the related origin requests of WebAuthn (the remote validation of an RP ID that is not a registrable domain suffix of the origin, `/.well-known/webauthn`, https://w3c.github.io/webauthn/#sctn-validating-relation-origin): `create()` rejects with a `SecurityError` before any fetch, where the test expects the `NotAllowedError` of a validation fetch blocked by the allowlist

connection-allowlist/tentative/webrtc-*.description: WebRTC (`RTCPeerConnection`): the `webrtc` parameter of the allowlists (https://w3c.github.io/connection-allowlists/#should-webrtc-be-blocked-by-connection-allowlists) has no connection to block or report

css/css-exclusions/*.description: CSS Exclusions (`wrap-flow`, `wrap-through` have no effect); Requires layout

css/css-navigation/*.description: CSS navigation (`@navigation` rule, `navigation()`/`link-to()` conditions and the related at-rules)

gamepad/gamepad-default-permissions-poli.description: the frame (`permissions-policy-gamepad.html`) posts `{ enabled }` without the `type: 'availability-result'` that `test_feature_availability()` of `/permissions-policy/resources/permissions-policy.js` waits for: the tests time out in every browser

gamepad/idlharness-extensions.https.wind.description: `/interfaces/gamepad-extensions.idl` was removed from web-platform-tests: `idl_test()` fails to fetch it

screen-details/getScreenDetails.tentativ.description: 2 of 5 subtests: the test waits for the `unload` event of the initial about:blank document of a removed iframe, which is not fired (as tested by dom/nodes/insertion-removing-steps/insertion-removing-steps-iframe.window.js); the last subtest does not run after the timeout

web-nfc/*.description: needs the Chromium MojoJS mock of the NFC adapter (`WebNFCTest` of `/resources/chromium/nfc-mock.js`)
an NFC adapter: the library has none, so `NDEFReader.scan()`, `write()` and `makeReadOnly()` reject with a `NotSupportedError` once the `nfc` permission is granted

webtransport/back-forward-cache-with-clo.description: the tentative tests expect the behaviors of Chromium: a page served with `Cache-Control: no-store` is kept in the back/forward cache. As in the other browsers, a document whose response has `Cache-Control: no-store` is not cached, so the BFCache executor reports a failed precondition

webtransport/back-forward-cache-with-ope.description: the tentative tests expect the behaviors of Chromium: a page served with `Cache-Control: no-store` is kept in the back/forward cache. As in the other browsers, a document whose response has `Cache-Control: no-store` is not cached, so the BFCache executor reports a failed precondition

webtransport/export-keying-material.http.description: `exportKeyingMaterial()` (https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/#dom-webtransport-exportkeyingmaterial): MsQuic, which establishes the sessions of the HTTP loader, does not expose the TLS exporter, so the promise is rejected with a `NotSupportedError`

webtransport/stream-stats.https.any.js.description: 2 subtests use the `stats-data-transfer.py` handler, which is not in `webtransport/handlers`: the session is rejected

webtransport/streams-close.https.any.js.description: 4 subtests create the errors with `new WebTransportError({streamErrorCode})`, the constructor of an older version of the specification (Chromium): the constructor is `WebTransportError(optional DOMString message = "", optional WebTransportErrorOptions options = {})` (https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/#web-transport-error-interface), so the dictionary is the message and the stream is aborted with the code 0

webusb/idlharness.https.any.js.description: the setup awaits `getFakeDevice().device` (a property of the promise, undefined) instead of the device: the objects of the device are not created, in every browser
`USBPermissionResult` and the `usb` permission of `navigator.permissions.query()` (Chromium does not implement them either)

webusb/usb.serviceworker.https.html.description: the test expects no `navigator.usb` in a service worker, as in Chromium: the IDL exposes `USB` and `WorkerNavigator.usb` in every worker (`[Exposed=(Worker,Window)]`), and `getDevices()` uses the permission storage of the service worker client in a `ServiceWorkerGlobalScope`

webxr/*.description: WebXR Device API; the tests run on the WebXR Test API (`navigator.xr.test`), which needs no hardware, and most of them (`xr_session_promise_test` of `/webxr/resources/webxr_util.js`) also need WebGL (`getContext("webgl")` returns null) for an `XRWebGLLayer`

old-tests/submission/Microsoft/foreignco.description: the test expects the SVG element names to be camelCased outside of an `svg` element (`<AlTglYph>` in a `div` to be `altGlyph`): the HTML parser only adjusts the SVG tag names in foreign content (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#parsing-main-inforeign)

old-tests/submission/Microsoft/selection.description: legacy test (old-tests, not maintained): it expects `select()` and `setSelectionRange()` on a focused text field to collapse the selection of the document around the field (anchor and focus at its parent) and `getSelection().toString()` to return the selected text of the field, which no specification defines

infrastructure/expected-fail/*.description: fails by design in every browser: the test checks that the WPT runner reports a failing subtest, a harness error or a timeout (the expectations of `infrastructure/metadata`)

infrastructure/testharness/lone-surrogat.description: fails by design in every browser: the test checks that the WPT runner reports a failing subtest, a harness error or a timeout (the expectations of `infrastructure/metadata`)

infrastructure/wpt-metadata/prefs/gecko..description: the test sets a preference of Gecko with the metadata of wptrunner (`prefs`)

infrastructure/testdriver/bidi/*.description: the WebDriver BiDi commands of the test driver (`test_driver.bidi.*`) that testdriver-vendor.js does not implement, or only for the current browsing context: the emulation overrides, the Bluetooth simulation, the permissions of other origins and the event subscriptions

infrastructure/testdriver/navigate.html.description: `test_driver.create_window()` and `test_driver.navigate()` are not implemented by testdriver-vendor.js

infrastructure/testdriver/set_get_window.description: `test_driver.set_window_rect()` does not move or resize the window: the viewport of the runner has a fixed size

infrastructure/testdriver/file_upload.su.description: the `file_upload.py` handler of the WPT server is not emulated

infrastructure/testdriver/actions/eventO.description: two mouse pointer sources pressed in the same tick: the test driver only fires the `mousedown` of the source pressed first in the call order (`b`), where WebDriver performs the actions of a tick in the order of the input sources (`a`, then `b`)

infrastructure/testdriver/actions/penPoi.description: a `pointerMove` action without properties keeps the properties of the previous `pointerDown` (a pressure of 0.36) instead of the default ones of WebDriver (a pressure of 0.5)

infrastructure/channels/*.description: the message channels of `/resources/channel.sub.js` need the WebSocket handler of the WPT server (`/msg_channel`), which is not emulated

infrastructure/server/wpt-server-http.su.description: the `{{browser_host}}` substitution of the `.sub.` files is not emulated (the requests to the host without a subdomain fail)

infrastructure/server/wpt-server-websock.description: the `{{browser_host}}` substitution of the `.sub.` files is not emulated (the requests to the host without a subdomain fail)

infrastructure/server/http2-websocket.su.description: the WebSockets over HTTP/2 (RFC 8441) of the WPT server are not emulated

infrastructure/server/test-pac.sub.html.description: the proxy auto-configuration file set by the metadata of wptrunner (`pac`) is not emulated

infrastructure/server/subdomain-flag.www.description: the `.www.` flag of the file names (the test is loaded from the `www` subdomain) is not emulated

infrastructure/assumptions/non-local-por.description: Local Network Access: a fetch from the `http-public` address space to a local address is not blocked

html/canvas/element/manual/draw-element-.description: HTML-in-canvas: all the 4000 pixels of the masked grayscale backdrop differ by 1 from the reference (3900 are allowed): the canvas bitmap is 8-bit (premultiplied, Rgba32) where the page is painted with 16-bit components: the drawable element, drawn into the canvas, then the canvas drawn onto the page, round the colors twice (e.g. the grayscale of the green 0.7152 * 128 = 91.55 is 92 in the canvas, 91 for the red component of the reference)

HTML-in-canvas: 32 antialiased pixels of the text "Hello" over the grayscale backdrop differ by 1 (the canvas is 1 lighter): the canvas bitmap is 8-bit (premultiplied, Rgba32) where the page is painted with 16-bit components: the drawable element, drawn into the canvas, then the canvas drawn onto the page, round the colors twice (the backdrop layer and the glyphs are rounded to 8 bits in the canvas)

HTML-in-canvas: 98 antialiased pixels of the edge of the circle drawn by `arc()` and of the text, under the grayscale backdrop filter and the `screen` blend mode, differ by 1: the canvas bitmap is 8-bit (premultiplied, Rgba32) where the page is painted with 16-bit components: the drawable element, drawn into the canvas, then the canvas drawn onto the page, round the colors twice

HTML-in-canvas: 34 antialiased pixels of the text and of the edges of the sibling over the grayscale backdrop differ by 1: the canvas bitmap is 8-bit (premultiplied, Rgba32) where the page is painted with 16-bit components: the drawable element, drawn into the canvas, then the canvas drawn onto the page, round the colors twice

HTML-in-canvas: two causes. (1) The edges of the color grids of the second and the fourth canvases (260 pixels of the columns x=269, x=289 and x=369, difference 85): the reference is at a fractional position (x=269.333, the second column of `grid: 256px / 1fr 1fr 1fr`) and its `clip-path: rect()` (the clip of the canvas imitated on the wrapper with `translate()` and `will-change: transform`) is not snapped: it cuts the snapped background of the grid with an antialiased edge (2/3 or 1/3 coverage), where the canvas, and the snapshot drawn into it, are snapped to x=269; snapping the translated `will-change` boxes breaks css/css-view-transitions/fractional-translation-from-transform.html and css/css-transforms/backface-visibility-hidden-animated-002.html, which expect their fractional position. (2) The pixels of the blurred `box-shadow` (4254 pixels, difference 1): the canvas bitmap is 8-bit (premultiplied, Rgba32) where the page is painted with 16-bit components: the drawable element, drawn into the canvas, then the canvas drawn onto the page, round the colors twice

HTML-in-canvas: "DOM changes made in the paint event will not show up until the subsequent rendering update": the library has no frame of a rendering update, a screenshot paints the current state of the document; the screenshot of the test is taken after the rendering update whose `requestAnimationFrame()` callback restores `opacity: .9` and whose paint event sets `opacity: .1` again, so the box is painted with the opacity .1 set by the paint event

HTML-in-canvas: the snapshot is recorded with the opacity 0 of the first keyframe: the `ready` promise of the CSS animations resolves in the "update animations and send events" step of the rendering update that starts them (current time 0), and the `requestPaint()` of `waitForCanvasPaint()`, called from it, fires the paint event at the paint step of the same rendering update, where the test expects a later frame (opacity 0.5 after the 1 ms of the 0.001% keyframe)

animation-worklet/worklet-animation-loca.description: the test waits for `animation.currentTime > 1000` on an animation whose effect ends at 1000 ms before it takes the screenshot: a worklet animation is an animation, which is finished and whose current time is limited to the end of its effect (https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-1/#update-an-animations-finished-state), so the screenshot is never taken; the worklet animations of the former Chromium implementation never finished

animation-worklet/worklet-animation-with.description: the test has no encoding declaration and one of its animator names is Japanese: decoded as windows-1252 (UTF-8 is not detected for a document of the network, as in the browsers: `encoding-detection/utf-8.html`), the name contains code points that are not identifier code points, so `registerAnimator()` throws a TypeError ("If name is not a valid <ident>"), the module does not register the animators and the constructor of the worklet animations throws before the screenshot is taken

the test creates its timeline with `new ScrollTimeline({ scrollSource, orientation })`, the options of an old draft of Scroll-driven Animations (now `source` and `axis`, with progress-based times instead of the times of a `timeRange`): the unknown members are ignored, so the timeline is the scroll timeline of the scrolling element of the document, which does not scroll (the animated box stays at its first keyframe, the same test with the root scroller passes); fails in every browser

compat/webkit-box-rtl-flex.html.description: the reference is not equivalent: `-webkit-box-flex: 1` distributes the free space from the content widths of the boxes (their flex basis is `auto`, as in Blink), where the `flex: 1` of the reference has a flex basis of 0: the green box is 249.56px wide (250px in the reference) and its `B`, aligned to the right (`direction: rtl`), is drawn 0.44px to the left (x=246.89 instead of 247.33), so 72 antialiased pixels of the glyph differ by up to 47. The backgrounds of the boxes are snapped to the same pixels, and the browsers that place the glyphs on whole pixels hide the offset

compat/webkit-input-placeholder.html.description: the legacy `::-webkit-input-placeholder` alias of `::placeholder` (https://github.com/whatwg/compat/issues/65): the selector parses, like every `-webkit-` pseudo-element, but matches nothing

css/CSS2/backgrounds/background-intrinsi.description: expects the percentage `width` and `height` of the root svg element of a background image to give it a size relative to the background positioning area (40% by 60% of it); an SVG image with percentage dimensions has no natural size and fills the area, as in every browser

css/CSS2/bidi-text/bidi-003.xht.description: the reference has the spaces of the reordered text on the right of each part; with the white space processing of CSS Text (a collapsible space that follows a collapsible space is collapsed, "ignoring bidi formatting characters"), the space that is kept before U+202C POP DIRECTIONAL FORMATTING is in the right-to-left override, so it is displayed on the left of the reversed text (as the spaces of the other parts), and no space separates the end of the override from the text after it. css/CSS2/box-display/block-in-inline-001.description: the test compares the background of an inline box (its content area: the ascent and the descent of the font, 14px + 3px for the 16px default font) with a line of the reference, whose `line-height: normal` adds the line gap of the font (18px), so it only passes with a default font without line gap, while CSS 2 leaves the height of the content area to the user agent (https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS2/visudet.html#inline-non-replaced: "this specification does not specify how"): the default font of the runner (Tinos, the metrics of Times New Roman) has a line gap of 0.67px, rounded to 1px as the other metrics (as Blink), so the box of the reference is 1px taller (Chrome fails it too; Firefox and Safari pass with their default fonts); verified on inline-formatting-context-002.xht, the other tests of the group have the same 1px rows of differences

css/CSS2/floats/floats-wrap-bfc-006.xht.description: the placement beside the floats is the expected one; the difference is the width of the table grid in the second and fourth tables, whose caption (190px and 192px) is wider than their cell (100px): the reference expects a grid of 100px (CSS 2.1, Firefox), but the used min-width of a table is the greater of its min-width, CAPMIN (the largest min-content contribution of its captions) and GRIDMIN (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#computing-the-table-width), so the grid is as wide as the caption. Chrome and Safari fail the same way

css/CSS2/floats/floats-wrap-bfc-with-mar.description: the first block formatting context root of the test (auto width, a margin on the side opposite to the float more negative than the space beside it) is expected to stay beside the float with a border box widened by its negative margin; this contradicts the non-tentative css/CSS2/floats/floats-wrap-bfc-with-margin-001.html (interoperable in Chrome, Edge and Firefox), where an auto-width root whose negative margin on either side, including the side opposite to the float, inflates its border box past the space beside the float is moved below the float; the behavior is unspecified (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/8142 asks to specify the one of -001); fails in every browser

css/CSS2/fonts/font-size-121.xht.description: expects `larger` and `smaller` to be the inverse of each other over six nested steps from `xx-small` and `xx-large` (the sizes of the two rows of glyphs must match); the scale factor of 1.2 of the browsers does not map the keywords onto each other (fails in every browser)

css/CSS2/generated-content/content-177.x.description: the test paints green glyphs exactly over the same red glyphs of the default font: with antialiased text, the partially covered pixels of the edges of a green glyph blend it with the red one under it, so some red remains whatever the positions (the rendering is the expected one: the glyphs are at the same positions, the differences are only these edges, at most 64 = 255/4). Firefox and Safari fail for the same reason; Chrome passes only because wptrunner runs it with `--enable-blink-features=NoFontAntialiasing` (tools/wptrunner/wptrunner/browsers/chrome.py). No specification requires aliased text

css/CSS2/generated-content/content-count.description: `content: counter(c, square)` is the glyph of the square of the counter style, the reference has `square` list markers, which the library draws as shapes, as Blink and Gecko do (the reference differs from the test by 648 pixels in Chromium)

css/CSS2/generated-content/quotes-036.xh.description: the "evil" version of quotes-035.xht (which passes; flag `may`) replaces three of its `div` elements with `br` and `hr` elements styled `display: inline` whose `::before` and `::after` hold the quotes, and expects them not to break the line: a `br` is a forced line break whatever its `display` (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#phrasing-content-3: `br { display-outside: newline; }`), so the text wraps after the `br` elements. Chrome, Firefox and Safari fail too

the balancing of the columns with the early breaks of a grid lanes container (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-break-3/#breaking-rules): the column height is balanced on the content of the strip, which does not take into account the early break that pushes the previous item of the lane with the item whose break before is avoided, so the columns are not tall enough for the items pushed together

the fragmentation in the stacking axis of a grid lanes container with dense packing (`grid-lanes-pack: dense`): the items are placed as in a container that is not fragmented, then fragmented with the flow of the container, so the dense item is not moved before the spanner to honor its `widows` and `orphans`

css/css-break/grid/grid-lanes/grid-lanes.description: the items (some of them span two tracks) are placed again in each column as in Gecko (the only browser that passes), except for the auto-placement cursor of the placement algorithm (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#grid-lanes-layout-algorithm), which the reference, written before the cursor was specified, does not have (with `flow-tolerance: 0px`, Gecko places an item whose tracks tie in the first ones); without the cursor, the library matches the 2 variants

css/css-break/grid/grid-lanes/row-breaks.description: a forced break (`break-before: column`) inside an item of a row with a fixed size (`grid-template-rows: 60px ...`) of a row grid lanes container fragments the row: the rest of the item and of its parallel item continue in the second column, followed by the next row, and the row with the forced break goes to the third column, where the fixed row stays in the first column (the content after the break overflows it into the second column) and the next row follows it there (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#pagination)

the forced break before the second item of a row of a row grid lanes container (`break-before: column`) is lost when the first item of the row has `break-before: avoid`: the row starts in the first column and is broken, where the forced break wins over the avoid value of the same break point and moves the whole row to the second column (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-break-3/#forced-breaks, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#pagination)

an item of a row grid lanes container with a negative block-start margin (`margin-top: -100px`, the second row starts at the top of the second column) is placed by its margin in the fragmentation flow, so it is painted in the first column (50px down) instead of at the start of the fragment of its row, at the top of the second column (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#pagination)

css/css-break/grid/grid-lanes/row-grid-l.description: the item of the second row of the row grid lanes container (stacked in the inline axis) has no width: it is 0px wide (its max-content size) in every browser, so the red background is visible where the test expects it (it fails in every browser)

the fragmentation of a grid lanes container in its grid axis as the one of a grid (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#fragmentation): its rows are not tracks of parallel flows, the items are fragmented as block content; the forced break before the item of the second row (the first in-flow content of the container) is not taken, the row starts in the first column

css/css-color/color-mix-non-srgb-001.htm.description: the references are the colors of the test clipped to sRGB per channel, as the browsers paint them, while the library CSS gamut maps the colors outside of sRGB (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-4/#css-gamut-mapping: the OkLCh chroma is reduced at constant lightness and hue): `color-mix(in lab, red, green)` is painted (160,108,0) instead of the clipped (161,108,0)

css/css-color/currentcolor-003.html.description: the `currentcolor` of `filter: drop-shadow()` on an inline box whose first fragment is on a first line with a `::first-line` color: the filter applies to the box as a whole (all its fragments) with the color of the style of the box, where the shadow of the fragment of the first line is expected in the `::first-line` color (the backgrounds, borders, outlines and shadows of the fragments are painted in it; only Firefox passes this test)

css/css-color/hsl-009.html.description: the reference box only matches when its out-of-sRGB `color(srgb ...)` is clipped channel by channel, as in the browsers, while the colors outside of the gamut of the display must be CSS gamut mapped (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-4/#css-gamut-mapping, which `canvas-srgb-gamut-mapping.html` checks against clipping); the `hsl()` color is a legacy sRGB color whose channels are in [0, 255] (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-4/#css-serialization-of-srgb, its computed value is the clamped `rgb()` color in the browsers), so the two boxes differ once gamut mapped: `hsl(60 5701% 100.96%)` paints (118,118,255) and `color(srgb 0.462304 0.462304 1.556896)` (148,167,255)

css/css-display/run-in/run-in-clear-*.description: the test expects `clear` on a run-in box to apply to the block box it runs in to (CSS 2: "for run-in boxes, this property applies to the final block box to which the run-in box belongs"); CSS Display 3 formats the run-in box "as if originally parented there" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display-3/#run-in-layout), as an inline box, to which `clear` does not apply: the block stays beside the float

css/css-display/run-in/run-in-basic-007..description: the test expects a run-in box to run in to a block box with `overflow: scroll`; in CSS Display 3 a run-in sequence only runs in to "a block box that does not establish a new formatting context" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display-3/#run-in-layout): the header stays in an anonymous block before the scroll container

css/css-display/run-in/run-in-float-betw.description: the run-in box runs in as expected, but the hidden right float ("Some text.") between the run-in box and the block shortens the first line of the block, which wraps earlier than in the reference, which has no float

css/css-display/run-in/run-in-replaced-0.description: the image runs in to the block and is sized as expected (100px square), but the text of the reference ("The blue square should be...") is not the text of the test ("Start of block. The blue square should be..."): the test cannot match

css/css-display/run-in/run-in-contains-i.description: the run-in box runs in as expected, but the reference expects the text of the float (in a table cell in an inline box of the run-in box) on the baseline of the line: the cell is wrapped in an anonymous inline-table whose row has no in-flow content, so its baseline is the bottom of the cell and the float is above the baseline of the line (as a float in a `display: table-cell` box of an inline box in Chrome)

css/css-display/run-in/run-in-contains-t.description: the run-in box runs in as expected, but the reference expects the text of the `display: table-caption` child on the baseline of the line: the caption is wrapped in an anonymous inline-table without row, whose baseline is its bottom margin edge, so the caption is above the baseline of the line (as a `display: table-caption` box in an inline box in Chrome)

css/css-flexbox/abspos/flex-abspos-align.description: an absolutely positioned child with `align-self: safe center` whose containing block is not the flex container, in a flex container whose writing mode is orthogonal to the one of the containing block: the overflowing box is aligned with the start edge of the inset-modified containing block in the cross axis of the flex container (it overflows the inset-modified containing block in that axis); the test expects the box centered there, as if the overflow were checked in the other axis of the containing block (where it fits), which is the behavior of Blink, the only browser that passes this tentative test of an open issue (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/11934, Blink aligns in the inset-modified containing block, Gecko in the static-position rectangle). css/css-flexbox/flex-container-max-conte.description: the reference contradicts the automatic minimum size of the items (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-flexbox-1/#min-size-auto): for the items that cannot grow with a flex basis of 0.2ch (cases 13 to 15 of the rows, and of the columns with 0.2em) it draws a 0.2ch-wide item, where an item is never smaller than its content-based minimum size (its min-content size, 1ch, or its specified size when smaller, 0.4ch), so its contribution and its used size are at least 0.4ch or 1ch (as the library renders them); the case 11 of the columns (`flex: 0 1 2em; height: 0.4em`) expects a container of 0.4em, where the contribution of the item is the larger of its max-content size (1em) and its preferred size (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-flexbox-1/#intrinsic-item-contributions; the reference of the same row case uses that contribution, 3ch). The column cases expect the block size of the container from the "Ideal Algorithm" of https://drafts.csswg.org/css-flexbox-1/#intrinsic-main-sizes, which the specification marks as not Web-compatible (w3c/csswg-drafts#8884, the Web-compatible algorithm is not written yet); the library, as the browsers, gives an auto-height column container the sum of the hypothetical main sizes of its items, so the cases 02, 04 to 06, 10, 12, 17, 20, 21, 23 and 24 of the columns differ too (e.g. `flex: 2em` gives a 2em container where the reference has the 1em contribution of the item). No browser passes.

css/css-fonts/matching/fixed-stretch-sty.description: the test relies on rasterizer precision that OpenType leaves to the implementation: the instances the matching selects (`wght` 700 of variabletest_matching.ttf) are not exactly the glyphs of the reference: the gvar deltas of `wght` 600, 700 and 800 give bars 1200.02, 1400.04 or 1599.99 units long (HarfBuzz hb-vector gives the same outline) where the default glyphs of the reference are 1200, 1400 and 1600 units long, so the antialiased edge pixel differs by 1; the browsers pass because their rasterizers round outlines to 1/64 pixel, which the OpenType specification does not require (Font Variations overview, "Variation data precision": "this specification has no other requirements for instance coordinates, scaled deltas or derived instance values to be rounded")

css/css-gaps/flex/fragmentation/flex-gap.description: the reference is a rendering of Blink whose gap decorations are not in the gaps between the items they separate, which contradicts https://drafts.csswg.org/css-gaps-1/#layout-painting (a column rule is painted in the column gap, along the items or tracks on both sides of it, in each fragment): a row flex container with a specified block size whose two lines are separated by a forced break: the column rule between the items of a line runs across its line, which is stretched (80px), in each fragment; the reference (Blink) has rules of 30px, the block size of the items: at the start of the first fragment, and 50px after the start of the second one, whose items are at its start (the rule of Blink is not beside the items: not reproduced)

css/css-gaps/grid/fragmentation/grid-gap.description: the reference is a rendering of Blink whose gap decorations are not in the gaps between the items they separate, which contradicts https://drafts.csswg.org/css-gaps-1/#layout-painting (a column rule is painted in the column gap, along the items or tracks on both sides of it, in each fragment): a grid with a block-start padding of 20px in columns of 10px: the padding is not broken, the row is in the second column in the test and in the reference, and the column rule of the test is between its two items; the reference (Blink) has the rule in the third column, at the offset of the row in the container before its fragmentation, without the items (not reproduced)

css/css-gaps/grid/subgrid/fragmentation/.description: the reference is a rendering of Blink that depends on how Blink groups the tracks: a grid with a definite block size (140px, five rows of 1fr separated by gaps of 10px, columns of 80px) whose rows 2 to 4 are spanned by a subgrid and whose row 5 has an item: the gap between the rows 3 and 4, which the subgrid spans across, starts at the break and disappears; the library moves up the row right after it (row 4, which has no item), Blink moves up the first row of the next set of tracks (row 5: a set groups the adjacent tracks of one track definition, here repeat(5, 1fr), between the lines where items start or end), so the item of row 5 starts 10px earlier, over the visible gap before it (an artifact of the sets of Blink: with five separate track definitions, Blink would move row 4). https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-2/#pagination truncates the gap at the break, and the track right after it (row 4) starts the next fragment, as the library lays it out

the test (a grid with baseline self-aligned and content-aligned items, fragmented in three columns) is rendered as expected, but its reference is not (not a test bug: Chrome and Firefox render both the same way). The reference is made of two grids with rows of 0px that hold hidden items of `height: 0` (2px with their borders) whose two lines overflow them at the end of the first column: these grid items are sliced at the end of the first column (17px there and 3px in the second column: the break between their lines breaks their box), the first grid is 106px tall instead of 102px, and the second grid starts in the second column, where the browsers keep the items 2px tall in the first column (their overflowing lines continue in the next column) and start the second grid in the first column. css/css-masking/clip-path/animations/cli.description: the coverage of the antialiased edges is the exact area of the pixels, which differs slightly from the one of the browsers the fuzziness of the test is tuned for: 628 pixels of the edge of the clip differ (by up to 2), 480 are allowed

css/css-masking/clip-path/clip-path-inli.description: the coverage of the antialiased edge of the clip (`border-box` with a `border-radius` of 50%) matches the `circle(50%)` of the reference, but the red outline that the clip hides is painted under the edge pixels before they are clipped: 364 pixels of the edge are tinted by up to 63 levels, where 62 levels on 332 pixels are allowed

css/css-masking/mask-image/backdrop-filt.description: the mask image and the probe image that ends the test are served after 10 s (`pipe=trickle(d10)`), the timeout of a reftest without `<meta name=timeout content=long>`: the `reftest-wait` class is removed after the timeout

css/css-masking/clip-path/clip-path-elem.description: the reference places the green box with `margin-top: 50%`, a percentage of the width of the containing block (400px of the 800px wide page, then 392.5px once the vertical scrollbar that the overflowing box causes appears), not of its height: the test clips the bottom half of the page (from 300px) as its assertion says; fails in every browser

css/css-masking/clip-path/clip-path-url-.description: a `clip-path: url()` that references a clipPath element of another document that is still loading (`support/resources.svg?pipe=trickle(d10)#circleClip`) is an unresolved reference, which does not clip (the red box is painted), while the tentative test expects an empty clip path (everything clipped) while the resource is loading; only Chrome passes

css/css-masking/mask-image/backdrop-filt.description: an element with several `mask-image` layers is expected to be entirely masked while one of the mask images is still loading (`url(...?pipe=trickle(d1000))`), a behavior that CSS Masking does not specify (tentative test); the library ignores the pending layer and paints the element with the other layer (`linear-gradient(black, black)`), so it is fully visible; only Chrome passes

css/css-masking/mask-image/mask-image-mu.description: an element with several `mask-image` layers is expected to be entirely masked while one of the mask images is still loading (`url(...?pipe=trickle(d1000))`), a behavior that CSS Masking does not specify (tentative test); the library ignores the pending layer and paints the element with the other layer (`linear-gradient(black, black)`), so it is fully visible; only Chrome passes

css/css-multicol/multicol-nested-014.htm.description: a float in a multi-column container that is nested in another one and fragmented by the outer columns: the floats are only pushed alone to the next column (by a new layout of the strip) in the containers that are not nested, so the float and the monolithic content after it, which are at the same position of the inner strip, are both moved to the next outer column, where the float is expected to stay in the next two columns of the first row

css/css-multicol/multicol-nested-016.htm.description: a nested multi-column container (5 inner columns of 10px) that starts 70px down the first outer column (30px left): the 60px block fills the inner columns 1 and 2, and the three lines (inline-blocks 30px tall and 500% wide) cannot start the third inner column without violating `orphans: 2`/`widows: 2`, so the row ends after the second inner column and the lines and the last block are in the first inner column of the second outer column, as the comment of the test describes (the second outer column is all green). The inner columns 3 to 5 of the first outer column (30x30px) then show the red background of the outer container, where the reference is a filled green square: placing the lines in these columns (which would cover them) leaves the second outer column red instead, so the layout of the browsers that pass (Blink) is not reproduced by any analyzed placement

css/css-overflow/clip-003.html.description: the test depends on overlay scrollbars: with classic scrollbars (15px), the vertical scrollbar of the `overflow: auto` wrapper narrows its scrollport to 35px, the 50px wide `.outer` child then overflows it horizontally and a horizontal scrollbar appears too (and conversely in the last case), while the reference uses `overflow: hidden scroll`; Chrome and Safari fail too, only Firefox passes; css-overflow-3: "Scrollbars which are always placed in a scrollbar gutter, consuming space when present, are called classic scrollbars" and "Whether classic scrollbars or overlay scrollbars are used [...] is UA defined" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow-3/#scrollbar-gutter-property): the comment of the test "there should be a vertical scrollbar, but not a horizontal one" only holds with overlay scrollbars

css/css-overflow/line-clamp/block-ellips.description: the line-clamp container is `5ch` wide and the reference box `5.1ch` (fails in every browser)

the test sizes its box in `ch` for Arabic letters that are as wide as the `0` of the monospace font (a monospace Arabic font): the glyphs of the Arabic fallback font (Scheherazade, as the proportional fonts of the browsers) are narrower, so one more word fits on the clamped line before the ellipsis (fails in every browser)

the test sizes its box in `ch` for Arabic letters that are as wide as the `0` of the monospace font (a monospace Arabic font): the glyphs of the Arabic fallback font (Scheherazade, as the proportional fonts of the browsers) are narrower, so one more word fits on the clamped line before the ellipsis (fails in every browser)

css/css-overflow/margin-block-end-scroll.description: fails in every browser: the test expects the scrollable overflow area of the scroll container to include the block-end margin (100px) of a `p` that overflows its fixed-height parent, so that `scrollTop = 200` hides the red box; the margin is not part of the scrollable overflow (maximum `scrollTop` 101, 99px of red stay visible)

css/css-overflow/overflow-clip-margin-01.description: the reference rounds the top-right corner of the overflow clip edge with a 27.52px radius, the shape of a spread of 20px from the padding edge (radius 10px, ratio 0.5: 10 + 20 * (1 - 0.5^3) = 27.5, as Chrome); https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow-4/#overflow-clip-margin shapes it "exactly the same way as an outer box-shadow with a spread radius of the same cumulative offset from the box's border edge": 15px from the border radius of 15px (ratio 1), a 30px radius, which the test paints (only the pixels of that corner differ; the other corners agree). Fails in Firefox (wpt.fyi)

css/css-overflow/overflow-clip-margin-vi.description: the reference expects the corners of the overflow clip edge of `overflow-clip-margin: border-box 5px` to be the radii of the padding edge (5px for the 15px top right corner with a 10px border) outset by 15px with the shadow spread formula (15.55px, the shape of Chrome), while css-overflow-4 says "The overflow clip edge is shaped in the corners exactly the same way as an outer box-shadow with a spread radius of the same cumulative offset from the box's border edge" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow-4/#overflow-clip-margin): the 15px border radius spread by 5px is 20px, which the library renders (only the top right corner of the first box differs; the `padding-box` and `content-box` cases match); only Chrome passes

css/css-overflow/text-overflow-028.html.description: 1 antialiased pixel differs by 1 from the reference: the width of the div is 10ch of Cousine 13px (78.0078125px), its overflow clip is snapped to the pixel (86px), and the ink of the glyph `A` at the end of the line ends at 86.0078px: the antialiasing of that 0.0078px sliver (1/255) is painted in the reference but clipped in the test. The browsers position the glyphs on whole pixels (or their layout unit, 1/64px, truncates the width to 78px)

css/css-overflow/text-overflow-string-01.description: the reference gets the inter-script spacing of `text-autospace: normal` (1/8ic: 3.75px) between the last Ahem letter of the span and the ideograph or the kana that follows it, which the string of `text-overflow` of the test, placed after the clipped text, does not get: the string of the reference is 3.75px to the right; and the string of the test is 40.9px wide (the space and the emoji of the emoji font of the test are 20.9px wide, for the `1ch + 13px` that the test adds to `2ic`), 0.9px more than the room left after the four Ahem glyphs, so one more glyph is replaced (fails in every browser)

css/css-overflow/text-overflow-string-02.description: the reference gets the inter-script spacing of `text-autospace: normal` (1/8ic: 3.75px) between the last Ahem letter of the span and the ideograph or the kana that follows it, which the string of `text-overflow` of the test, placed after the clipped text, does not get: the string of the reference is 3.75px to the right (passes in Firefox only, which has no `text-autospace`)

the reference gets the inter-script spacing of `text-autospace: normal` (1/8ic: 3.75px) between the last Ahem letter of the span and the ideograph or the kana that follows it, which the string of `text-overflow` of the test, placed after the clipped text, does not get: the string of the reference is 3.75px to the right (passes in Firefox only, which has no `text-autospace`)

css/css-position/multicol/vlr-ltr-rtl-in.description: the containing block formed by an inline box whose `direction` is not the one of its block container: the test (tentative) expects the start and end edges of the fragments of the inline box in the direction of the block container, as Blink computes them; the rectangle is computed in the writing mode of the inline box, as CSS Position 3 says ("the block-start and inline-start content edges of the first box fragment of the ancestor, and the block-end and inline-end content edges of the last box fragment", the 'direction' of the ancestor in CSS 2.1 §10.1); Firefox and Safari fail it too

css/css-position/multicol/vlr-rtl-ltr-in.description: the containing block formed by an inline box whose `direction` is not the one of its block container: the test (tentative) expects the start and end edges of the fragments of the inline box in the direction of the block container, as Blink computes them; the rectangle is computed in the writing mode of the inline box, as CSS Position 3 says ("the block-start and inline-start content edges of the first box fragment of the ancestor, and the block-end and inline-end content edges of the last box fragment", the 'direction' of the ancestor in CSS 2.1 §10.1); Firefox and Safari fail it too
