css/css-position/multicol/vrl-rtl-ltr-in.description: the containing block formed by an inline box whose `direction` is not the one of its block container: the test (tentative) expects the start and end edges of the fragments of the inline box in the direction of the block container, as Blink computes them; the rectangle is computed in the writing mode of the inline box, as CSS Position 3 says ("the block-start and inline-start content edges of the first box fragment of the ancestor, and the block-end and inline-end content edges of the last box fragment", the 'direction' of the ancestor in CSS 2.1 §10.1); Firefox and Safari fail it too

css/css-position/overlay/overlay-transit.description: the runner runs the event loop until it is idle before the screenshot, advancing its virtual clock to the next timer: a 60s `overlay` transition would end before it

`showPopover()` then `hidePopover()` in the same task start no `overlay` transition: there is no style change event between them (the before-change style has `overlay: none`); Blink updates the styles in `showPopover()` (to find the focus delegate), so its before-change style has `overlay: auto` and the green `::backdrop` stays rendered; fails in Firefox and Safari

the dialog closed while its `overlay` and `display` transition stays rendered in the top layer with its `::backdrop`, but it is no longer `:modal` (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#close-the-dialog sets is modal to false): it loses the `position: fixed; inset-block: 0` of `dialog:modal` and is painted at the top of the viewport instead of centered, and it keeps the focus (focus ring) where the reference blurs it; Blink centers it (fails in Firefox and Safari)

the runner runs the event loop until it is idle before the screenshot, advancing its virtual clock to the next timer: the 60s `overlay` transition of the popover shown second ends (it is then rendered in the top layer, red over the green popover), where the browsers take the screenshot after the load, while the transition delays the rendering in the top layer

css/css-position/sticky/position-sticky-.description: the boxes are painted at their fractional positions: the text of the third sticky cell is at x = 130.14px in the test (the width `64.138px` of the first cell) and at 130px in the reference, so its antialiased edges differ; Chrome paints each sticky box in a composited layer whose offset is snapped to the pixel grid (the test is for a rounding bug of these layers); Firefox and Safari fail it too

css/css-pseudo/active-selection-041.html.description: the selection of a replaced element (`img::selection`): the highlight is only painted over the text

css/css-pseudo/first-letter-001.html.description: the white inline box of the no-break space covers its content area (56px for the 50px font), not the line box (58px with `line-height: normal`): 1px of the red background of the block is visible above and below it; fails in every browser

css/css-pseudo/marker-letter-spacing.htm.description: the references expect the `letter-spacing` after the last character of an outside marker (as Chrome, the second reference) or only after its suffix (as Firefox, the first reference); the spacing "is not applied at the beginning or end of a line" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#letter-spacing-property): the outside markers, which are the only content of the line of their box, are 25px narrower

css/css-pseudo/marker-line-break.html.description: the test expects the text of a marker to wrap with `line-break: anywhere`, `overflow-wrap: anywhere` or `word-break: break-all`, but the user agent style sheet of CSS Lists gives `white-space: pre` to `::marker` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists-3/#ua-stylesheet), which forbids the soft wraps; only Chrome passes

css/css-pseudo/marker-overflow-wrap.html.description: the test expects the text of a marker to wrap with `line-break: anywhere`, `overflow-wrap: anywhere` or `word-break: break-all`, but the user agent style sheet of CSS Lists gives `white-space: pre` to `::marker` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists-3/#ua-stylesheet), which forbids the soft wraps; only Chrome passes

css/css-pseudo/marker-word-break.html.description: the test expects the text of a marker to wrap with `line-break: anywhere`, `overflow-wrap: anywhere` or `word-break: break-all`, but the user agent style sheet of CSS Lists gives `white-space: pre` to `::marker` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists-3/#ua-stylesheet), which forbids the soft wraps; only Chrome passes

css/css-pseudo/selection-input-011.html.description: the selection of the value is highlighted with `::selection` as in the reference, but the reference focuses its `input` (it is painted with a focus ring): the test relies on `select()` giving the focus to the control, as in Chrome, which the standard does not specify (the only different pixels are the ones of the focus ring); Firefox and Safari fail too

css/css-pseudo/selection-over-highlight-.description: the background of `::selection` covers the content area of the text (ascent + descent), 1px shorter than the line box that the reference fills (the browsers extend the selection to the line box). Extending it to the line box fixes this test but breaks 24 passing tests of css-pseudo (`highlight-painting-*`, `active-selection-*`, `selection-intercharacter-*`, `highlight-cascade/*`) whose references paint the background of a span (the content area)

css/css-ruby/block-ruby-001.html.description: as in Gecko, no line break between the bases of a ruby segment without annotation (the reference uses `white-space: nowrap`): each base is a ruby column

css/css-ruby/block-ruby-002.html.description: the inlinification of the computed `display` of the block-level ruby containers in a ruby container (`block ruby` instead of `ruby`): the boxes are inlinified, not the computed values

css/css-ruby/break-within-bases/*.description: the line breaks inside the ruby bases (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ruby-1/#break-within): a ruby column is a unit of the line breaking (its items are the items of its bases followed by the items of its annotations), so breaking it needs the bases and the annotations to be broken at different positions on each line; Chrome only

css/css-ruby/collapse-trailing-whitespac.description: the reference pairs the base `n` with the annotation `n`, which is hidden (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ruby-1/#autohide: its text content is the text content of its base, as in Gecko), where the base `n ` of the test (with a space) keeps its annotation; the test passes in Chrome, which does not hide annotations (the trailing space of the base is removed at the end of the line as expected)

css/css-ruby/rbc-rtc-basic-001.html.description: the column of an annotation without base (the second annotation of a ruby with one base) does not overhang the text after the ruby, where the column of the reference, whose base is a no-break space, overhangs the white space that follows it by 7.5px (`ruby-overhang: auto`): the next two rubies are 7.5px to the right (passes in Firefox only)

css/css-ruby/ruby-bidi-003.html.description: the extent of an annotation is the content area of its text (the ascent and descent of its font), but the margin box of an atomic inline: the block of the reference, inlinified to an inline-block, is as tall as the `line-height: 1` of the `rt`, so the annotation of the test is 4px taller and its base 2px lower; the Hebrew characters have no glyph in the fonts of the runner

css/css-ruby/ruby-box-generation-*.description: the reference assumes that the annotations do not overhang (`ruby-overhang: auto`: they "may overhang adjacent content"): the annotations wider than their base overhang the inter-segment white space before and after their column (`ruby-overhang: auto`, as Blink), where the reference (made for Gecko, which does not overhang) puts that white space in a ruby base of its own segment, which is not overhung: the columns `l` (002) and `t` (005) are 0.9px narrower than in the reference (passes in Firefox only)

css/css-ruby/ruby-inlinize-recursive-sim.description: the extent of an annotation is the content area of its text (9px), but the margin box of an atomic inline (8px, the `line-height: 1` of the `rt`): the inlinified blocks of the test are inline-blocks (`display: block` becomes `inline flow-root`, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display-3/#inlinify), so the annotation that only contains them is 1px shorter than the one of the reference, whose text is in an inline box

css/css-ruby/ruby-intrinsic-isize-002.ht.description: the text of each ruby base is shaped separately, so the kerning pair across two adjacent bases is lost: `<rb>ABC</rb><rb>DEF</rb>` is 63.125px wide (32.898px + 30.227px) where the single text `ABCDEF` of the reference is 62.242px (the serif font of the runner kerns `C` and `D` by -0.883px), so the second block is 0.883px wider and the blocks after it are shifted (the shaping across inline box boundaries without change of formatting, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-3/#boundary-shaping, is not applied across ruby bases)

css/css-ruby/ruby-justification-001.html.description: the expansion of the ruby columns by the justification of their line (`text-align: justify`): they are not expanded, and the annotation (an inline-block of 100px in an `rtc`) spans the two bases, which are centered in its column; the reference has no annotation and the bases at the start of the line. Chromium 152 matches the reference because it lays out `rtc` as an inline box (it does not implement `ruby-text-container`): the extra space of the justified line goes to the space before it

css/css-ruby/ruby-overhang-spaces-013.ht.description: the test is made for a default font whose Latin `a` is half an ideograph wide (the Japanese fonts that the browsers use for `lang=ja`): with tab stops of `1ic`, the tabs before and after the ruby are then 0.5ic wide and the annotation overhangs them on both sides; the `a` of the default font of the runner is 0.44ic wide, so the tab after the column does not end on the tab stop that the reference assumes (and the overhang used by the line breaking, 11.1px, differs from the one of the positioned line, 20px: the box is 8.9px wider than its content); passes in Chrome only

css/css-ruby/ruby-overhang-spaces-019.ht.description: the test is made for a default font whose U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT is fullwidth (the Japanese fonts that the browsers use for `lang=ja`), with a blank quarter on each side that the annotation overhangs (5px); the middle dot of the default font of the runner is proportional (6.7px), and the annotation overhangs a quarter of it (1.7px): the test is 6.7px wider than the reference; passes in Chrome only

css/css-ruby/ruby-overhang-spaces-vertic.description: the Japanese fallback font of the runner (M+ 1p) has no vertical metrics (`vhea`, `vmtx`): its upright glyphs advance by the ascent and the descent of the font (1.395em) in vertical text, while the brackets that are set sideways advance by 1em; the reference assumes that the blank half of a bracket is half of the advance of an ideograph (the brackets set sideways are overhung by 10px, the reference expects 13.95px)

the Japanese fallback font of the runner (M+ 1p) has no vertical metrics (`vhea`, `vmtx`): its upright glyphs advance by the ascent and the descent of the font (1.395em) in vertical text, while the brackets that are set sideways advance by 1em; the reference assumes that the blank half of a bracket is half of the advance of an ideograph (the brackets set sideways are overhung by 10px, the reference expects 13.95px); the font has no `vhal` feature either

css/css-scroll-snap/scroll-target-align-.description: the optional use of the scroll snap alignment of the target (`scroll-snap-align: center`) by the scroll to the fragment when the scroll container has `scroll-snap-type: none` (test flagged `may`): the target is aligned at the start of the scrollport (with its `scroll-margin` and the `scroll-padding`), the green stripe is in the first quarter instead of the second one; only Firefox passes

the optional use of the scroll snap alignment of the target (`scroll-snap-align: center`) by `scrollIntoView()` when the scroll container has `scroll-snap-type: none` (test flagged `may`): the target is aligned at the start of the scrollport (with its `scroll-margin` and the `scroll-padding`), the green stripe is in the first quarter instead of the second one; only Firefox passes

css/css-sizing/aspect-ratio/replaced-ele.description: the frames of the videos are not decoded: the media backend of the tests gives an opaque black frame, painted with `object-fit: contain` in the middle of the green box, where the test expects the green frame of the video

css/css-shapes/shape-outside/shape-image.description: the float area of the image with `shape-margin` is the expected one (the text is at 120px), but the test paints the 100x100 image, whose right half is transparent, scaled to 200x200 and compares it with a solid rectangle: the interpolation of the scaled image blurs the edge of its opaque half (400 pixels differ slightly); the test fails in all the browsers

css/css-sizing/max-content-input-001.htm.description: expects `height: max-content` and `width: max-content` on `<input>` and `<textarea>` to be the size of their text (7 lines, 11ch, 27 columns) instead of their intrinsic size (`size`, `rows`, `cols`); fails in every browser

css/css-tables/tentative/paint/backgroun.description: 19 pixels on the hard color stop at 75% of the `linear-gradient(45deg, ...)` differ by 23 (silver 192 and darkgray 169 swapped): the line of that stop passes exactly through the centers of a diagonal of pixels (x - y = -20 in the 50x230 gradient box), so the side of the stop each center falls on depends on the rounding of its position on the gradient line, which is computed from the background positioning area of the column (translated into each cell) in the test and from the box of a div in the reference; no fuzziness is allowed

css/css-tables/visibility-collapse-colsp.description: the clipping of the contents of a cell that spans a collapsed column or row (`visibility: collapse`) to the shrunk box of the cell (css-tables-3 #visibility-collapse-cell-rendering): the overflowing text is painted; fails in every browser

css/css-tables/visibility-collapse-rowsp.description: the clipping of the contents of a cell that spans a collapsed column or row (`visibility: collapse`) to the shrunk box of the cell (css-tables-3 #visibility-collapse-cell-rendering): the overflowing text is painted; fails in every browser

css/css-text-decor/invalidation/selectio.description: the `::selection` rule of the test draws black wavy lines (`text-decoration-color: black`) and the element of the reference green ones (`text-decoration-color: green`); fails in every browser

css/css-text-decor/text-decoration-color.description: the last line expects the underline of a text with `-webkit-text-stroke-color: LinkText` to be painted in the color of the stroke; `text-decoration-color` is `currentcolor`, the black `color` of the text (only Safari passes)

css/css-text-decor/text-decoration-skip-.description: `text-decoration-skip-ink: auto` for the upright glyphs of vertical text (`text-orientation: upright`): the ink is skipped by the lines of the horizontal text and of the sideways glyphs only, so the underline crosses the upright glyphs; fails in every browser

`text-decoration-skip-ink: auto` for the upright glyphs of vertical text (`text-orientation: upright`): the ink is skipped by the lines of the horizontal text and of the sideways glyphs only, so the underline crosses the upright glyphs; fails in every browser

css/css-text-decor/text-decoration-wavy-.description: the wave is continuous across the descendant elements (its phase is anchored to the coordinates), but each fragment paints its part as a separate path: 8 antialiased pixels at the joins differ by at most 9 from the single path of the reference

css/css-text-decor/text-emphasis-punctua.description: the emphasis marks extend their line box by a fractional amount (1.5px above the half-leading of `line-height: 2`: the two lines of the test are 33.5px tall), where the two lines of the reference are 34px and 32px tall: the second line is 0.5px higher than in the reference and its text is antialiased at another position; fails in every browser

css/css-text-decor/text-decoration-decor.description: the transparent `x` lowered by `vertical-align: -10px` touches the underline of its decorating box (the top of its x-height is 0.3px inside the 1px line), and `text-decoration-skip-ink: auto` skips the underline across the glyph (8px); the `x` of the reference is on the baseline and its underline has no gap

css/css-text-decor/text-decoration-inset.description: the reference keeps the underline blue under the selected text, but the decorations of the originating element are painted in the `color` of `::selection` in the selected part (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo-4/#highlight-painting, WPT `css/css-pseudo/selection-originating-decoration-color.html`): the middle of the underline is green; its insets are the expected ones (the line goes from 28px to 252px)

the `-webkit-box-decoration-break` alias, which the test uses for WebKit (it is in no specification): the declaration is dropped and the box keeps `slice`, so the 20% inset refers to the decorated text of both lines (200px) and only applies at the start of the first line and at the end of the last one

css/css-text/hanging-punctuation/hanging.description: the test is rendered as expected (the parentheses hang), but its reference emulates the hanging with an inline box that has negative margins and relies on the negative inline-end margin to bring back on the line the last word, which overflows it by 1em: as in Chrome and Firefox, the content of an inline box must fit on the line before its negative inline-end margin is applied (WPT css/css-grid/firefox-bug-1881495.html, which Safari fails), so the line of the reference is broken before the last word (Safari, the only browser with `hanging-punctuation`, is the only one that passes)

the reference fits 11 fullwidth characters on a line of 10em thanks to the trimming of the fullwidth punctuation (`text-spacing-trim: normal`: the opening bracket after the ideographic comma and the closing bracket at the end of the line are set half-width); the Japanese fallback font of the runner (M+ 1p) has no `halt` feature, so its punctuation is not trimmed (as in Chrome) and the line of the test breaks one character earlier; passes in Chrome only, with a system font that has the feature

css/css-text/hyphens/hyphens-auto-004.ht.description: the reference puts the ideographic spaces (U+3000) after `regulation` on a line of their own, as Chrome and Safari do; with `white-space: normal`, "if there remains any sequence of white space, other space separators, and/or preserved tabs at the end of a line", "the UA must hang this sequence (unconditionally)" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-3/#white-space-phase-2): they hang at the end of the second line, after `lation`, as `css/css-text/white-space/trailing-ideographic-space-001.html` and `-002` require (which this engine passes and every browser fails); Firefox fails this test too

css/css-text/hyphens/hyphens-auto-contro.description: the runner has no monospace font with a U+2010 HYPHEN glyph like its U+002D: the bundled monospace font (Cousine) has no U+2010, the hyphen is the U+2010 of a fallback font (Tinos), the reference uses U+002D

css/css-text/hyphens/i18n/hyphens-i18n-a.description: the Dutch hyphenation patterns of hyph-utf8 have no hyphenation opportunity before the diminutive suffix of `cafeetje` (only `ca-feetje`), so its spelling change at the break (`café-tje`, implemented for the soft hyphens, `hyphens-i18n-manual-001`) is not used; no browser passes

there is no Hungarian hyphenation dictionary (the patterns of hyph-utf8 are under copyleft licenses), so `Összeg` is not hyphenated automatically (the spelling change `Ösz-szeg` is implemented for the soft hyphens, `hyphens-i18n-manual-002`); no browser passes
there is no Uyghur hyphenation dictionary (hyph-utf8 has none), so the word is not hyphenated automatically; no browser passes

css/css-text/hyphens/i18n/hyphens-i18n-m.description: the Uyghur word fits in the `4ch` of the box with the Arabic fallback font of the runner (Scheherazade, narrower than the fonts of the browsers), so it is not broken at the soft hyphen (where the hyphen would be U+0640 ARABIC TATWEEL); no browser passes

css/css-text/hyphens/i18n/hyphens-i18n-a.description: there is no Cree hyphenation dictionary (hyph-utf8 has none), so the syllabics are not hyphenated automatically (the hyphen after the Canadian syllabics is U+1400 CANADIAN SYLLABICS HYPHEN); the runner has no font for the Canadian syllabics; no browser passes

css/css-text/letter-spacing/letter-spaci.description: the test predates `text-autospace`: with its initial value `normal`, 1/8ic of inter-script spacing is added between a digit and an ideograph of `12三456七89` ("this property is additive with the word-spacing and letter-spacing properties"), so `12三` and `七89` are 5.125em wide and do not fit in the 5em box as the reference expects (the lines break next to the ideographs); the rest of the test matches, and the test with `text-autospace: no-autospace` is identical to its reference (fails in every browser)

the test expects a line to break between a U+200B and the preserved space after it (the space starts the next line, with its letter spacing); UAX #14 (LB7, LB8: `ZW SP* ÷`) only allows the break after the spaces that follow the U+200B, so the space hangs at the end of the line and the next line starts with the `x` (fails in every browser)

the reference is 2em wide (its two characters have no `letter-spacing`), the float of the test is 3em wide: two characters and the spacing of 1em between them (the spacing after the last character of a line is not applied, the invisible formatting characters that follow it being ignored), all green. Fails in every browser

the test expects the letter spacing model of the previous drafts of CSS Text 3: the spacing between two characters is the one of the innermost element that contains both of them (rendered inside that element, after the text-empty inline boxes between the characters). The current drafts (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#letter-spacing-property) add half of the spacing of each character on each of its sides, which gives other positions at the boundaries of the elements of this test, and note that the tests need to be updated; this engine adds the spacing of the element of a character after it, as the browsers (fails in every browser)

css/css-text/line-breaking/line-breaking.description: `…` is replaced by U+2026 by the HTML parser (the numeric character references of the C1 controls are mapped to Windows-1252): there is no U+0085 in the document and no forced line break after the fifth square (the other characters of the classes BK and NL break the lines); fails in every browser

U+034F COMBINING GRAPHEME JOINER is a combining mark (line breaking class CM) since Unicode 15.1, no longer GL: it attaches to the character before it, and there is a soft wrap opportunity between it and the atomic inline (fails in every browser)

css/css-text/text-align/text-align-match.description: the test expects the last line of an element with `text-align: match-parent; text-align-all: left` to be aligned to the right, the start of its right-to-left parent; `text-align-last: match-parent` "computes to its parent's computed value", which is `auto`, so the last line follows the `text-align-all: left` of the element (Firefox and Safari pass, Chrome fails)

css/css-text/text-autospace/text-autospa.description: the test expects inter-script spacing between the ideographs and the ASCII punctuation `!` and `#` of a Chinese text; `text-autospace: normal` is `ideograph-alpha ideograph-numeric` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#text-autospace-property), which only separates the ideographs from the non-ideographic letters and numerals, and `punctuation` only has an effect in French (passes in Chrome only)

css/css-text/text-fit/text-underline-off.description: the reference of the `per-line-all` case with `text-underline-offset: auto` underlines the text of a `span` of 40px from a block container of 20px, so its underline is at the position of the font at 20px, where the test has a line scaled by 2 whose boxes (also the root inline box, which is the decorating box) have a used font size of 40px: the underline is at the position of the font at 40px (in Blink the automatic underline position does not depend on the font size; the other cases of the test match)

css/css-text/text-spacing-trim/text-spac.description: the vertical variants (`vrl`) expect the classification of Chrome, from the glyphs of the font in the vertical flow: no trimming of a fullwidth parenthesis next to a fullwidth colon or semicolon that the font keeps upright (`国；（国` and `国）；国` in Japanese, the colons and semicolons in Chinese), as if they were neither closing nor middle dot punctuation. "The UA must classify fullwidth colon punctuation [U+FF1A and U+FF1B] and fullwidth dot punctuation under either the fullwidth closing punctuation category or the fullwidth middle dot punctuation category" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#fullwidth-ambiguous; the table there makes the colons closing punctuation in vertical Simplified Chinese, and middle dots in Japanese and Traditional Chinese, the colon and the semicolon alike): the engine classifies them by language and trims the parenthesis next to them; the horizontal variants pass (passes in Chrome only)

the last row expects the line `国国国国“` to be broken before the opening quotation mark that ends the text, so that it starts a line and is trimmed (its reference sets it with `halt` without a break); UAX #14 forbids that break since Unicode 15.1 (rule LB19a: `× QU (eot)`, the quotation mark is not surrounded by East Asian characters), so the quotation mark stays after the last ideograph with its full width (passes in Chrome only)
the test does not set `text-spacing-trim: trim-all` (its reference trims every punctuation with `halt`): it fails in Chrome too

css/css-text/text-transform/text-transfo.description: the reference has `i` (U+0069) for the lowercase of U+0130, whose full case mapping is `i̇` (U+0069 U+0307, SpecialCasing.txt, outside of Turkish and Azeri: https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-3/#text-transform-mapping; the test passes with U+0069 U+0307 in the reference): the two only render alike with a font that removes the dot of the `i` before U+0307, as Doulos SIL, the web font of the test, but `/fonts/DoulosSIL-R.woff` does not exist in WPT, and the fallback font (Arimo) has no U+0307, which comes from another font (9 pixels of the dot differ); fails in every browser

expects the simple uppercase mappings of the Greek letters with a iota subscript (`ᾀ` → `ᾈ`) instead of the full mappings of SpecialCasing.txt (`ἈΙ`) that `text-transform` uses (fails in every browser)

css/css-text/white-space/text-wrap-balan.description: the margin box of the boxes starts at 15.8px (8px + 1ch of the 13px monospace font), so their content starts at 18.8px while their 3px borders are painted on whole pixels (16px to 19px); the `I` of Cousine, drawn from 18.8px, covers 8% of the last pixel of the border in the reference, where the `overflow: hidden` of the test clips it at the pixel-snapped padding edge (19px): 1 pixel differs (Chrome and Firefox, which pass, round the glyph origins to whole pixels or use a font whose ink does not reach the border); a fix needs either glyph origins on whole pixels or clips that are not pixel-snapped, both of which change many other tests

css/css-text/white-space/textarea-pre-wr.description: expects the spaces before the forced line breaks of the value (`XX \nXX `, lines of 3ch in a box of 3ch) to hang, so that the right-aligned `XX` are at the end edge; a preserved space followed by a forced line break hangs conditionally (css-text-3: only when it does not fit), so the lines fill the box and `XX` stay at its start edge; fails in every browser

css/css-text/white-space/trailing-other-.description: the hanging sequence of spaces and other space separators is as wide as the one preserved by `white-space: pre`, but the test expects the background of its inline box (its content area) to fit in the line box of `line-height: 1`: the content area of the default font is 17px high at 16px (its ascent and descent), so the half-leading is -0.5px, floored as in Blink, and the background of the span covers the row of pixels above the line, where the reference has none (fails in every browser)

css/css-text/white-space/white-space-col.description: the segment break at the start of the `span` is preserved by `white-space-collapse: preserve-breaks` as a forced line break (an empty first line); the reference has no such line (fails in every browser)

css/css-text/word-break/word-break-break.description: the test expects no soft wrap opportunity between two U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS (class PR) with `word-break: break-all`; UAX #14 allows it (rule LB31), so the line is broken after the second one, which fits (passes in Chrome only)

the tentative test expects the boundary between the last character of an inline box with `word-break: break-all` and the first character after it (`b|c`) to have no soft wrap opportunity, where the engine applies `break-all` to the character before the boundary (`b` is an ideograph, ID ÷ AL); "which elements' line-break, word-break, and overflow-wrap properties control the determination of soft wrap opportunities at such boundaries is undefined" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-3/#line-break-details); fails in every browser

css/css-text/word-space-transform/word-s.description: the reference expects the spaces inserted by `word-space-transform: space` to collapse with the collapsible spaces next to them and with each other (one space between the letters); the transformation happens "after Phase I: Collapsing and Transformation" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#text-transform-order) and the assert of the test says that the "inserted spaces don't collapse with adjacent ones": `a<wbr> b` has two spaces (fails in every browser, none implements the property)

the declaration of the test is misspelled (`word-space-transfor: space auto-phrase`), so the property is not set and no space can be inserted between the Thai words as the reference expects (fails in every browser)

the test is in two nested `div` elements with `font-size: 2em` each (4em), and its reference in one: the ideographic spaces are inserted as expected, but the text of the test is twice as large as the reference (fails in every browser)

the test expects a space followed by `<wbr>` or U+200B, and `<wbr>` followed by U+200B, to give a single (fullwidth) space: "Word space transformation and text transformation happen after Phase I: Collapsing and Transformation" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#text-transform-order), so the spaces that replace the separators do not collapse with the spaces next to them, as `word-space-transform-002.html` ("inserted spaces don't collapse with adjacent ones", which this engine passes) requires for the same sequences; no browser implements the property

css/css-transforms/animation/translate-a.description: fails in every browser: the `rect` of the reference is 200x200 while the one of the test is 100x100 (both end translated by 100px 100px)

css/css-transforms/perspective-svg-child.description: the 3D transforms of the SVG elements without CSS box (the transforms of the SVG content are 2D affine matrices): the `perspective` of the svg element is not applied to its `rect` child with `transform: translateZ(-200px)`, which is not scaled by 0.5; only Firefox passes

the 3D transforms of the SVG elements without CSS box (the transforms of the SVG content are 2D affine matrices): `transform: perspective(200px) translateZ(-200px)` on a `rect` does not scale it by 0.5; only Firefox passes

css/css-ui/caret-eol-004.tentative.html.description: a selection set by a script is not scrolled into view: the caret at the end of `abcdefghijkl` in an editing host of 5ch with `overflow: hidden` (`selectAllChildren()` then `collapseToEnd()`) is painted at the end of the text, outside of the scrollport, so the rendering is the one of the reference without caret. The test expects the caret at the end of the visible line; only Firefox passes this tentative test.

css/css-ui/compute-kind-widget-no-fallba.description: the test sets, at the author level, every longhand enumerated by `getComputedStyle()` that is not in its own list of the properties that disable the native appearance; the library enumerates `background-position-block` and `background-position-inline` (css-backgrounds-4 logical longhands of `background-position`), which the list of the test does not have, so the `meter` and the `progress` are devolved as specified (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui-4/#appearance-disabling-properties: "if [...] a cascaded value exists [...] for any property that disables native appearance for widgets, then that widget is rendered as a devolved widget", `background-position` is in the list); the browsers pass because they do not support these longhands (`background-repeat` alone does not disable the native appearance anymore)

css/css-ui/outline-color-004.html.description: the outer box has `outline-style: solid` and `outline-color: auto`, which computes to `currentcolor` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui-4/#outline-color: "Otherwise, outline-color: auto computes to currentColor"): the inner box inherits `currentcolor` (`outline-color: inherit`) and paints its focus ring in its own color (red), where the reference expects it to inherit `auto` (the accent color, green); fails in Chrome and Firefox

css/css-values/ch-unit-019.html.description: the icon font of the test has no glyph for `0`, and the test expects `ch` to fall back to 0.5em (1em in upright vertical text), as for a measure that is "impossible or impractical to determine": `ch` is the advance measure of the `0` glyph "in the font used to render it" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-4/#ch), the fallback font that renders the `0` here, whose advance is measurable (0.5em in horizontal text, but 1.1em in upright vertical text, so the second rectangle is 105px wide); only Chrome passes, as it only looks for `0` in the first available font (Firefox and Safari fail)

css/css-view-transitions/japanese-tag.ht.description: the test has no encoding declaration and its view transition names are Japanese: decoded as windows-1252 (UTF-8 is not detected for a document of the network, as in the browsers: `encoding-detection/utf-8.html`), the names contain code points that are not identifier code points (U+00A0, U+0081…), so the declarations and the selectors are invalid; the browsers pass with the same decoding because they accept every non-ASCII code point in an identifier

css/css-view-transitions/inline-with-blo.description: the capture of an inline box split by a block child (its fragments before the block, the block and after it): only its first fragment is painted in the image, whose size is the bounding box of the fragments

css/css-view-transitions/nested/group-ch.description: the test uses `view-transition-group: none`, which the specification does not define (`normal | contain | nearest | <custom-ident>`; Chrome only): the group of the element is nested, and clipped, like the other ones

css/css-view-transitions/scoped/auto-nes.description: the automatic nesting of the groups of a scoped view transition in the group of its root element, which clips them as the root element does (`overflow: clip`): a tentative behavior of Chrome pending csswg-drafts#13420, not in the specification (the `::view-transition` pseudo-element "is exempted from that clip", and the groups are only nested by `view-transition-group`)

css/css-view-transitions/scoped/from-sca.description: the test expects the old image of a root element whose transform is `scale(0)` to be empty (Chrome rasterizes nothing), so that only the new image at half opacity is visible; the specification ignores the transform of a captured element ("the captured image should include [...] some low-quality representation of the contents rather than transparent pixels"): the old and the new images are both painted at half opacity

css/css-view-transitions/scoped/scope-ma.description: the `::view-transition` pseudo-element tree of a scoped view transition whose root element is a MathML `math` element or an outer `svg` element: the layer is only built for the elements whose children are CSS boxes (`BoxTreeBuilder.BuildScopedViewTransitionLayer`), so the yellow element is painted instead of the green overlay

css/css-view-transitions/scoped/scope-re.description: the `::view-transition` pseudo-element tree of a scoped view transition whose root element is a replaced element (`img`, `canvas`, `video`, `iframe`, `embed`, `audio`): the layer is only built for the elements whose children are CSS boxes (`BoxTreeBuilder.BuildScopedViewTransitionLayer`), and the captured element is not painted, so the blue backing shows instead of the green overlay

css/css-view-transitions/scoped/scope-sv.description: the `::view-transition` pseudo-element tree of a scoped view transition whose root element is a MathML `math` element or an outer `svg` element: the layer is only built for the elements whose children are CSS boxes (`BoxTreeBuilder.BuildScopedViewTransitionLayer`), so the yellow element is painted instead of the green overlay

css/css-view-transitions/shadow-part-wit.description: the `view-transition-class` values are not tree-scoped: a class declared in a shadow tree is matched by the selectors of the document

css/css-view-transitions/view-transition.description: the backdrop root (https://drafts.fxtf.org/filter-effects-2/#BackdropRoot) of `view-transition-name`: the `backdrop-filter` of a descendant of the named element filters the content painted behind the named element

css/css-writing-modes/ch-units-vrl-007.h.description: the test expects `height: 5ch` of a cell with `writing-mode: vertical-rl; text-orientation: upright` to be 5 advances of the horizontal `0` (a 50px square); the advance measure of `ch` "is its advance width or height, whichever is in the inline axis of the element" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-4/#ch): the vertical advance of the upright `0` is 1em, so the cell is 100px tall, as in all the browsers (which fail the test)

css/css-writing-modes/wm-propagation-bod.description: the test expects the text of `html::after` to be typeset in the principal writing mode propagated from `body` (sideways for `sideways-*`, upright for `vertical-*` with `text-orientation: upright`); the propagation only changes the used value of the root element (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes-4/#principal-flow: "this does not affect the computed values of writing-mode, direction, or text-orientation of the root element itself"): the pseudo-element inherits the computed `writing-mode` of `html`, so its text has the typographic mode of that value (upright in 042 and 047, sideways in 049 and 054), as in all the browsers (which fail the tests)

html/canvas/element/filters/2d.filter.ca.description: the canvas draws the shadow of the filter on its opaque teal bitmap, which rounds each composited pixel to 8 bits (128 x 254/255 = 127.498 gives 127 where the faint shadow has an alpha of 1/255), as the browsers do; the SVG reference composites the same filter result (rounded to premultiplied 8-bit components as the one of the canvas) on the teal rectangles of the page, which keeps 16 bits per component, and the screenshot converts 127.498 to 128 (`PixelConversions.ToByte` rounds with a bias of 1/256 of a level, so that a tie of 16 bits gives the same byte whether it was rounded once or twice): the teal pixels under the faint edges of the shadows differ by 1 level (1,663 pixels, no fuzziness is allowed)

html/rendering/non-replaced-elements/the.description: the reference renders the annotation of the legend with `display: ruby` as a block with a whole line, but an interlinear annotation container is sized to contain exactly the margin boxes of its annotations (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ruby-1/#interlinear-block), inline boxes as tall as their content area: 1px shorter than the line of the reference; Chrome, Firefox and Safari fail too

html/rendering/replaced-elements/embedde.description: the controls of the media elements are not rendered: an `audio` element with `controls` is an empty box, which the tests expect to differ from a blank page

html/rendering/non-replaced-elements/for.description: tentative test of an open issue (w3c/csswg-drafts#14190) that fails in every browser: it expects `align-content` to position the text of `input`, `textarea` and `select` (here the line of an `input` or of a `select` is always centered, and the lines of a `textarea` start at the top) and `align-content: normal` to center the content of a `button` (here it is at the top)

html/rendering/non-replaced-elements/the.description: a fieldset with `height: 30px` and a 160px legend: the reference expects the block-end border right after the block-start border, which is centered on the legend (a border box of 40px placed 70px lower); as in the browsers (the test fails in Chrome, Firefox and Safari), the border box keeps its specified block size (30px + the borders: 70px) and is painted from the block-start border, 70px lower, so the two borders overlap and nothing is painted over the red box of the test

html/rendering/replaced-elements/images/.description: the reference is the bare image `/css/support/60x60-green.png`, which cannot match a test page with a paragraph of text and the body margins; fails in every browser (here the reference is also blank: image documents are not implemented)

html/rendering/widgets/button-layout/ano.description: the test expects the content of a `display: grid` `button` at the top, as in Chrome and Firefox; the user agent style sheet of the HTML Standard gives the buttons `align-content: center`, which centers the row track of a grid button (as in Safari)

html/rendering/widgets/button-layout/inp.description: 2 pixels of the ellipsis: the label of an `input` button is elided by the painter of the form controls, the one of the `button` of the reference by the inline layout, which place the ellipsis a fraction of a pixel apart at the 13.333px font of the controls

html/rendering/widgets/the-select-elemen.description: the label of a drop-down `<select>` with native appearance from its first child `<button>` (whatwg/html#12474, an open issue: the HTML Standard renders the label of the selected option); Chrome, Firefox and Safari fail too

html/semantics/embedded-content/the-ifra.description: the PDF documents are not rendered (no PDF viewer): the `iframe` navigated to `sandbox.pdf` is empty whether it is sandboxed or not

html/semantics/embedded-content/the-img-.description: the second frame of the lossy `animated.webp` decodes to rgb(1, 128, 1) with libwebp 1.5 (as with the WebP decoder of Meziantou.Framework.Imaging), but the reference `green.png` is rgb(0, 128, 0) and the test has no fuzzy matching

html/semantics/embedded-content/the-vide.description: the frames of the videos are not decoded (the media backend of the tests gives opaque black frames): the reference is an image of the first frame of the video (the test fails in Chromium, Gecko and WebKit too)

html/semantics/forms/customizable-combob.description: the customizable combobox (an `<input list>` with `appearance: base` showing its `<datalist>` as a popover): the focused input and the arrow key do not show the options, where the reference shows them under the input with the focus ring of the active option

html/semantics/forms/the-select-element/.description: the reference list box is `box-sizing: content-box`; the rules of the base appearance of the HTML Standard give a list box `box-sizing: border-box` and `block-size: calc(max(24px, 1lh) * size)`, so its rows overflow its content box by its 2px of borders and it has a vertical scrollbar (Chrome passes: its list box is not `border-box`; Firefox and Safari fail)

the select elements have the `min-block-size: calc-size(auto, max(size, 24px, 1lh))` of the user agent style sheet of the base appearance, so they are 24px tall; the `span` elements of the reference have no minimum size and are 20px tall (fails in every browser)

the filterable select (an `<input filter>` that filters the options of a `<select>`): the arrow key in the input does not make the second option the active option (`:active-option`), whose focus ring the reference paints

html/semantics/grouping-content/the-li-e.description: the test expects the ordinal values of the HTML Standard (the list owner of an `li` without `ol`/`ul`/`menu` ancestor is its parent: 1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 3), which are for the non-CSS user agents: a CSS user agent renders the markers with the `list-item` counter of CSS Lists (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#lists), whose scope (the element that instantiates it, its following siblings and their descendants, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists-3/#nested-counters) continues through the nested `div`, `span` and `blockquote`: 1 to 6

html/semantics/grouping-content/the-ol-e.description: the test expects the ordinal values of the HTML Standard (3, 2, 1), which are for the non-CSS user agents: in a CSS user agent the `reversed` attribute is the presentational hint `counter-reset: reversed(list-item)` (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#lists), whose initial value counts the list items in the scope of the counter (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists-3/#instantiate-counter), including the next sibling `p { display: list-item }` of the list: 4, 3, 2; Firefox fails too

html/semantics/interestfor/interestfor-k.description: interest invokers (`interestfor`): focusing the button does not show interest, and the `:interest-source`, `:interest-target` and `:has-partial-interest` pseudo-classes never match (no purple/green/yellow backgrounds); only Chrome passes

html/semantics/interestfor/interestfor-p.description: interest invokers (`interestfor`): hovering the `<a interestfor>` does not show its `popover=hint` target, so the green box of the popover does not cover the red container; only Chrome passes
interest invokers (the `interestfor` attribute) and their `::interest-button` pseudo-element, which is not generated; the tests also fail in every browser

html/semantics/menu/tentative/*.description: the tentative menu elements (`<menubar>`, `<menulist>`, `<submenu>`, `<menuitem>`): they are unknown elements without default style, and a `<menulist>` is not a popover (`showPopover()` throws `NotSupportedError`); the tests also fail in every browser

mathml/relations/css-styling/first-line-.description: expects `::first-line` and `::first-letter` on a `div` with `display: inline math`, which computes to `inline` on an element that is not a MathML element (https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#new-display-math-value): an inline box has neither (they apply to block containers); Chromium 152 renders the same as the library (the items 1 and 2 are not green)

mathml/relations/css-styling/mozilla-393.description: the italic `Y` of the `mi` (STIX Two Math) has an italic correction of 1.76px, which https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#layout-of-mrow adds to the inline size of the `mstyle` laid out as an mrow (11.47px) but not to the one of the `mi` (9.71px): the `mathbackground` and the CSS background of the `mi` of the test end at x=18, the `mathbackground` of the `mstyle` of the reference at x=19 (22 pixels of the column x=18, by up to 111). The test assumes that the background of an `mi` covers the same area as the one of an `mstyle` around it

mathml/relations/css-styling/table-width.description: the test expects the cell to contain the ink of the italic `f` glyphs (Gecko includes the italic overhang of the glyphs in the inline size of a token element); the 48px italic `f` overflows its `mi`/`mtext` box and the `td` by about 10px on the right, as in Chrome and Safari; only Firefox passes; MathML Core (https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#layout-of-mtext): "The min-content inline size, max-content inline size and inline size of the math content box are equal to the one of the anonymous child" (the advances of the text, not its ink)

permissions-policy/experimental-features.description: the experimental `vertical-scroll` policy-controlled feature: the viewport of the iframe whose document is not allowed to scroll vertically (`allow="vertical-scroll 'none'"`) still has its vertical scrollbar; no browser passes (the difference was not visible before the scrollbars were painted)

quirks/line-height-preserved-segment-bre.description: the test is in quirks mode and its reference (`ref-filled-green-100px-square.xht`) in standards mode: the green square is rendered as expected (the inline box of the preserved segment break gives its 100px line), but the paragraph that starts the body has no top margin in quirks mode (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#flow-content-3: "any element with default margins that is the child of a body [...] element and has no substantial previous siblings is expected to have [...] its margin-block-start property [set] to zero"): the whole page is 8px higher than the reference; fails in every browser

quirks/percentage-height-quirk-min-heigh.description: the percentage height calculation quirk only applies to `height`: a percentage `min-height` of an element whose containing block has an auto height resolves to 0 instead of against the ancestor with a definite height (whatwg/quirks#95)

scroll-animations/animation-trigger/anim.description: animation triggers (`animation-trigger`, `timeline-trigger`, Web Animations 2): the properties are parsed but have no effect, so the animation plays immediately instead of staying at its first keyframe until its trigger is activated (the screenshot shows it a frame after its start, slightly blue instead of green)

animation triggers (`animation-trigger`, `timeline-trigger`, Web Animations 2): the properties are parsed but have no effect, so the animation plays immediately instead of waiting for its trigger (its first keyframe, red and translated, is displayed); only Chrome passes

scroll-animations/css/scroll-timeline-on.description: a scroll progress timeline whose source is a pseudo-element (`scroll-timeline: --foo` on an `::after` scroll container): the named timeline of the pseudo-element is found, but a pseudo-element has no scrolling box for the timeline (the source is its originating element, which is not a scroll container), so the timeline is inactive; only Chrome passes

svg/animations/media-fragment-override-a.description: the temporal media fragments of the SVG images (`#t=npt:3,3.01`): the animations of an SVG image are sampled at the begin of its timeline (only Firefox implements them)

svg/coordinate-systems/viewBox-synthesiz.description: a tentative behavior that only Gecko implements: the test expects the viewBox of an SVG image to be synthesized per axis when its root has a width or a height only (the content is stretched in that axis); the library, as Chromium and WebKit, synthesizes a viewBox only when the root has both a width and a height

svg/interact/use-instance-hover.html.description: the user action pseudo-classes of the element instances of a `use` element: the shadow tree is painted without cloning the referenced element, so `:hover` matches the `use` element under the pointer but not the instance of the `rect` it references

svg/painting/marker-005.svg.description: 21 pixels of the antialiased top and left edges of one clipped marker differ by at most 8 levels: the test clips the content of the marker to its viewport, the reference clips the same content with a `clipPath` element, and the edges of the content that coincide with the edges of the clip do not get the same coverage (Chromium and Gecko fail the test too)

svg/painting/reftests/non-scaling-stroke.description: `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke` on SVG text: the glyphs are stroked with the width in the user space of the text (`Painter.SvgText.cs` ignores the `NonScaling` flag of the stroke style, which only the shapes apply), so the `scale(2)` of the group doubles the stroke of `Hello` (16 px on the screen instead of 8 px)

svg/painting/reftests/text-shadow-03.htm.description: the test expects the shadow of a text that is filled and stroked to be the shadow of the first of the fill and the stroke that is painted (Chromium: the stroke with `paint-order: stroke`); the library paints the shadows of the fill and of the stroke, as `css/css-text-decor/text-shadow/svg-stroke.html` requires (Gecko and WebKit fail this test too)

mathml/relations/css-styling/first-line-.description: the test expects no red, but the `math` element is an atomic inline of the first line of the block: the background of the `::first-line` of the block is painted behind it, as in the browsers (the test fails in Chrome, Firefox and Safari)

mathml/presentation-markup/mrow/legacy-m.description: the squares that the HTML parser moves out of `math` (the `span` child of `annotation` in the test, of `mrow` in the reference) and the ones it keeps in a token element are swapped between the test and the reference, and a line that contains an `mtext` or `annotation-xml` with the 50px inline-block is 56px tall (the strut of the bundled math font, STIX Two Math, has a 6px descent) while a line with the bare inline-block is 54px tall: the second square is 2px higher than in the reference; the test assumes a math font whose strut is not deeper than the one of the default font, only Chrome passes; the trees differ because of the HTML parser (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#parsing-main-inforeign: a `span` start tag in foreign content pops the elements up to a MathML text integration point, an HTML integration point or an HTML element), and the height of a line depends on the strut of the font of its block container (CSS 2 section 10.8.1: "each line box starts with a zero-width inline box with the element's font and line height properties"; MathML Core user agent style sheet: `math { font-family: math; line-height: normal }`)

mathml/presentation-markup/operators/mo-.description: the rendering of the U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS content of an `mo` with the glyph of U+2212 MINUS SIGN (a WebKit behavior: the hyphen of the primary font is painted, 16.8px wide instead of 20.5px); only Safari passes

the test expects the spacing of the MathML 3 operator dictionary for U+223F SINE WAVE (lspace and rspace of 3/18em); this character is not in the operator dictionary of MathML Core, so it gets the default 5/18em (the `mo` is 1.8px further and the row 3.6px wider); Chrome fails too; MathML Core: the category of an operator that is not in the dictionary is Default, whose lspace and rspace are 0.2777777777777778em (https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#dfn-algorithm-for-determining-the-properties-of-an-embellished-operator, https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#operator-dictionary); Firefox and Safari pass with the MathML 3 dictionary

mathml/presentation-markup/scripts/stret.description: the test expects the stretchy operator of the `mover` not to be stretched; with the algorithm for stretching operators along the block axis of MathML Core, the embellished operator is the only child of its row, so it is stretched to its own ink extent, which includes the overscript: the arrow is 50px tall instead of 25px; Chrome and Firefox fail too, only Safari passes; MathML Core (https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#dfn-algorithm-for-stretching-operators-along-the-block-axis): "If LNotToStretch is empty, perform layout with block stretch size constraint (0, 0) for all the items of LToStretch. Calculate the unconstrained target sizes Uascent and Udescent as respectively the maximum ink ascent and maximum ink descent of the margin boxes of in-flow children that have been laid out in the previous step. Lay out or relayout all the elements of LToStretch with block stretch size constraint (Uascent, Udescent)"

the test expects the stretchy operator of the `mover` not to be stretched; with the algorithm for stretching operators along the block axis of MathML Core, the embellished operator is the only child of its row, so it is stretched to its own ink extent, which includes the overscript: the double bar is stretched below the overscript instead of keeping its 25px; Chrome fails too; MathML Core (https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#dfn-algorithm-for-stretching-operators-along-the-block-axis): "If LNotToStretch is empty, perform layout with block stretch size constraint (0, 0) for all the items of LToStretch. Calculate the unconstrained target sizes Uascent and Udescent as respectively the maximum ink ascent and maximum ink descent of the margin boxes of in-flow children that have been laid out in the previous step. the reference `math > mrow > munderover > mo` is an embellished operator, around which the `math` row adds the lspace and rspace of the arrow (5/18em = 6.9px, MathML Core: add-space is true for the `math` element), while the test sets `lspace="0em" rspace="0em"`: the reference is 6.9px to the right of the test; Chrome and Safari fail too, only Firefox passes; MathML Core (https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#layout-of-mrow): "Set add-space to true if the box corresponds to a math element or is not an embellished operator" and "If the child is an embellished operator and add-space is true then increment inline-offset by its lspace property"

css/css-grid/subgrid/independent-formatt.description: the test expects a fieldset with `display: grid` and `grid-template-rows: subgrid` to be a subgrid of its parent grid (Firefox and Safari); the grid container of a fieldset is its anonymous fieldset content box (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#anonymous-fieldset-content-box), whose parent, the principal box of the fieldset, is a block container that establishes a block formatting context: the content box is not a grid item, so `subgrid` behaves as `none` (as in Chrome, which fails this test too)

css/css-grid/grid-lanes/baseline/grid-la.description: expects the baseline content-alignment of the items in the stacking axis (`align-content: baseline | last baseline` on the items of a column grid lanes container, and on the vertical items of a row one): the reference is a grid whose items share the baseline of their contents in a row (a column), but "Baseline alignment is not supported in the stacking axis" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#baseline-alignment; an earlier masonry draft aligned the items placed first in each track); the rows of `last baseline` items match. css/css-page/monolithic-overflow-017-pri.description: the pagination is as expected (the monolithic content overflows the first three pages, a repeated footer at the bottom of each page, `PASS` on the fourth page above the last footer), but the reference expects the hotpink background of the repeated footer (and its text) painted over the black monolithic content that overflows the row of the body of the table: that is the painting order of Blink (each table section paints its backgrounds in its own turn, in tree order), whereas CSS 2 paints all the backgrounds of the table, its row groups included, before the in-flow content of its cells (https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#painting-order, E.2 step 4: "Otherwise, for table: [...] row group backgrounds [...]", then the block-level descendants in tree order), so the black box covers the footer; Firefox fails it too

css/css-page/monolithic-overflow-032-pri.description: the monolithic content that does not fit in an empty page is sliced, and a box with `box-decoration-break: clone` does not repeat its edges at the slices, but Blink and Gecko (as the comment of the test says; Gecko passes, Blink fails) also end the fragment of the box right after the monolithic content (with its block-end edges) and start a new fragment of the box after it in the same page (with its block-start edges): the content after the monolithic content is placed after the end of the monolithic content without these edges (the third and next pages differ). The fragmentation places one fragment of a box per page (FragmentSlicer, keyed by the fragmentainer index): two fragments of the same box in a page is not supported (it needs a fragmentainer that starts inside a page, after the end of the monolithic content, as Blink does by growing the page over it)

css/css-page/body-background-srl-print.h.description: the canvas background of a `sideways-rl` root element stitched across two pages: the first page shows the right half of the gradient (lightgray), as the text of the test says, but the reference shows a white first page (Chrome and Firefox fail the test)

css/css-page/body-background-vrl-print.h.description: the background of the body (propagated to the canvas) is positioned in the root element stitched across the pages (`box-decoration-break: slice`, "as though the element were rendered with no breaks present, and then sliced by the breaks afterward", https://drafts.csswg.org/css-break-3/#valdef-box-decoration-break-slice): in `vertical-rl` the block-start side, which the first page contains, is the right side of the stitched box, the white half of the gradient (`90deg`: lightgray on the left, white on the right), but the reference expects the lightgray half on the first page and the white half on the second one (the layout of the boxes and of the absolutely positioned paragraph is as expected; the `vertical-lr` variant passes); fails in Chrome and Firefox (as the `sideways-*` variants)

css/css-break/float-with-large-margin-bo.description: a float whose border box fits in the rest of the first page but not its block-end margin (1in): the specification does not define what happens to the margins of a float at a break (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/9191, open: "Gecko does B, Blink does D"); as in Blink, the float is pushed to the next page with its margin (the margin of a float is not truncated, see FloatPusher), where the test expects the behavior of Gecko (the float stays on the first page and its margin continues on the second one); fails in Chrome

css/css-break/underflow-from-next-page-p.description: a box after a forced page break with a negative block-start margin (`margin-top: -50vh`): the forced break is at the end of the paragraph before the box, and the box is placed before it in the strip (the margins after a forced break are preserved: the break is at `max(end of the content before, start of the box - its positive margin)`), so it ends on the first page and there is no second page. Blink starts the second page with the box at a negative offset (-50vh), and the reference expects `PASS` at the middle of the first page: the part of the box above the page area of the second page is painted in the first page (the pages show the content stitched across them): both the break after the box and the painting of the content of a page that underflows into the previous page are missing (the page area clips the content of its page); Firefox fails it too. The breaks map the positions of the strip to the pages in order (`FlowMap`): a box after a forced break whose position in the strip is before it cannot be placed in the next page without mapping the content in the order of the content instead of its positions

css/printing/page-overflow-crash-print.h.description: a crash test of Gecko (bug 1697291) turned into a mismatch print reftest that asserts that something is printed; but `* { offset-path: path(M 1 7 H 1 V -1 H -1 L 1 0) }` applies a motion path to each of `html`, `body` and `details` (https://drafts.fxtf.org/motion-1/#offset-path-property): each one is moved so that its anchor (its center, or its top-left corner for `#a` with `offset-anchor: 0px 0px`) is at (1px, 7px) of its containing block and rotated by the direction of the path (`offset-rotate: auto`, -90deg after the zero-length first segment). css/css-break/grid/grid-lanes/row-expans.description: the grid-lanes container with row lanes (`grid-template-rows`) fragmented in its grid axis by the columns: the second row is deferred to the next column by `break-before: column` on its item and expands there (forced break inside its item); the painting differs in 5200 pixels from the reference (the test checks that a row-spanning item laid out in a fragmentainer keeps the size of its rows there when a row it spans is deferred and expands in a later column, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#pagination)

the grid-lanes container with row lanes (`grid-template-rows`) fragmented in its grid axis by the columns: the second row breaks softly (a forced break inside its item and a `break-inside: avoid` item spanning rows 2 / 4) and expands in the next column; the painting differs in 5200 pixels from the reference (the test checks that a row-spanning item laid out in a fragmentainer keeps the size of its rows there when a row it spans breaks softly and expands in a later column, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#pagination)

the grid-lanes container with row lanes (`grid-template-rows`) fragmented in its grid axis by the columns: the growth of the second row (a forced break inside an item, a `break-inside: avoid-column` sibling) causes a soft break and the row expands across three columns; the painting differs in 5200 pixels from the reference (the test checks that a row-spanning item laid out in a fragmentainer keeps the size of its rows there when a row it spans grows in a later column, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#pagination)

css/css-gaps/grid-lanes/column-gap-decor.description: the row rule (stacking-axis gap decoration) before an item that spans several tracks is only painted in the tracks where an item precedes it; the CSSWG resolved (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/14684#issuecomment-6928803010, Nov 16 2026) that when a spanning item is not the first item of at least one of its tracks, there is a gutter above it in all the tracks it spans: the reference, changed upstream for this resolution, adds the rule above the full-width spanner in the first track (240 pixels: the 60px x 4px rule of the track where the spanner is first)

the row rule (stacking-axis gap decoration) before an item that spans several tracks is only painted in the tracks where an item precedes it; the CSSWG resolved (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/14684#issuecomment-6928803010, Nov 16 2026) that when a spanning item is not the first item of at least one of its tracks, there is a gutter above it in all the tracks it spans: the test, changed upstream for this resolution, expects the rule above the spanner in the second track, where it is the first item (240 pixels: the 60px x 4px rule of the track where the spanner is first)

`overlap-join` at the junction before a spanning item where two row rules of different widths cross the column rule (`row-rule-width: 4px, 12px`): the column rule is extended by half of the 4px rule of the first track instead of half of the 12px rule, the widest crossing rule the test expects (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-gaps-1/#inset), so it ends 4px short (32 pixels)

css/css-gaps/grid/grid-gap-decorations-0.description: `overlap-join` at a junction where no row rule paints (`row-rule-style: none`): the column segments are extended by half the row gap plus half the computed `row-rule-width` (`medium`, 3px), so they overlap by 3px at the center of the row gap (36 pixels of the semi-transparent rules); the test and its reference, changed upstream (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-gaps-1/#junction-segment-endpoint), expect the crossing rule width to count only when the crossing rule paints, so the segments meet at the center

css/css-viewport/zoom/iframe-zoom-scroll.description: the display list of the nested document of a zoomed iframe is scaled by the zoom (Painter.Replaced), its viewport scrollbar included: the 15px classic scrollbar of the scrollable iframe at `zoom: 4` is painted 60px wide, where the reference (the root element zoomed in an unzoomed iframe) has a 15px scrollbar (7569 pixels differ, by up to 128)

css/css-viewport/zoom/iframe-zoom-webgl-.description: WebGL (`getContext("webgl")` returns null): the script throws on `gl.clearColor` and the screenshot is never taken

svg/render/reftests/blending-svg-root-co.description: the `mix-blend-mode` of an SVG element inside an outer `svg` element that is a CSS stacking context (`contain: paint`) blends with the content behind the `svg` element: the isolated groups are only the stacking contexts whose child stacking contexts (CSS boxes) blend (`Painter.CollectIsolatedGroups`), the blending SVG descendants of an outer `svg` element do not make it one (https://drafts.fxtf.org/compositing-1/#isolation: an element that has a stacking context is an isolated group); the black rect is painted green (all 40000 pixels differ)

svg/render/reftests/blending-svg-root-po.description: the `mix-blend-mode` of an SVG element inside an outer `svg` element that is a CSS stacking context (`position: sticky`) blends with the content behind the `svg` element: the isolated groups are only the stacking contexts whose child stacking contexts (CSS boxes) blend (`Painter.CollectIsolatedGroups`), the blending SVG descendants of an outer `svg` element do not make it one (https://drafts.fxtf.org/compositing-1/#isolation: an element that has a stacking context is an isolated group); the black rect is painted green (all 40000 pixels differ)

svg/render/reftests/blending-svg-root-fl.description: the `mix-blend-mode` of an SVG element inside an outer `svg` element that is a CSS stacking context (a flex item with `z-index: 0`) blends with the content behind the `svg` element: the isolated groups are only the stacking contexts whose child stacking contexts (CSS boxes) blend (`Painter.CollectIsolatedGroups`), the blending SVG descendants of an outer `svg` element do not make it one (https://drafts.fxtf.org/compositing-1/#isolation: an element that has a stacking context is an isolated group); the black rect is painted green (all 40000 pixels differ)

svg/render/reftests/blending-svg-will-ch.description: `will-change: opacity` on an SVG `g` element does not make it an isolated group (only clip-path, mask, filter, mix-blend-mode and `isolation: isolate` do, https://drafts.fxtf.org/compositing-1/#csscompositingrules_SVG): the `mix-blend-mode: difference` rect inside it blends with the green background behind the `svg` element (all 40000 pixels differ)

css/selectors/crashtests/chrome-bug-5657.description: the instance of the `<image>` element in the use-element shadow tree of the `<use>` element (the clone of the element of `<defs>`) neither fetches its image nor fires `error` (https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/struct.html#UseShadowTree: the instances are rendered as the elements), only the original element of `<defs>` does: `crash(evt.target)` returns early for it (its root is the document), so the test-wait class is never removed. The `evt` parameter of the event handlers of the SVG elements that the handler uses is supported

editing/crashtests/designMode-on-when-te.description: the loop `for (const i = 0; i < 20; i++)` throws a TypeError (assignment to a constant variable) after its first iteration, so the test-wait class is never removed

selection/crashtests/selectall-and-find-.description: `window.find()`: the test-wait class is never removed

editing/crashtests/designMode-document-w.description: `iframe.contentWindow.focus()` does not fire the `focus` event at the window of the iframe, whose listener removes the test-wait class

editing/crashtests/inserthorizontalrule-.description: the `object` element whose `data` is set to the empty string does not fire `error` three times, so the test-wait class is never removed

editing/crashtests/move-focused-editing-.description: `execCommand("insertUnorderedList")` in the editing host fires no `input` event at the list, whose listener removes the test-wait class

service-workers/cache-storage/crashtests.description: the body of a cloned response that is put in the cache is locked (`TypeError: The stream is locked`), so the test-wait class is never removed

dom/nodes/crashtests/multiple-append-mut.description: the page navigates in a loop (the runner stops it after 2,000 documents): each `append(node1, node2)` of `runTest()` removes `#node2` (to put it in the fragment of the converted nodes) and inserts it again, so the iframe it contains loses its navigable (its unload handler moves `node1`) and gets a new one that loads the `srcdoc` again, whose load handler calls `runTest()` again, and the load event of the top-level document, which the crash test waits for, is delayed by each new iframe load. The test completes in Edge (the only browser of wpt.fyi with results)

navigation-api/navigate-event/navigate-f.description: the navigations started from the `formdata` event abort each other (`AbortError`) and no animation frame runs for 10 seconds, so the page never becomes ready
